If the error is not cleared, press the Cutter button.
If it is still not cleared, turn the printer off and on again.
If it is still not cleared, contact support.
entries.note: The LED table names the error; the steps come from the same guide's 'DK Roll errors' and 'Unable to reset an error' rows.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB LED: Cover open error
steps: Open the DK Roll Compartment Cover, then close it.
If the error is not cleared, press the Cutter button.
If it is still not cleared, turn the printer off and on again.
If it is still not cleared, contact support.
entries.note: The LED table names the error; the steps come from the same guide's 'DK Roll errors' and 'Unable to reset an error' rows.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB LED: Transferred data error
steps: Open the DK Roll Compartment Cover, then close it.
If the error is not cleared, press the Cutter button.
If it is still not cleared, turn the printer off and on again.
If it is still not cleared, contact support.
entries.note: The LED table names the error; the steps come from the same guide's 'DK Roll errors' and 'Unable to reset an error' rows.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB LED: Memory full error
steps: Open the DK Roll Compartment Cover, then close it.
If the error is not cleared, press the Cutter button.
If it is still not cleared, turn the printer off and on again.
If it is still not cleared, contact support.
entries.note: The LED table names the error; the steps come from the same guide's 'DK Roll errors' and 'Unable to reset an error' rows.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB LED: Access point connection error
steps: The printer could not connect to the Wi-Fi access point.
Recheck the network name (SSID) and network key and set up Wi-Fi again.
Open the DK Roll Compartment Cover, then close it.
If the error is not cleared, press the Cutter button.
If it is still not cleared, turn the printer off and on again.
If it is still not cleared, contact support.
entries.note: The LED table only names the error; Wi-Fi steps are from the guide's network setup problems table.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB LED: Security error
steps: Recheck and select the correct Wi-Fi security settings (SSID and network key).
Open the DK Roll Compartment Cover, then close it.
If the error is not cleared, press the Cutter button.
If it is still not cleared, turn the printer off and on again.
If it is still not cleared, contact support.
entries.note: The LED table only names the error; steps are from the guide's network setup problems table.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB LED: Mass storage error
steps: Open the DK Roll Compartment Cover, then close it.
If the error is not cleared, press the Cutter button.
If it is still not cleared, turn the printer off and on again.
If it is still not cleared, contact support.
entries.note: The LED table names the error; the steps come from the same guide's 'DK Roll errors' and 'Unable to reset an error' rows.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB LED: USB host errors (excessive voltage, unsupported device, hub connection)
steps: Something plugged into the printer's USB host port is not supported, draws too much power, or is a USB hub.
Unplug that device.
Open the DK Roll Compartment Cover, then close it.
If the error is not cleared, press the Cutter button.
If it is still not cleared, turn the printer off and on again.
If it is still not cleared, contact support.
entries.note: Unplugging the device is implied by the error names; reset steps are from 'Unable to reset an error'.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: Status LED flashes rapidly (system error)
steps: Contact support; this is a system error that needs the manufacturer's service.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: the Status LED is not lit
steps: Check the AC power cord is inserted correctly.
If it is, try another electrical socket.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: the printer does not print, or a printing error is received
steps: Check the cable is connected securely.
Check the DK Roll is installed correctly; if not, remove and reinstall it.
Check there is enough roll remaining.
Check the DK Roll Compartment Cover is closed.
Turn the printer off and on again; if the problem remains, contact support.
If connected through a USB hub, connect it directly to the computer, or try another USB port.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: streaks, poor quality characters, or the label is not fed correctly
steps: Lint or dirt from the roller may be stuck on the print head.
Clean the roller.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: a data transmission error appears on the computer
steps: Check whether the Status LED is flashing orange (cooling mode).
Wait until it stops flashing, then print again.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: labels are jammed in the cutter
steps: Do not try to free the cutter yourself.
Contact support.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: the label is not ejected correctly after printing
steps: Check the Label Output Slot is not blocked.
Remove the DK Roll and reinstall it.
Make sure the DK Roll Compartment Cover is closed correctly.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: cancel the current print job
steps: Make sure the printer is on.
Press the Power button.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: the print quality is poor
steps: Dirt or lint on the roller may be stopping it rolling freely.
Clean the roller.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: "Received data in buffer" and printing does not start
steps: The printer has not received the complete print data.
Turn the printer off, then on again.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: the printer is in cooling mode
steps: The thermal head is too hot; the printer stops and resumes only after it cools.
A hot head may print marks outside the print area.
Give the printer good ventilation and keep it out of enclosed spaces.
It happens more often at high altitude (above 10,000 ft).

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: DK Roll errors
steps: Check you are using the correct DK Roll.
Check there are enough labels remaining.
Check the DK Roll is installed correctly.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: cutter error
steps: Keep the DK Roll Compartment Cover closed and press the Power button.
The cutter moves back to its normal position and the printer turns off by itself.
Once it is off, check the label outlet and remove any jammed labels.
Contact support.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: unable to reset an error
steps: Open the DK Roll Compartment Cover, then close it.
If the error is not cleared, press the Cutter button.
If it is still not cleared, turn the printer off and on again.
If it is still not cleared, contact support.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: printing over USB repeatedly pauses and continues
steps: In the Windows printer's Printing preferences, open the Other tab and select "After one page of data is received" (buffered printing).
Or disconnect the LAN cable until USB printing is finished.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: printed barcodes cannot be read
steps: Print labels so the barcode bars are aligned with the print head as the guide shows.
Do not reduce or enlarge barcodes.
Try another scanner.
Set Print Quality to "Give priority to print quality".

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: barcodes printed from other applications cannot be read
steps: If the barcode was created in landscape orientation, change the Orientation setting in the printer driver's Basic tab to Landscape and try again.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: Wi-Fi security settings (SSID/Network Key) are incorrect
steps: Recheck and select the correct security settings.
The default may use the router maker's name or model number; see the router's instructions.
Ask the router maker, internet provider or network administrator.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: cannot connect or print using Wi-Fi or Bluetooth
steps: When setting up Wi-Fi, move the printer within about 1 metre (3.3 feet) of the mobile device.
Move the printer to an area free of obstructions such as walls or furniture.
Move wireless computers, Bluetooth devices, microwave ovens and cordless phones away from the printer and the router.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: the router uses MAC address filtering
steps: Print the Printer Settings Report to find the printer's MAC address.
Add that address to the router's allowed list.
entries.note: Adding the address to the router is implied; the guide only says how to find it.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: the router does not broadcast its network name (stealth mode)
steps: Type the correct SSID name by hand during installation or in the Printer Setting Tool.
Check the SSID in the router's instructions and set up Wi-Fi again.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: printer is not connected correctly to the network
steps: Check the printer is in the connection mode you want.
Wi-Fi LED flashing every three seconds: the network is connected incorrectly and the Wi-Fi settings must be set up again.
Wireless Direct: search for the printer from the Wi-Fi device.
Wired LAN: check the LAN cable is connected correctly.
Bluetooth: search for the printer from the device you want to connect.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: still cannot complete Wi-Fi or Bluetooth setup
steps: Turn the printer off, then on again.
Try setting up Wi-Fi and Bluetooth again.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: does not reconnect after the Bluetooth link to an iPad or iPhone is lost
steps: Turn the Auto Reconnect function on.
It is set from the Printer Setting Tool on a computer.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: not found on the network (no usable IP address)
steps: Check the IP address and subnet mask of the computer and the printer are correct and on the same network.
Confirm the printer's network settings with the Printer Setting Tool.
Ask the network administrator if unsure.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: will not print after an earlier job failed
steps: If the failed job is still in the computer's print queue, delete it (Cancel All Documents).

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: checked everything and it still does not print over the network
steps: Uninstall the printer driver and the software.
Reinstall them.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: security software or firewall is blocking the printer
steps: Allow access when the security software's alert appears during installation or printing.
Some security software blocks access without showing an alert; see its instructions or ask its maker how to allow access.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: check the firmware version
steps: Turn the printer on.
Load a 62 mm or wider DK Roll.
Press and hold the Cutter button for several seconds to print the report.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: print the printer settings report
steps: Turn the printer on.
Load a 62 mm or wider DK Roll.
Press and hold the Cutter button for two seconds; the report prints.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: load the DK Roll
steps: Make sure the printer is turned off.
Pull the release levers on both sides, hold the printer by the front and lift the DK Roll Compartment Cover firmly.
Place the DK Roll in the Roll Spool Guide with the spool arm firmly in the guide and the stabiliser in the printer's notch.
Thread the roll straight, with its edge against the upright edge of the Label Output Slot, and push the first label through until the end comes out.
Close the DK Roll Compartment Cover.
Turn the printer on and press the Feed button to align the end of the roll.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: hard to insert the first label when loading
steps: Try inserting it from the side, under the sensor.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: do not leave printed labels in the printer
steps: Printed labels left in the printer cause jams.
When the printer is not in use, take the DK Roll out and close the cover to keep dust out.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: remove the protective sheet before first use
steps: Before using the printer, remove the protective sheet from the Label Output Slot.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: turn the printer on and off
steps: On: press the Power button; the Status LED turns green.
Off: press and hold the Power button.
Do not unplug the power cord until the orange Status LED has gone out.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: connect to the shop's Wi-Fi (Infrastructure Mode)
steps: Write down the Wi-Fi network name (SSID) and password.
Turn the printer on; the first time, or after a reset, it enters easy wireless setup mode.
Run Brother's software installer on the computer and follow the on-screen instructions.
Select your SSID if asked.
If the Wi-Fi state is unknown or it must be set up again, reset the printer's Wi-Fi settings first.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: turn the Wi-Fi function on
steps: Press and hold the Wi-Fi button on the printer for one second.
The Wi-Fi LED starts flashing green once every three seconds.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: turn Bluetooth on to pair
steps: Press the Bluetooth button on the printer; the Bluetooth LED lights blue.
Search for the label printer from the computer or device and select it.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: reset settings with the printer buttons
steps: Turn the printer off.
Press and hold the Power and Cutter buttons for about one second; the Status LED lights orange and the Wi-Fi LED flashes green.
Keep holding Power and press Cutter twice to reset network settings, four times to reset transferred data and device settings, or six times to reset everything to factory settings.
Release the Power button; the LEDs flash four times and then stay lit.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: clean the roller
steps: Disconnect the AC power cord.
Cut a DK label and peel off its backing.
Press the sticky side of the label against the roller to lift off the dirt.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: clean the label outlet when adhesive causes jams
steps: Disconnect the AC power cord.
Clean the label outlet with a cloth or cotton swab dipped in alcohol.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: clean the outside
steps: Disconnect the AC power cord.
Wipe with a soft, dry cloth; use a cloth slightly damp with water on stubborn marks.
Do not use paint thinner, benzene, alcohol or other organic solvents on the case.

entries.title: Brother QL-1110NWB: the print head cleans itself
steps: DK Rolls are designed to clean the print head automatically as they pass it during printing and feeding.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: low/medium/high beeps, green LED
steps: Normal: the scanner has powered up.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: medium beep with a green flash
steps: Normal: a barcode was read successfully.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: low/low/low/extra low beeps, red LED
steps: Parity error on a serial (RS-232) connection.
This is normal while the register restarts; otherwise the scanner's serial settings need to match the register: contact support.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: four long low beeps, red LED
steps: A transmission error: the barcode was read but the data was ignored.
This happens when the scanner is not set up correctly or is connected to the wrong kind of host.
The scanner's communication settings must be set to match the register: contact support if you do not have the setup barcodes.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: five long low beeps, red LED
steps: Conversion or format error.
The scanner's conversion settings are wrong, or the barcode contains characters the register connection cannot send.
Contact support to correct the scanner's settings.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: red LED blinks fast when the trigger is pulled
steps: The scanner has been disabled by a command from the register.
The register or point-of-sale software has to enable it again.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: low, high, low, high beeps, red LED (while scanning)
steps: The scanner's batch storage memory is full and it cannot store new barcodes.
Bring the scanner back in range or put it in the cradle so the stored scans can be sent.
entries.note: The table states the meaning only; returning to range or the cradle is how batch mode uploads in the same guide.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: one low beep when placed in the cradle
steps: Normal: the scanner was inserted into the cradle and detected power.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: low, high beeps, green LED
steps: Normal: the Bluetooth connection is established.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: high, low beeps, red LED
steps: The Bluetooth connection was lost.
The scanner tries to reconnect by itself; if it does not, pull the trigger to restart reconnecting, or put it in the cradle.
entries.note: Reconnect behaviour is from the guide's Auto-Reconnect section.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: long low, long high beeps, red LED (not during setup)
steps: Bluetooth page timeout: the cradle or other device is out of range or not powered.
Check the cradle has power and move back into range.
Pull the trigger to restart reconnecting.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: long low, long high, long low, long high beeps
steps: The other device rejected the Bluetooth connection attempt.
The scanner forgets that pairing.
Scan the pairing barcode on the cradle again to make a new connection.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: green LED blinking fast
steps: The scanner is trying to reconnect over Bluetooth.
Barcodes scanned during this time are not sent (a transmission error beep sounds).
Wait for it to reconnect, or move back into range.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: high, low, high, low beeps after scanning the cradle barcode
steps: Normal: the pairing barcode was read.
A low/high beep follows when the connection to the cradle is made.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: four short high beeps and red LED for 4 seconds when the trigger is released
steps: Low battery.
Put the scanner in the cradle to charge.
entries.note: Charging in the cradle is the implied action.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: scanner LED solid red while charging
steps: A charging error occurred.
The battery does not charge above 40°C (104°F); let the scanner cool and keep it within the recommended temperature range.
If it continues, contact support.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: scanner LED while charging
steps: In the cradle, solid green means the scanner is charging.
On the micro USB cable, fast continuous green blinking means charging and solid green means fully charged.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: four short high beeps when trying to scan (USB)
steps: The scanner has not finished starting up on USB.
Wait several seconds and scan again.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: long low/long high beeps, red LED while scanning setup barcodes
steps: Input error: an incorrect barcode or Cancel was scanned, or the setup barcodes were scanned in the wrong order.
The scanner stays in programming mode; scan the correct setup barcode.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: high/low/high/low beeps, green LED after a setup barcode
steps: Normal: the setting was changed successfully.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: high/low beeps, green LED after a setup barcode
steps: The scanner is waiting for a value.
Scan the number barcodes to enter it.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: low/high/low/high beeps while scanning setup barcodes
steps: The scanner is out of storage space for settings.
Scan the Default Parameters barcode from the guide, then set it up again.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: low/high/low beeps
steps: An invalid data-formatting (ADF) rule was detected, or there was an ADF transmit error.
The scanner's formatting rules need to be corrected: contact support.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: power-up beeps (low/medium/high) heard more than once
steps: Normal while the register is restarting or after the USB host type is changed; USB power to the scanner was switched off and on.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: scanner beeps frequently
steps: Check the system has power; if a power supply is needed, reconnect it.
Check the correct interface cable is used.
Check for loose cables and reconnect them.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278 cradle LED: green
steps: Solid green: the cradle has power; while charging it means fully charged.
Green going off, then on: Bluetooth connection established.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278 cradle LED: red blinking
steps: Transmission error between the cradle and the register.
Check the cradle's cables are firmly inserted.
If it continues, reconnect: unplug the cradle's power supply and host cable, wait three seconds, plug the host cable and then the power back in, and pair the scanner again.
entries.note: The LED table states the meaning; the reconnect steps are from the guide's Lost Connection to Host section.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278 cradle LED: amber blinking
steps: Normal: the scanner is charging.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278 cradle LED: amber blinking fast
steps: Charging error.
Reseat the scanner in the cradle and keep it within the recommended temperature range (the battery does not charge above 40°C / 104°F).
If it continues, contact support.
entries.note: The table states the meaning only; the temperature limit is from the charging section.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278 cradle LED: solid red
steps: The cradle has entered its boot loader (maintenance mode).
Contact support.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: the aiming pattern does not appear when pressing the trigger
steps: If the setup needs a power supply, reconnect it.
Check the correct host interface cable is connected and that cables are not loose.
The scanner may be disabled by the register (some IBM and OPOS modes): the point-of-sale software must enable it.
The aiming pattern may have been turned off in the scanner's settings.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: aiming pattern shows but the barcode does not read
steps: The scanner may not be set to read that type of barcode; it has to be programmed for it.
Scan a test barcode of the same type to see whether the label is damaged.
Move the barcode completely inside the aiming pattern and field of view.
Move the scanner closer to or further from the barcode.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: scanner reads the barcode but nothing reaches the register
steps: Reconnect the interface cable if it is loose.
Pair the scanner to the cradle by scanning the PAIR barcode on the cradle.

If the cradle has lost its connection to the register, in this exact order: disconnect the power supply, disconnect the host cable, wait three seconds, reconnect the host cable, reconnect the power supply, and pair again.
The scanner or cradle may be set for the wrong host type; scan the correct host type barcode from the guide.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: the register displays scanned data incorrectly
steps: The scanner is not set up to work with this register: scan the appropriate host type barcode.
On a keyboard wedge setup, set the correct keyboard type and turn off CAPS LOCK.
The right editing options may need programming (for example UPC-E to UPC-A conversion).

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: lost connection to the register (re-establish the cradle connection)
steps: Check all cables are firmly inserted and the power supply, if used, is plugged in.
Disconnect the power supply from the cradle.
Disconnect the host interface cable from the cradle.
Wait three seconds.
Reconnect the host interface cable, then the power supply if one is needed.
Pair again by putting the scanner in the cradle or scanning the pairing barcode.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: pair the scanner with its cradle
steps: Put the scanner in the cradle (pairing on insertion is on by default), or scan the pairing barcode on the cradle.
A high/low/high/low beep means the pairing barcode was read; a low/high beep means the connection is made.
Do not scan items or setup barcodes until pairing completes.
Each cradle's pairing barcode is unique to that cradle.
entries.note: Our sheet says pairing is only by scanning the cradle barcode; Zebra's guide says inserting the scanner in the cradle also pairs it by default.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: pairing a different scanner to a cradle
steps: By default (unlocked mode) a new scanner can be paired at any time by scanning the cradle's PAIR barcode or inserting it in the cradle; this unpairs the previous scanner.
In locked mode a different scanner is rejected until the connection maintenance interval expires, or until you scan Lock Override and then the cradle's PAIR barcode.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: unpair a scanner from its cradle
steps: Scan the Unpairing barcode in the product reference guide.
This frees the cradle for pairing with another scanner.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: scanner went out of range and stopped working
steps: The scanner tries to reconnect by itself; the green LED blinks while it does.
If reconnecting times out it sounds a long low/long high beep and goes into low power mode.
Pull the trigger to start reconnecting again.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: five high beeps every 5 seconds
steps: The scanner is out of range and trying to reconnect, with the out-of-range beep turned on.
Move back into range of the cradle.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: pull the trigger twice to reconnect
steps: Pressing the trigger twice makes the scanner try once to connect to the last device it was connected to.
This does not work with every kind of host connection.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: charge the scanner in the cradle
steps: Insert the scanner straight down into the top of the cradle; it rotates forward so the contacts meet.
The cradle LED starts flashing to show charging has started.
Fully charge the battery before first use.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: charge with the micro USB cable
steps: The micro USB cable is for charging only.
Connect the micro USB end to the scanner and the other end to a PC or a USB wall outlet.
The scanner LED flashes green when charging starts.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: charging takes a long time
steps: Charge time depends on the kind of host and power source the cradle is connected to.
Charging takes longer the more the scanner is scanning while it sits in the cradle; point it so it is not set off by accident.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: battery does not charge or scanner stops scanning in a hot place
steps: The battery does not charge above 40°C (104°F).
In presentation mode above that temperature the battery drains and the scanner stops scanning until it cools and recharges.
Use and charge it between 0°C and 40°C (32°F to 104°F), ideally 5°C to 35°C.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: turn the battery off for storage or shipping, and back on
steps: Scan the Battery Off barcode in the guide, in hand-held mode.
Pull the trigger to turn the battery back on.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: replace the battery
steps: Turn the screw on the battery compartment counterclockwise and remove it.
Take the battery out and wait at least 5 seconds.
Insert the new battery and push down.
Turn the screw clockwise to tighten, without over-tightening.
Charge fully before first use.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: clean the scanner
steps: Use a soft cloth dampened with hydrogen peroxide or mild dish soap, or pre-moistened wipes; never apply liquid directly.
Gently wipe all surfaces, including the trigger area.
Wipe the scan window with a lens tissue and dry it straight away with a soft non-abrasive cloth.
Let it air dry before use.
A dirty window can affect scanning accuracy.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: cleaners that damage the scanner
steps: Do not use acetone, ammonia solutions, benzene, 70% isopropyl alcohol (including wipes), ketones or the other chemicals Zebra lists.
Approved cleaners are hydrogen peroxide and mild dish soap.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: low/medium/high beeps
steps: Normal: the scanner has powered up.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: 4 long low beeps (red LED)
steps: Transmission error: the barcode was read but the data did not reach the register.
This happens when the scanner is not set up correctly or is connected to the wrong kind of host.
The scanner's communication settings must match the register; scan the correct host type barcode or contact support.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: 5 low beeps (red LED)
steps: Conversion or format error.
The scanner's conversion settings are wrong, or the barcode has characters this register connection cannot send.
Contact support to correct the scanner's settings.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: low/low/low/extra low beeps
steps: RS-232 (serial) receive error.
Normal while the register restarts; otherwise the scanner's serial parity must be set to match the register: contact support.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: low/high beeps while scanning setup barcodes (red LED)
steps: Input error: an incorrect barcode, the wrong order, or Cancel was scanned.
Scan the correct setup barcodes again.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: high/low beeps after a setup barcode
steps: The scanner is waiting for a value.
Enter it by scanning the numeric barcodes.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: high/low/high/low beeps after a setup barcode
steps: Normal: the setting was changed successfully.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: low/high/low/high beeps while scanning setup barcodes
steps: The scanner is out of storage space for settings or formatting rules.
Scan the Default Parameters barcode from the guide and set it up again, or contact support.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: low/high/low beeps
steps: An invalid data-formatting (ADF) rule was detected, or there was an ADF transmit error.
The scanner's formatting rules need correcting: contact support.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: power-up beeps (low/medium/high) more than once
steps: Normal: the USB host switched power to the scanner off and on more than once.
It usually happens when the PC or register starts from cold.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: 4 short high beeps when trying to scan
steps: The scanner has not finished starting up on USB.
Wait several seconds and scan again.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: scanner beeps frequently
steps: Check the system power; if the setup needs a power supply, reconnect it.
Check the correct host interface cable is used.
Check for loose cable connections and reconnect them.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208 LED in hand-held use
steps: Green: a barcode was read successfully.
Red: transmission error, conversion or format error, or RS-232 receive error.
Off: no power, or the scanner is on and ready to scan.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208 LED in the stand (hands-free)
steps: Green: on and ready to scan.
Momentarily off: a barcode was read successfully.
Red: transmission, conversion or format error, or RS-232 receive error.
Off: no power, or the scanner is in low power mode.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208 LED: red, alternating between solid and fast blinking
steps: A firmware download is finishing.
Wait until it stops before using the scanner; it then sounds the low/medium/high power-up beeps.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: the aiming pattern does not appear when pressing the trigger
steps: If the setup needs a power supply, reconnect it.
Check the correct host interface cable is connected and no cable is loose.
The scanner may be disabled by the register (some IBM and OPOS modes): the point-of-sale software must enable it.
The aiming pattern may have been turned off in the scanner's settings.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: aiming line shows but the barcode does not read
steps: The scanner may not be programmed to read that barcode type.
Scan a test barcode of the same type to see if the label is damaged.
Move the barcode completely inside the aiming pattern and the field of view.
Move the scanner closer to or further from the barcode.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: scanner reads the barcode but nothing reaches the register
steps: Scan the host type barcode that matches the register.
Reconnect the interface cable if it is loose.
Four long low beeps mean a transmission error: the communication settings must match the register.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: the register displays scanned data incorrectly
steps: Scan the host type barcode that matches the register.
On a keyboard wedge setup, set the correct keyboard type and turn off CAPS LOCK.
The right editing options may need programming (for example UPC-E to UPC-A conversion).

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: connect the interface cable
steps: Push the cable's modular connector into the port on the back of the scanner until it clicks.
Tug the cable gently to check it is secure.
Connect the other end to the register.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: remove the interface cable
steps: Press the cable's connector clip through the access slot in the scanner's base.
Carefully slide the cable out.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: connect external power (only if the register does not power the scanner)
steps: Plug the power supply into the power jack on the interface cable.
Plug the other end into an AC outlet.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: scan in hand-held mode
steps: Place the red aiming line over the barcode.
Press and hold the trigger until the scanner beeps and the LED flashes.
Release the trigger.
Hold small, fine barcodes closer and large ones farther away.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: scan hands-free in the gooseneck stand
steps: Place the front of the scanner into the stand's cup.
Bend the gooseneck to adjust the angle.
Present the barcode; on a good read the scanner beeps and the LED goes off for a moment.

entries.title: Zebra DS2208: clean the scanner
steps: Use a soft cloth dampened with hydrogen peroxide or mild dish soap, or pre-moistened wipes; never apply liquid directly to the scanner.
Gently wipe all surfaces and around the trigger.
Wipe the scan window with a lens tissue and dry it at once with a soft non-abrasive cloth.
Let it air dry before use.
A dirty window can affect scanning accuracy.

entries.title: Zebra DS9308: what the beeps mean
steps: Low/medium/high beeps: power up.
Medium beep: barcode read.
4 long low beeps: transmission error, the data was ignored.
High/low/high/low beeps: setting saved.
High/low beeps: correct setup sequence.
Long low/long high beeps: incorrect setup sequence, or Cancel barcode scanned.

entries.title: Zebra DS9308: what the LED means
steps: Hand-held: off means ready to scan or no power; green flash means barcode read; red means transmission error.
In the stand (presentation): green means ready to scan; off for a moment means barcode read; red means transmission error; off means no power.

entries.title: Zebra DS9308: scanner not working
steps: No power: connect the scanner to a powered host, or connect the power supply.
Scanner disabled: make sure the correct host interface cable is used.

entries.title: Zebra DS9308: reads the barcode but data does not reach the register
steps: Scan the host parameter barcode that matches the register.
Make sure all cable connections are secure.
If a data-formatting (ADF) rule is invalid it must be re-programmed.

entries.title: Zebra DS9308: not reading a barcode
steps: Make sure the scanner is programmed to read that type of barcode.
Check the barcode is not damaged; try a test barcode of the same type.
Move the scanner closer to, or further from, the barcode.

entries.title: Zebra DS9308: scanned data shows incorrectly on the register
steps: Scan the host parameter barcode that matches the register.
Select the correct country and language encoding scheme.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: "Err 1" on the display
steps: This is an initial zero range error: something was on the platter when the scale was turned on.
Empty the platter.
Turn the scale on again.
entries.note: Turning on again with an empty platter follows the manual's power-on instructions.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: "O-L" on the display
steps: Overload: the item is heavier than the scale's maximum.
Remove the item.
Check the scale's capacity in its specifications (SW-2: 5 lb, SW-5: 10 lb, SW-10: 20 lb, SW-20: 50 lb).

entries.title: CAS SW scale: "BAT" on the display
steps: The battery is low.
Fit new batteries; the battery compartment is on the bottom of the scale.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: "LObAt" on the display, then the scale shuts off
steps: The batteries were not replaced after the BAT warning.
Fit new batteries (6 D-size) in the compartment on the bottom of the scale.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: turn the scale on
steps: Make sure the platter is empty.
Press the ON/OFF key.
The display shows all segments and counts up from 0 to 9; press ZERO to stop the count early.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: display is not zero with nothing on the platter
steps: Press the ZERO key.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: what the STABLE, ZERO and NET lamps mean
steps: ZERO lamp: the scale is at zero.
NET lamp: a tare (container weight) has been entered.
STABLE lamp: the weight on the platter is stable.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: weigh with a container (tare)
steps: Place the empty container on the platter.
Press the TARE key.
Put the product in the container; the display shows only the product's weight.
When container and product are removed, the display shows the container's weight with a minus sign.
Press TARE again to clear it; the display returns to 0.000.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: change the unit of weight
steps: Press the UNIT key; the display shows "UnIt" for a second.
Keep pressing UNIT until the unit you want shows (g, kg, lb or oz).

entries.title: CAS SW scale: set or turn off Auto Power Off
steps: Make sure the scale is off.
While pressing the ZERO key, press the ON/OFF key; the display shows AP-10 (or the previous setting).
Press the TARE key until the setting you want shows: AP-00 keeps the scale on continuously; AP-10, AP-20 and AP-30 turn it off after 10, 20 or 30 minutes without use.
Press the ZERO key to save.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: scale switches itself off when not used
steps: Auto Power Off is set; it turns the scale off after 10, 20 or 30 minutes without use to save the battery.
Change the setting to AP-00 to keep it on.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: power and warm-up
steps: Plug the scale into a proper power outlet using the proper adapter; an incorrect adapter could damage the scale.
For best performance plug it in 30 minutes before use to warm up.
Push the plug firmly into the wall outlet and never pull it out by the cord.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: level and place the scale
steps: Place the scale on a firm surface where the temperature is steady.
Adjust the four corners until the built-in leveling indicator shows the scale is even.
Keep it away from heaters, direct sunlight and other electromagnetic devices, which can interfere with accurate reading.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: keep water and humidity away
steps: Do not spill water on the scale or keep it in humid conditions; this can cause electric shock or incorrect readings.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: moving the scale
steps: Hold the bottom of the scale when moving it, not the platter.
Avoid sudden shocks; the internal mechanism could be damaged.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: damaged, defective or reading inaccurately
steps: Do not take the scale apart.
Contact support to arrange repair by a CAS authorized dealer.
Have the scale checked periodically by an authorized dealer for consistent, accurate readings.

entries.title: CAS SW scale: batteries
steps: The scale takes 6 D-size 1.5 V batteries, in the compartment on the bottom.
Battery life is about 500 hours on manganese batteries and 1000 hours on alkaline.
Take the batteries out when the scale will not be used for a long time; leaking batteries are hazardous.

entries.title: Star cash drawer: first checks before troubleshooting
steps: Identify the cash drawer model.
Work out whether it is a USB drawer or a printer-driven drawer (RJ12 cable to the printer).
Check all cables are securely connected and not visibly damaged.
Note the main problem: does not open, opens partially, or is not detected.

entries.title: Star cash drawer (printer-driven) does not open: check the cable
steps: Star drawer cables are labelled to show which end goes to the drawer and which to the printer.
Check the cable supplied with the drawer is securely in the printer's DK port.
Unplug the cable from both the drawer and the printer, look for damage, and plug it back in fully.
Run a cash drawer test from the point-of-sale app.

entries.title: Star cash drawer opens from Star's own test but not from the register
steps: If the drawer opens in a test from a Star application, the printer and drawer are working.
The problem is likely the point-of-sale application or software.
Contact the point-of-sale or software provider.

entries.title: Star cash drawer will not open electronically: use the key
steps: Use the supplied key to unlock the drawer by turning it counter-clockwise.
Pull the drawer open.
If it opens with the key but still not electronically after the cable and test steps, contact support.

entries.title: Star cash drawer: key does not open the drawer (drawer release test)
steps: Lift the cash drawer about 2 to 4 inches (5 to 10 cm) above a flat surface.
Gently release it onto the surface; this may dislodge whatever is stopping the drawer.
Use the key to open the drawer.
If it opens, reconnect the drawer and run a cash drawer test.
If the key still does not open it, contact support.

entries.title: Star cash drawer opens only partially
steps: Check and reseat the drawer cable at both ends and test again.
Unlock the drawer with the key (counter-clockwise) and pull it open.
Look inside with a flashlight and remove any objects or debris blocking the mechanism.
Close the drawer and open it with the key again.
If it still opens only partially, try the drawer release test (lift 2 to 4 inches and gently release), then contact support if it persists.

entries.title: Star CD3 series cash drawer: open with the manual release lever
steps: This applies to CD3 series drawers only.
Carefully tilt the drawer backward to reach the bottom rear.
Find the manual release lever near the back.
Press the lever inward until the drawer opens.
Look inside with a flashlight and remove anything blocking the mechanism.
entries.note: Our device is the CD4; Star's article says this lever is on CD3 series only.

entries.title: Star USB cash drawer does not open: check the DIP switches
steps: Check all DIP switches on the bottom of the drawer are in the OFF position (away from the numbers).
Check the green LED is lit, if the drawer has one.
Run a cash drawer test.

entries.title: Star USB cash drawer does not open: check the cable and USB port
steps: Unplug and replug the USB cable at both the drawer and the register, fully inserted.
Try a different USB port on the same device.
Plug a known-working USB device into the original port to see if the port works; if not, try another port or restart the register.
If a printer is available, connect the drawer to the printer's DK port with its cable and test it there.

entries.title: Star cash drawer: remove or replace the till insert
steps: Disconnect the drawer cable and take out all cash.
Unlock the drawer and pull it fully open.
Grasp the till insert and lift it straight up.
Lower the replacement straight down so it sits flat and fully seated.
Make sure the key and lock are in the opened position and close the drawer.

entries.title: Star cash drawer: remove and refit the metal drawer tray
steps: Unlock the drawer, pull it fully open and lift out the till insert.
Grasp the sides of the metal tray and lift until it reaches the stop on the rails.
Tilt the front down and pull the tray out of the housing.
To refit, hold the tray at a slight downward angle, line its rollers up with the rail rollers, slide it in about two inches, then lower it and push it fully in.
Check it opens and closes smoothly, refit the till insert and close the drawer.

entries.title: Star thermal printers (TSP100 series, mC-Print): faded or light printing
steps: Three common causes: the thermal head needs cleaning, debris is keeping the head off the paper, or the paper quality is poor.
Power off the printer, open the cover and remove the paper roll.
Check the thermal head area and clear any debris.
Wipe the thermal head with a cotton swab or soft cloth moistened with 70% isopropyl alcohol and let it dry; do not clean it while hot.
Put the roll back, close the cover and turn the printer on.
Check the paper: try the roll in another working printer, try a known-good roll, or a brand-new roll from a different box.

entries.title: Star thermal printers: rule out bad paper when print is faded
steps: Test the current roll in another working printer, if there is one.
Try a known-good roll from another printer in the affected one.
Load a brand-new roll from a different box to rule out defective or heat-damaged paper.

entries.title: Star thermal printers: blank receipts
steps: Three common causes: the paper is not thermal paper, the paper is loaded incorrectly, or the thermal head is obstructed or dirty.
Scratch the paper surface with a coin or fingernail; a grey or black mark means it is thermal paper.
Check the roll is loaded the right way for the model.
Turn off the printer, remove the roll, clear loose paper or debris around the thermal head and clean the head.
If it still feeds blank paper, contact support.

entries.title: Star thermal printers: several feet of blank paper feed after each receipt (web-based point of sale)
steps: This is a margins and paper size setting in the web browser, not a printer fault.
The browser's margin and paper size settings need to be configured; contact point-of-sale support.

entries.title: Star SP700: faded or light printing, or missing dots
steps: Power the printer off and open the front cover by the grips at both ends.
Remove the ribbon cartridge by raising the finger grips.
Reinsert it, pressing down until it clicks, with the ribbon sitting behind the print head; if it will not fit, turn the ribbon feed knob clockwise while mounting it.
Turn the ribbon feed knob clockwise to tighten any saggy ribbon and close the cover.
If prints are still faded, replace the cartridge with a new one.

entries.title: Star SP700: ribbon does not advance
steps: Turn the ribbon feed knob clockwise and print a test.
If the ribbon does not advance, replace the cartridge.
If a new cartridge also does not advance, the ribbon spindle may be worn or broken and the printer may need repair: contact support.

entries.title: Star SP700: use Star-branded ribbon cartridges
steps: Non-Star ribbon cartridges may damage the printer's ribbon spindle.
A worn or broken spindle causes light print because the ribbon stops advancing.

entries.title: Star TSP100 series: reset the auto-cutter (cutter error, or cover will not open or close)
steps: A power cut or paper jam can leave the cutter blade out.
First turn the power switch off and back on; this usually resets a locked cutter.
If not, power the printer off and remove the front cover.
Remove any visible jammed paper; do not touch the thermal head.
Turn the knob in front of the cutter until the blade is back in its home position, all the way towards the front of the printer.
Open the rear cover, remove any jammed paper and close it.
Refit the front cover and turn the power on.

entries.title: Star thermal printers (TSP100III, TSP100IV, mC-Print3): print a self-test
steps: Make sure paper is loaded.
Power the printer off.
Press and hold the FEED button.
Power the printer on, releasing FEED only when printing begins.
The printout shows firmware version, interface, MAC address, IP address and Bluetooth name.
entries.note: Star's TSP100IV online manual describes a different method (cover open, press FEED until the Power LED flashes); both are Star's own.

entries.title: Star SP700: print a self-test
steps: Timing is critical.
Power the printer off.
Press and hold the FEED button.
Power the printer on and release FEED immediately on hearing the first beep.

entries.title: Star thermal printers: making print darker (print density)
steps: Clean the thermal head first; that may fix light print without changing density.
Print density can be changed in the Star printer utility or driver.
The point-of-sale software may also control density and override the printer setting; ask the point-of-sale provider.

entries.title: TSP143IV: when to reset the communication settings
steps: When switching from a static IP address to automatic (DHCP).
When a new network or router has been installed, or the printer is being set up on a new Wi-Fi network.
To recover from a forgotten password for the printer's network settings page.
When troubleshooting network or Bluetooth connection problems, or resetting the Bluetooth name or pairing permissions.
Keep the printer on, with paper loaded, and do not power it off during the reset.

entries.title: Star TSP100III, TSP100IV, mC-Print: change the paper width setting with Star Quick Setup Utility
steps: With the printer on and connected to the phone or tablet, open the app and tap Selected Printer.
Select the printer.
Select Device Settings, then Advanced Settings or Memory Switch Settings depending on the model.
Tap Print Width, choose the width, and tap Apply.
Print a self-test to confirm.
The receipt width must also be set in the point-of-sale software.

entries.title: Star Ethernet and Wi-Fi printers: error when no IP address arrives within 20 seconds
steps: By default the printer tries to get an IP address from the network for up to 20 seconds, then reports an error.
A setting called DHCP timeout can be disabled to extend that period; it involves DIP switches or a button sequence and is a technician task.

entries.title: Star SP700: signs that dot alignment needs adjusting
steps: Overlapping or duplicated text.
Every other line indented.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: scanner not working
steps: Check the system power.
Make sure the battery is charged.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: reads barcodes but nothing reaches the register (not paired)
steps: The scanner may not be paired to its cradle.
Scan the pairing barcode on the cradle.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: storing and replacing the battery
steps: For storage, keep batteries at half charge in a dry, cool place, removed from the scanner.
Batteries stored over six months may lose some quality for good.
Replace the battery when run time drops noticeably.
Use only Zebra approved batteries.

entries.title: Zebra DS2278: pair directly with a PC, tablet or phone
steps: Scan the HID Bluetooth Classic barcode in the quick start guide.
Then find and connect the scanner from that device's Bluetooth settings.

entries.title: Clover KDS: what it is and how it mounts
steps: The Clover KDS shows orders to kitchen staff in place of paper tickets.
It supports VESA 100 mm mounts and works with countertop stands, wall mounts and other stands.

entries.title: Clover KDS: orders still reach the kitchen screen when the internet is down (Clover Local Connect)
steps: Clover devices on the same local network (Wi-Fi or wired) can talk to each other directly, so an order taken at the register still shows on the KDS without internet.
This is temporary: internet is still needed to process card payments and save sales data.
All Clover devices must be on the same local network.

entries.title: Clover KDS and registers: network set-up best practices
steps: Use a dedicated router for the Clover devices, connected to the internet provider's modem or gateway.
Use only one router on the Clover network; if Wi-Fi must cover a large area, add an access point, not another router.
Where possible connect Clover devices to the router with wired Ethernet; add Ethernet switches if more ports are needed.
Do not connect anything other than Clover devices to that network.
Do not let customers or guests use that network.

entries.title: Clover: the Kitchen operations report is blank
steps: The report only has data for merchants using a Kitchen Display System.
Merchants who use only a kitchen printer and have not set up a KDS see a blank report.
To read it: log in to the Clover dashboard and select Reports, then Kitchen operations, then a date range.

entries.title: Valor VL300 PIN pad: connect it to a VL100
steps: Power down the VL100.
Connect the PIN pad's micro-USB cable to the USB1 or USB2 port of the VL100.
Power on the VL100.

entries.title: Valor VL300 PIN pad does not turn on when connected to the VL100
steps: The VL100 has to be configured to accept an external PIN pad.
Contact support to turn on External PinPad Support for the terminal in the Valor portal.
Then run a Package Download on the VL100 to apply the change.

entries.title: Valor VL300 PIN pad shows "Keys Not Present"
steps: Connect an Ethernet cable to the Ethernet port on the PIN pad's Y-cable.
Power cycle the PIN pad by pressing and holding its Power button; a key (RKI) download starts.
When it completes, the Ethernet cable can be removed.
If the message stays, contact support.
entries.note: Contacting support if it persists is our addition for escalation; the article ends at the download.

entries.title: Valor VP300 PIN pad: connect it to a VP100
steps: Power down the VP100.
Connect the PIN pad's RJ45 cable to the Pin Pad port of the VP100.
Power on the VP100.
If the PIN pad does not turn on, contact support: the VP100 must be configured for External PinPad Support and then run a Package Download.

entries.title: Blank or black screen, will not power on, or not responding: first checks
steps: Check that the device is plugged into a power source and every cable is firmly connected.
Restart the device, or do a hard reboot by holding the power button down for 10 seconds.
Check that the device is on a strong, stable Wi-Fi network, and restart your router if needed.
Swipe down from the top of the screen to open Settings and install a software update if one is offered.
Look for visible damage and re-seat any detachable part such as the printer or card reader.
If none of this helps, the device may need to be replaced.

entries.title: Check for a software update when a device misbehaves
steps: Swipe down from the top of the screen to open the device Settings menu.
Update the software if the device prompts you to.

entries.title: Check a faulty device for damage and loose parts
steps: Look over the hardware for visible damage.
Take out and put back any detachable part, such as the printer or card reader.
Replace any lost or damaged cables or hubs.

entries.title: Troubleshooting did not fix the device
steps: If the basic checks (power, reboot, network, updates, re-seating parts) do not fix it, the device may need to be replaced.
Contact support to arrange a replacement.

entries.title: How fast the internet needs to be for Clover
steps: Run a speed test at speedtest.net.
Clover recommends at least 8 Mbps download and 384 Kbps upload.

entries.title: Ways a Clover device can connect to the internet
steps: Depending on the device, it can connect by Ethernet, by Wi-Fi, or by the SIM card in the device over a cellular network.

entries.title: Use Ethernet for countertop devices and kitchen printers
steps: Connect countertop devices by Ethernet where you can; it is the most stable connection.
Put a kitchen printer on the same network as the other devices, or it cannot talk to them.
If you use Wi-Fi instead, make sure the kitchen printer is on the same Wi-Fi network as the other devices.

entries.title: Wi-Fi requirements for Clover devices
steps: The router must be password-protected.
It must use at least WPA security; most modern routers default to WPA2.

entries.title: Add or forget a Wi-Fi network after setup
steps: Swipe down from the top of the screen to open the device settings.
Add the new Wi-Fi network or forget the old one there.

entries.title: Wi-Fi keeps dropping: keep taking payments
steps: Turn on the Offline Payments option so you can keep taking payments while not connected.
The payments are processed once the device is back online and logged in.

entries.title: Keep guests and other equipment off the Clover network
steps: Create two networks with different passwords: one for guests and one for the business.
Check your router manual if you are not sure how to create a guest network.

entries.title: Avoid running Clover on a hotspot
steps: Avoid hotspots: they may be slower and cannot support many devices at once.
If you must use one, connect nothing to it except Clover devices.

entries.title: Start a device replacement or return
steps: Replacements and returns both start by contacting support.
Have ready: Merchant ID (MID), device type and serial number, purchase date, and the reason for the return.
Support creates the shipping label for the device going back, and for a replacement also ships the new device.
entries.note: Source says to contact Clover support.

entries.title: What to do on the device before returning or replacing it
steps: Sync all orders so no transactions are left pending.
Uninstall apps that have monthly fees so you are not charged again.
Deactivate the SIM card on a device that uses cellular data.

entries.title: Print the shipping label for a return or replacement
steps: After support has opened the return, log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Business operations, select Devices and printers.
Select the Devices tab and find the device you are returning.
In the manage column, select Print shipping label.

entries.title: Pack a Clover device for return
steps: Put the device in a carton and pack it securely.
Include all cables, power supplies and accessories so you are not charged for missing parts.
Seal the carton and attach the printed shipping label.
Remove or cover any other label.

entries.title: Ship a returned Clover device
steps: Write down the tracking number for each device you send back.
Schedule a UPS pickup or drop the package at a UPS location.
Track it at www.ups.com or by calling 1-800-PICK-UPS.
When it is received, the Devices and printers page on the dashboard updates.

entries.title: Activate a replacement device
steps: Follow the steps on the new device to activate it.
If it asks for an activation code, find it on the Devices and printers page of your dashboard.

entries.title: See all your Clover devices on the dashboard
steps: On the dashboard select Settings > View all settings.
In Business operations, select Devices and printers.
Select the Devices tab.
From there you can track a device order, replace a device, view device details, name a device, activate a device, or factory reset a device.
If your hardware is not listed, check you are logged in with the correct admin account or role.

entries.title: Find the serial number, model and software version on the device
steps: Open the Device Settings app.
Scroll down and select About Device.
Read the serial number, model, software version and Reboot Time.

entries.title: What the 8-digit activation code is
steps: A Clover device needs an 8-digit activation code before first use and after a factory reset.
It is unique to each device.
It is not the 4- or 6-digit passcode you log in with.

entries.title: Find the device activation code
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard: the code is in a banner across the top of the home screen until the device is activated.
Check the business owner's email: the code is emailed when the device first connects to a network, and is also in the shipping notification email.
If the owner opted in, the code is also sent by text message; the partly masked phone number shows on the activation screen.
If you still cannot find it, contact support with your Merchant ID or Tax ID ready.

entries.title: Activation code after a factory reset
steps: After a factory reset the device needs a new activation code.
The new code is emailed to the business owner.

entries.title: Find your Merchant ID (MID) on the dashboard
steps: On the dashboard select Settings > View all settings.
Under About your business, select Business information.
The MID is at the top left of the page.

entries.title: Internet is down: will orders still reach the kitchen display?
steps: With Clover Local Connect, Clover devices on the same local network (Wi-Fi or wired) talk to each other directly.
An order taken at the register still shows on the KDS while the internet is down.
This is temporary: you still need the internet to process card payments and save sales data.

entries.title: Set up the network so the KDS keeps working offline
steps: Use a dedicated router for the Clover devices and connect it to the modem from your internet provider.
Use wired Ethernet to the router where possible; Wi-Fi, wired, or a mix all work.
If you mix Wi-Fi and wired, use only one router for the Clover network.
Need more wired ports: add Ethernet switches.
Need more Wi-Fi coverage: add an access point, not another router.
Connect nothing but Clover devices to that network and keep customers and guests off it.

entries.title: KDS on a mixed Wi-Fi and wired network: one router only
steps: When some Clover devices are on Wi-Fi and some are wired, there must be a single router for the Clover network.

entries.title: Read the Kitchen operations report
steps: On the dashboard select Reports > Kitchen operations.
Pick the date range: today, this week, or this month.
The report shows item volume per hour, average preparation and fulfillment times, items prepared per station, and the slowest items.

entries.title: Kitchen operations report is blank
steps: The report only has data for merchants using the Kitchen Display System.
If you only use a kitchen printer and have not set up a KDS, the report is blank.

entries.title: Replace a lost or damaged power cord, cable or hub
steps: Work out which power cord, USB cable, Ethernet cable or hub is missing or damaged.
Contact support to buy the correct replacement part.
entries.note: Source says to contact customer support to buy the part.

entries.title: Look after cables and hubs
steps: Label each cable so it is easy to reconnect if unplugged.
Check cables and hubs for wear from time to time and replace them before they fail.

entries.title: Bring a connected order (kitchen) printer online
steps: Make sure the Clover device is plugged in, on your network and activated, and that an accessory printer is plugged in and on the same network.
On the Clover device, open the Printers app.
Select Add in the lower right corner.
Tap Order printer; a list of printers on your Clover network appears.
Tap the printer to add. It then shows in the list of online printers.
Repeat for each further printer, one at a time.

entries.title: Choose which items print on an order printer
steps: In the Printers app, find the printer under Order printer and tap it.
Under Labels to auto-print, tick the label, such as Kitchen or Bar.
Items with those labels print to this printer automatically.

entries.title: Order does not print on the kitchen or order printer
steps: Confirm the labels are assigned correctly.
Check that the printer is online.
Make sure the Clover device and the printer are on the same network.

entries.title: Test an order printer after setup
steps: Create a test order with items that carry the printer label (for example Kitchen or Bar).
Send the order. It should print on the chosen order printer.

entries.title: Stop an order printer printing for a while
steps: Go to the printer itself.
Switch off its power.

entries.title: Remove a printer from your Clover device
steps: On the Clover device, open the Printers app.
Tap the printer name.
Tap Delete at the top right.

entries.title: Use the PIN Entry Aid for a customer with a visual disability (Flex Pocket)
steps: When the Enter PIN screen appears, place the PIN Entry Aid on top of the device and wrap its corners around the corners of the device.
If the customer would rather run the card as credit, press Skip and remove the aid.
Hand the device to the customer to enter the PIN.
A tone tells the customer the PIN was submitted and the card can be removed.
Remove the aid and finish the transaction.
Keep the aid stored close to the device.
entries.note: Source names the Flex 3 and Flex Pocket.

entries.title: Use the PIN Entry Aid on a Mini 3
steps: On the Enter PIN screen, press the Accessible PIN entry button.
Place the aid on the device with its top lined up with the top of the screen, so Cancel, Clear and Enter line up with the buttons.
Rotate the screen to the customer to enter the PIN.
A tone tells the customer the PIN was submitted and the card can be removed.
Rotate the Mini back, remove the aid and continue as the screen prompts.
To go on without the aid at any time, press Use screen and remove it.

entries.title: Where to keep the Mini 3 PIN Entry Aid
steps: Keep it close to the Mini 3.
Clover suggests attaching it to the Mini's charging cable with the lanyard provided.

entries.title: Start accessibility mode for a visually impaired cardholder (Flex 4, Flex Pocket)
steps: Set the volume to a comfortable level.
On the Present card screen, turn on the Accessibility mode option.
The device speaks the amount and tells the cardholder to tap or insert the card.
After the card is inserted, the device reads out the accessibility options.
The customer slides a finger down the screen to hear each option and double-taps anywhere to choose the last one announced.

entries.title: Accessibility mode: where the sound comes from
steps: If wired headphones are connected, the audio plays through them.
Otherwise it plays through the device speakers.

entries.title: Accessibility mode: PIN entry with the tactile overlay
steps: If the customer asks, place the tactile overlay precisely over the screen.
The device speaks the amount and describes the PIN pad layout.
The customer enters the PIN using the overlay; each digit is confirmed by a sound.
The customer presses Enter and the payment goes through as normal.

entries.title: Accessibility mode: practice PIN entry
steps: Practice mode lets a customer learn the layout before paying.
The customer must never enter a real PIN in practice mode, because every digit is spoken aloud.
After the practice entry the customer returns to the accessibility options to make the real payment.

entries.title: Phone or tablet needed for the Clover Go app
steps: The Clover Go app needs iOS 11 or higher, or Android 6 or higher.
Download it from the App Store or Google Play.

entries.title: Turn on location sharing before taking payments in the Go app
steps: Turn on location sharing on the phone or tablet.
Clover uses the location of transactions to protect against fraud.

entries.title: Clover Go card reader does not offer tips
steps: In the U.S., card readers are preset to either accept or reject tips.
If yours is not preset to accept tips and you want them, contact support.

entries.title: Log in to the Clover Go app for the first time
steps: Open the Go app and tap Get Started.
Enter your Clover account email and password and tap Log In.
If two-factor authentication is on, enter the code sent to you.
If you have more than one location, pick one and tap Continue.
Enter the passcode for your Clover account. The Home screen appears.

entries.title: Forgot the Clover Go app password
steps: On the login screen tap Forgot Password.
A password reset is sent to your Clover account email.

entries.title: Go app asks for email and password again
steps: After the first login you normally only need your passcode, fingerprint or face recognition.
If you log out, or do not use the app for seven days, you must log in again with email, password and passcode.

entries.title: Find your passcode for the Go app
steps: On the dashboard select Employees > Employee List.
Select your name, then Edit Employee, to see your profile and passcode.

entries.title: Reach Clover's live support from the device
steps: On a Clover device, tap Help on the home screen.
In the Clover Go app, open the menu and tap Help.
Your direct support phone number is printed on your statement.

entries.title: What a tamper alert means
steps: Clover devices have sensors that detect misuse or harm; if tampering is detected the device locks PIN-entry transactions.
In rare cases a drop or a shake can trigger it.
Clover emails you when a tamper is detected.
Contact support.

entries.title: Device tampered, return to manufacturer
steps: This can appear on the Get Help screen during setup.
The message cannot be cleared: the device has to be replaced.
Contact support for a replacement device.

entries.title: Tamper Detected
steps: This screen can appear in the Setup Wizard, or as an error in the Sale, Refund and other apps after activation.
The only way to remove it is to get a new device.
Contact support for a replacement.

entries.title: What still works on a tampered device
steps: PIN-entry payments are disabled.
You can still take transactions that do not need a PIN, and take orders, run reports and sync with other Clover devices.
Replace the device as soon as possible to get full payment function back.

entries.title: Request a replacement for a tampered Station, Mini or Flex from the device
steps: You must be an owner or admin.
Open the Setup app.
Tap Payments, then PIN Entry, then Prompt for PIN.
Tap Save.
Tap 'I need to accept PIN payments, please send me a replacement Clover device that accepts PIN payments'.
Tap OK.
You get an email with the activation code and tracking details when the replacement ships.
Activate the new device, then send the tampered one back in the same box using the return label inside.

entries.title: Cost of replacing a tampered device
steps: If the device is still in warranty the replacement is free of charge.
Shipping and handling fees may apply.

entries.title: Clover Go reader: suspected tampering message in the Go app
steps: On a Go G3 reader a message in the Clover Go app says tampering is suspected, and an email is sent to the account address.
The reader can no longer take payments.
Contact support for a replacement reader.
Meanwhile you can still take payments in the Go app by scanning or keying the card, where available.

entries.title: Clover Go G2 reader lights flash in a random pattern
steps: Random flashing lights on a Go G2 reader mean a tamper was detected.
The reader can no longer take payments and must be replaced.
Contact support for a replacement.

entries.title: Inspect a device for signs of tampering
steps: Look for cutting, disassembly, broken seals or broken ports on the outside.
Look for unusual wires or overlays in the chip slot or near the PIN area.
Check for loose wires, broken connectors, a different number of connections, or cables of a different color.
Notice any change in resistance when inserting or removing a card.
Check whether the device has moved, has scratches around the display seams, or has missing or peeling Clover labels.
If you suspect tampering, contact support.

entries.title: Should I factory reset my Clover device?
steps: Do not factory reset unless support tells you to, or you are cancelling the account or receiving a replacement.
A reset erases all data on the device, including transactions stored while offline.
The old activation code stops working; a new one is emailed and shown when you log in to your Clover account.

entries.title: Factory reset deletes offline transactions
steps: Transactions stored while offline are deleted by a factory reset.
Transactions that were accepted but not yet batched are saved before being removed from the device.

entries.title: Factory reset from the Setup app (only when support directs)
steps: Open the Setup app on the device to reset.
Tap Devices and select the device you are using.
Tap Factory Reset and tick the box confirming that all offline transactions on the device will be deleted.
Afterwards follow the on-screen steps to activate and connect the device.

entries.title: Factory reset from the Settings app (only when support directs)
steps: Open the Settings app, or swipe down from the top right of the screen and select Settings.
Tap Reset, then Factory data reset.
Tap Reset Device to confirm.

entries.title: Factory reset a device from the dashboard (only when support directs)
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings, then Devices and printers, then the Devices tab.
Find the device and select device details.
Select Factory Reset and confirm that all data and unprocessed orders on the device will be lost.

entries.title: Frozen Station Solo or Station Duo: hard reboot
steps: Unplug the display cord from the bottom of the Station.
Wait 10 seconds.
Plug the display cord back in.
Let the device reboot, then log in.
If it does not restart, contact support.

entries.title: Frozen Mini: hard reboot
steps: Unplug the power cord from the Mini hub.
Open the paper door and take out the paper roll.
Hold the green reset button at the back of the paper roll cavity for a full 15 seconds.
Plug the power cord back into the hub. The Clover logo appears.
If it does not restart, contact support.

entries.title: Frozen Flex or Flex Pocket: hard reboot
steps: Take the device off its charging cradle or unplug the power cord.
Hold the power button down for 32 seconds, then release.
Press the power button again until the Clover image appears.
Put it back on the cradle or reconnect the power cord.
Enter your passcode when asked.
If it does not restart, contact support.

entries.title: Frozen Compact: hard reboot
steps: Unplug the display cord from the bottom of the Compact.
Wait 10 seconds.
Plug the cord back in.
Let it reboot, then log in.
If it does not restart, contact support.

entries.title: Device does not restart after a hard reboot
steps: If the device does not restart after the hard reboot steps for its model, contact support.

entries.title: Why the device restarts by itself every day
steps: Clover devices reboot automatically every 24 hours for performance and security.
It takes about 1 to 2 minutes.
All settings and data, including offline payments, are kept.
By default it happens at a random time between 3 am and 5 am local time.

entries.title: Clover Needs to Reboot
steps: This notice appears one minute before the daily reboot, with a 60-second countdown.
Do nothing and it reboots after the countdown.
Tap Cancel to put it off until the next day.
Tap Change Reboot Time to pick another time.
Tap Reboot Now to reboot at once.

entries.title: Change the daily automatic reboot time
steps: Swipe down from the top right corner of the home screen and tap the Settings icon.
Tap About device at the bottom of the list.
Tap Reboot time.
Set the time on the clock and tap Done.

entries.title: Device did not do its daily reboot
steps: If the device was manually rebooted within 6 hours before the reboot time, it skips the automatic reboot that day.
It reboots the next day at the usual time.

entries.title: Connect a Clover device to Wi-Fi from Settings
steps: Open the Settings app.
In Wireless & Networks, tap WiFi.
If WiFi is off, slide the switch to ON; a list of networks appears.
Select your network, or search for it by name.
Enter the network password.
When connected, the network name shows a status of Connected.

entries.title: Wi-Fi signal is weak
steps: Check the network status icons at the top of the screen for connection and signal strength.
If the Wi-Fi signal is low, move the device to a different spot and see whether it improves.

entries.title: Older device on the AT&T 3G network cannot take payments
steps: AT&T shut down its 3G network on February 28, 2022.
A device that only used AT&T 3G must be connected to Wi-Fi (or Ethernet for a 3G Mini), or be replaced with a 4G device.
For a 3G Mini: connect an Ethernet cable to the hub, open Settings and check the network is connected.
entries.note: Applies to older 3G units, not current models.

entries.title: When a simple restart (soft reboot) helps
steps: Restart the device to fix random network dropouts.
Restart it to improve slow performance.
Restart it so settings you just changed take effect.

entries.title: Restart (soft reboot) a Station
steps: Swipe down from the top right corner of the screen.
Tap Reboot, then tap Reboot again when asked.
The Station powers off for a moment and turns back on by itself.

entries.title: Restart (soft reboot) a Mini or Flex
steps: Swipe down from the top right corner of the screen.
Tap Reboot, then tap Reboot again when asked.
The device powers off for a moment and turns back on by itself.

entries.title: Restart (soft reboot) a Compact
steps: Swipe down from the top right corner of the screen.
Tap Reboot, then tap Reboot again when asked.
The Compact powers off for a moment and turns back on by itself.

entries.title: Restart a Kiosk running in Kiosk mode
steps: Press and hold the Clover logo in the lower-left corner of the screen.
Enter the admin passcode.
Select Exit Kiosk Mode.
Press and hold the device power button until the power menu appears.
Tap Reboot, then Reboot again when asked.
If Restart is not offered, select Power off, wait about 10 seconds, then press the power button to turn the Kiosk back on.

entries.title: Restart a customer-facing Kiosk device in a tethered setup
steps: Tap the four corners of the screen to leave customer-facing mode.
Enter the admin passcode on the lock screen.
Tap Reboot, then Reboot again when asked.

entries.title: Cannot get to device settings on a customer-facing Kiosk
steps: In a tethered setup the customer-facing device runs a full-screen app that blocks device settings.
Tap the four corners of the screen and enter the admin passcode to leave customer-facing mode first.

entries.title: Do not pull cables from a Station while it is on
steps: Do not remove cables while the Station is powered on.
Removing the display cable (green sticker) while on can permanently damage the device.
USB devices plugged into the bottom of the printer can be added and removed while it is on.
entries.note: Written about the original Clover Station; the hard-reboot article for Station Solo/Duo does tell you to unplug the display cord. The two Clover articles differ.

entries.title: Station does not recognize a newly plugged-in USB device
steps: USB devices can be plugged into the bottom of the printer while the Station is on.
Reboot the Station so it recognizes the new USB device.

entries.title: Screen is dark: the device may be asleep
steps: Clover devices are meant to stay powered on.
When idle the device goes to sleep; tap the touchscreen to wake it.
It also restarts by itself every 24 hours and may restart after a software update.

entries.title: Turn a Clover device off (general rule)
steps: On most devices, hold the power button for more than 10 seconds until a menu with a shut down option appears.
A device with no power button is powered down by unplugging it for 10 seconds.

entries.title: Turn off a Flex or Flex Pocket
steps: From the home screen, swipe down from the top right. A power button appears.
Press the power button until the screen asks to Shut Down.
Confirm Shut Down.

entries.title: Turn off a Kitchen Display
steps: Find the power button on the bottom of the device.
Press and hold it for a few seconds until the device begins to shut down.

entries.title: Turn off a Kiosk
steps: Find the power button on the back of the Kiosk.
Press and hold it for a few seconds until the device begins to shut down.

entries.title: Turn off a Mini
steps: From the home screen, swipe down from the top right. A green power button appears.
Press the power button until the screen asks to Shut Down.
Confirm Shut down.

entries.title: Turn off a Station Solo
steps: Find the power button on the right side at the back of the main display.
Press and hold it for a few seconds until a menu appears.
Select Shut Down and confirm if asked.
Wait a few moments for it to power down.

entries.title: Turn off a Station Duo (both screens)
steps: Find the power button on the right side at the back of both the main display and the customer-facing display.
Press and hold both power buttons at the same time until menus appear on both screens.
