steps: Plug the USB magstripe reader into a USB port on the computer.
In Virtual Terminal select Take Payment under Transaction Type.
Fill in the sale details.
Select the Card Number field and swipe the card. The number and expiration date fill in.
Select Complete Payment.

entries.title: Verify a card without charging it
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select New Sale.
From the transaction type menu, select Verification.
Enter a name or email address.
Enter the card details.

entries.title: Change Virtual Terminal settings
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Settings > View all settings.
Under Transactions, select Virtual Terminal.
Choose transaction settings (authorization, verification, tip, convenience fee, sales tax) and which customer fields to ask for.
Select Save.

entries.title: Saved card still asks for the CVV
steps: This is expected. The system does not save the CVV; it must be entered for each transaction.

entries.title: Taxes are not applied automatically in Virtual Terminal
steps: Set up taxes and fees first under Settings > View all settings > Taxes & Fees.
The Payments Plus plan does not support automatically applied taxes and fees.

entries.title: Take a bank account (ACH) payment over the phone in Virtual Terminal
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select New Sale, then Take payment under Transaction Type.
Enter the amount and choose checking or savings, business or personal.
Enter the customer's name, account number and routing number.
Enter the customer's identification and full address.
Select Complete Payment.
Read the consent language to the customer and record their responses.
Tick the acknowledgment box and select Submit.

entries.title: Bank account (TeleCheck ACH) payments are not available
steps: TeleCheck ACH has to be activated on the account.
Contact support to activate it.

entries.title: Create and send an invoice
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales activity > Invoices.
Select Create new invoice.
Select or add the customer and a payment due date.
Choose Quick charge and enter the amount, or Itemized invoice and add items.
Select Review and send.
Choose any extra delivery method (text message or share a link), then select Send.

entries.title: Change or cancel an invoice after sending
steps: An unpaid invoice can be cancelled.
A paid invoice cannot be cancelled; issue a refund instead.

entries.title: Cannot send an invoice by text message
steps: Text message delivery is only for US-based businesses on the Essentials plan and above.
The business must be enrolled in a toll-free number.
The customer needs a phone number on file.

entries.title: View, print, share, remind or cancel an invoice
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales activity > Invoices.
Find the invoice by customer, or filter by date and status.
Select Options on the invoice.
Choose Send reminder, View invoice, Cancel invoice, Print invoice or Share invoice link.

entries.title: Invoice status shows 'Failed'
steps: There was a problem with the customer's payment.
Common reasons: insufficient funds, an expired card, risk and fraud concerns, or usage restrictions such as location or merchant type.

entries.title: Invoice status shows 'Expired'
steps: The invoice is past its expiration date.
Invoices expire 180 days after creation.

entries.title: Edit a pending invoice
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales activity > Invoices.
Open the invoice and select Edit (pencil icon).
Change items, taxes, due date or note.
Select Continue.
Tick 'Send an updated invoice' if wanted, then select Save changes.

entries.title: Send an invoice from the Clover Go app
steps: In the Clover Go app, select New Sale on the bottom bar.
Select Create invoice at the top right.
Select Add customer and choose or add the recipient.
Enter the amount and an optional note.
Set a payment due date and select Send invoice.
Check the invoice and select Send invoice, then Done.

entries.title: 'Create invoice' is not available in Clover Go
steps: Create invoice is not available when there are items in the cart.
Either empty the cart, or check out: select Take payment, then More options, then 'Send as an invoice'.

entries.title: Create a recurring payment plan
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales activity > Recurring Payments.
Select Create New Payment Plan.
Enter the plan name, default subtotal and frequency.
Tick 'Activate plan' to enable billing.
Save.

entries.title: Put a customer on a recurring payment plan
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select New Sale.
Under Transaction type, select Recurring payment.
Select the payment plan.
Add or find the customer and enter their card (with their permission to keep it on file).
Set the start date and optional end date.
Select Create Recurring Payment.

entries.title: Pause a recurring payment plan
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Sales Activity > Recurring Payments.
Find the plan and select Options > Pause.
Confirm.
Billing stops for all customers on the plan until it is reactivated.

entries.title: Cannot delete a recurring payment plan
steps: Only plans with no active subscriptions can be deleted.
Deleting a plan removes all plan information; customer invoices stay under Invoices.

entries.title: Before taking payments in the Clover Go app
steps: The app needs iOS 11 or higher, or Android 6 or higher.
Turn on location sharing.
Check tip preferences and signature options in the dashboard.

entries.title: Clover Go card reader does not offer tips
steps: Card readers are preset to either accept or reject tips.
If the reader is not preset to accept tips, contact support.

entries.title: Log in to the Clover Go app
steps: Open the app and tap Get Started.
Enter the Clover account email and password and tap Log In.
If two-factor authentication is on, enter the code sent to the device.
If there are several locations, tap one and tap Continue.
Enter the passcode for the Clover account.

entries.title: Find your passcode
steps: Log in to the Clover dashboard.
Select Employees > Employee List.
Select your name, then Edit Employee. The profile shows the passcode.

entries.title: Forgot the password in the Clover Go app
steps: On the login screen, tap Forgot Password.
A password reset is sent to the Clover account email.

entries.title: Clover Go asks for email and password again
steps: After the first login, only the passcode (or fingerprint or face) is normally needed.
After logging out, or after 7 days without using the app, a full login with email, password and passcode is required again.
The app may also ask to pick from a grid of images.

entries.title: Switch location in the Clover Go app
steps: Go G2 on a phone: on the Home screen, tap the current location at the top, then tap the location you want.
Go G1: tap Menu at the top left, tap Switch Location, choose the location, then choose whether it is the primary location or just for this session.

entries.title: Switch users in the Clover Go app
steps: Go G2: from the More menu tap Settings, tap Log Out and confirm, then the other user logs in with their email, password and passcode.
Go G1: tap Menu, tap Log Out, tap Switch User, pick the user and enter their passcode.

entries.title: Clover Go does not recognize the email and password
steps: This may be because there are multiple Clover accounts.
If you have logged in to this account before, tap Returning User and select your name.
If you are new on this account, enter your dashboard login email and password.
If the password is not accepted, tap Access your Account and enter the account email to get a reset email.

entries.title: Clover Go does not recognize the passcode
steps: If you have logged in before, tap Switch User and select your name from the list.
If you do not remember the passcode, have the manager reset it from the dashboard.

entries.title: Clover Go will not log in: usual causes
steps: Login problems on the Go app are typically about the email, password or passcode tied to the Clover account.

entries.title: What Tap to Pay on iPhone needs
steps: The account owner must enable it.
Surcharging must not be enabled on the account.
iPhone XS or later with iOS 16 or higher.
A device passcode set on the iPhone.

entries.title: Tap to Pay on iPhone is not available
steps: Tap to Pay on iPhone does not work on accounts with surcharging enabled; if surcharging is turned on later, it becomes unavailable.
The owner must have accepted Apple's terms; until then the button does not appear for employees.
The owner can enable it under More > Settings > Tap to Pay on iPhone.

entries.title: Take a contactless payment with Tap to Pay on iPhone
steps: Open the Clover Go app and build the order.
Select Tap to Pay on iPhone.
Turn the iPhone toward the customer.
The customer holds their card flat at the top of the iPhone over the contactless symbol for a few seconds, or taps their phone or watch there.
When the check mark appears the transaction is complete.

entries.title: Use the PIN Entry Aid on a Flex
steps: At the Enter PIN screen, place the PIN Entry Aid on top of the Flex and wrap its corners around the corners of the device.
If the customer prefers credit, press Skip and remove the aid.
Give the Flex to the customer to enter their PIN.
A tone tells them the PIN was submitted and the card can be removed.
Remove the aid and complete the transaction.

entries.title: Use the PIN Entry Aid on a Mini 3
steps: At the Enter PIN screen, press the Accessible PIN entry button.
Place the PIN Entry Aid on the device, top edge lined up with the top of the screen.
Rotate the screen toward the customer to enter their PIN.
A tone tells them the PIN was submitted.
Rotate the Mini back, remove the aid and continue.
To go without the aid at any time, press 'Use screen'.

entries.title: Accessibility mode for PIN entry on a Flex
steps: On the Present card screen, activate the Accessibility mode option.
The device speaks the amount and asks the cardholder to tap or insert the card.
After the card is inserted the customer slides a finger down the screen to hear each option and double-taps to choose it.
Options: enter PIN on screen with speech, Chip & PIN with tactile overlay, or practice mode.
Audio plays through wired headphones if connected, otherwise the speaker.

entries.title: Accessibility mode is missing on an older Flex
steps: Accessibility mode is on Flex 3, Flex 4 and Flex Pocket.
It is not available on Flex 1 or Flex 2.

entries.title: Practice mode speaks the digits aloud
steps: In practice mode every digit entered is spoken aloud.
Customers must never use their real PIN in practice mode.

entries.title: Find a table or order on a Flex (Clover Dining)
steps: Open Clover Dining on the Flex.
Select the search icon at the top right.
Search by table name, order ID, order number, order note, customer name or last 4 digits of the card.
Select the table or order, or start a new order.

entries.title: 05: NO EXISTING HOST (iPOSpays gateway response)

entries.title: R01: Insufficient Funds (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: The available and/or cash reserve balance is not sufficient to cover the dollar value of the debit entry.
What to Do: You can try the transaction again (you will need to re-enter it as a new transaction) up to two times within 30 days of the original authorization date.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R02: Account Closed (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: A previously active account has been closed by action of the customer or the RDFI.
What to Do: Contact your customer for a different bank account, or for another form of payment.
If you have not yet shipped the goods or provided the services covered by the payment, you may want to wait to do so until you have confirmation of a settled payment.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R03: No Account/Unable to Locate Account (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: The account number structure is valid and it passes the check digit validation, but the account number does not correspond to the individual identified in the entry, or the account number designated is not an open account.
What to Do: Contact your customer and confirm the Routing Number, Bank Account Number and the exact name on the bank account. (You can request a copy of a voided check so that you can verify.).
If this information does not exactly match what you initially entered, make changes and submit a NEW payment.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R04: Invalid Account Number (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: The account number structure is not valid. The entry may fail the check digit validation or may contain an incorrect number of digits.
What to Do: Obtain the correct bank account number. (You can request a copy of a voided check so that you can verify.).
Submit a NEW payment using the corrected bank account number.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R05: Unauthorized Consumer Debit using Corporate SEC Code Entry (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: Account number structure not valid: entry may fail check digit validation or may contain incorrect number of digits.

* You cannot re-submit this transaction. Any additional transactions you attempt to process against this account will also be returned unless your customer specifically instructs his bank to accept them.
What to Do: Contact your customer and resolve any issues that caused the transaction to be disputed.
You can ask the customer for a different form of payment, or ask to debit a different bank account.
If you need to debit the same bank account, instruct your customer to call the bank and remove the block on transactions.

Unfortunately, there is no dispute resolution available to you within the ACH Network. If your customer continues to claim the transaction was not authorized, but you have proof that it was properly authorized, you will need to sue your customer in Small Claims Court to collect. If this action is taken, please contact Vericheck.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R06: Returned per ODFI's Request (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: The ODFI has requested that the RDFI return the ACH entry. If the RDFI agrees to return the entry, the ODFI must indemnify the RDFI according to Article Five (Return, Adjustment, Correction, and Acknowledgment of Entries and Entry Information) of these Rules.

The ODFI may request a return from the RDFI for any reason. The RDFI's compliance with the request remains optional at the RDFI's discretion. The RDFI must advise the ODFI of its decision within 10 banking days of receipt of the ODFI's request.
What to Do: Please contact Vericheck.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R07: Authorization Revoked by Customer (adjustment entries) (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: Authorization Revoked by Customer – Consumer, who previously authorized ACH payment, has revoked authorization from Originator (must be returned no later than 60 days from settlement date and customer must sign affidavit).

What to Do: Immediately suspend any recurring payment schedules entered for this bank account. This will prevent additional transactions from being returned while you address the issue with your customer. Then contact your customer and resolve any issues that caused the transaction to be disputed or the schedule to be cancelled.
You can ask the customer for a different form of payment, or ask to debit a different bank account.
If you need to debit the same bank account, instruct your customer to call the bank and remove the block on transactions.

Unfortunately, there is no dispute resolution available to you within the ACH Network. If your customer continues to claim the transaction was not authorized, but you have proof that it was properly authorized, you will need to sue your customer in Small Claims Court to collect. If this action is taken, please contact Vericheck.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R08: Payment Stopped or Stop Payment on Item (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: The Receiver of a recurring debit transaction has the right to stop payment on any specific ACH debit. The RDFI should verify the Receiver's intent when a request for stop payment is made to ensure this is not intended to be a revocation of authorization.

A stop payment order shall remain in effect until the earliest of the following occurs: a lapse of six months from the date of the stop payment order, payment of the debit entry has been stopped, or the Receiver withdraws the stop payment order.

The RDFI determines that a stop payment order has been placed on the item to which the PPD debit entry constituting notice of presentment or the PPD Accounts Receivable Truncated Check Debit Entry relates.
What to Do: Contact your customer and resolve any issues that caused the transaction to be stopped.
You can re-enter the returned transaction again with proper authorization from your customer. You can also ask your customer for a different form of payment.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R09: Uncollected Funds (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: Sufficient book or ledger balance exists to satisfy the dollar value of the transaction, but the dollar value of transactions in the process of collection (i.e., uncollected checks) brings the available and/or cash reserve balance below the dollar value of the debit entry.
What to Do: You can try the transaction again (you will need to re-enter it as a new transaction) up to two times within 30 days of the original authorization date.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R10: Customer Advises Not Authorized; Item Is Ineligible, Notice Not Provided, Signatures Not Genuine, or Item Altered (adjustment entries) (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: For entries to Consumer Accounts that are not PPD debit entries constituting notice of presentment or PPD Accounts Receivable Truncated Check Debit Entries in accordance with Article Two, subsection 2.1.4(2), the RDFI has been notified by its customer, the Receiver, that the Originator of a given transaction has not been authorized to debit his account.

What to Do: The Receiver may request immediate credit from the RDFI for an unauthorized debit. The request must be made in writing within fifteen (15) days after the RDFI sends or makes available to the Receiver information pertaining to that debit entry.

Immediately suspend any recurring payment schedules entered for this bank account. This will prevent additional transactions from being returned while you address the issue with your customer. Then contact your customer and resolve any issues that caused the transaction to be disputed or the schedule to be cancelled.
You can ask the customer for a different form of payment, or ask to debit a different bank account.
If you need to debit the same bank account, instruct your customer to call the bank and remove the block on transactions.

Unfortunately, there is no dispute resolution available to you within the ACH Network. If your customer continues to claim the transaction was not authorized, but you have proof that it was properly authorized, you will need to sue your customer in Small Claims Court to collect. If this action is taken, please contact Vericheck.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R11: Customer Advises Entry Not Within the Authorization Terms (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: Used by the RDFI to return an entry for which the Originator and Receiver have a relationship, and an authorization to debit exists, but there is an error or defect in the payment such that the entry does not conform to the terms of the authorization (i.e., "an incorrect amount," "payment was debited earlier than authorized"). For ARC, BOC or POP errors with the original source document and errors may exist (i.e., "document is ineligible", "notice was not provided to Receiver", "amount was not accurate per the source document").

What to Do: The originator can correct the underlying error, e.g. correct the amount, the date, and resubmit the corrected entry as a new entry. No new authorization is needed from the customer. The new corrected entry must be submitted and originated within 60 days of the Settlement Date of the R11 Return Entry.
If a correction and new entry submission is not possible, the resolution would be similar to receiving a return with the R10 code. See "What to do" for R10 code.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R12: Branch Sold to Another DFI (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: A financial institution may continue to receive entries destined for an account at a branch that has been sold to another financial institution. Because the RDFI no longer maintains the account and is unable to post the entry, it should return the entry to the ODFI.
What to Do: Obtain new Routing Number and Bank Account Number information, then enter a NEW transaction using the updated account numbers.
If the transaction was part of a recurring payment schedule, be sure to update the schedule to use the new bank account.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R13: RDFI not qualified to participate (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: Financial institution is not qualified to participate in ACH or the routing number is incorrect.
What to Do: Double-check that you entered the Routing Number correctly, and contact your customer to confirm it if necessary. Then submit a NEW payment using the correct routing number.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R14: Representative Payee Deceased or Unable to Continue in that Capacity (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: The representative payee is a person or institution authorized to accept entries on behalf of one or more other persons, such as legally incapacitated adults or minor children. The representative payee is either deceased or unable to continue in that capacity. The beneficiary is not deceased.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R15: Beneficiary or Account Holder (Other Than a Representative Payee) Deceased (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: (1) The beneficiary is the person entitled to the benefits and is deceased. The beneficiary may or may not be the account holder; or (2) the account holder (acting in a non-representative payee capacity) is an owner of the account and is deceased.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R16: Account Frozen (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: The funds in the account are unavailable due to specific action taken by the RDFI or by legal action.
What to Do: Obtain a different form of payment. You will not be able to process transactions using this bank account until it is un-frozen.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R17: File Record Edit Criteria (Specify) (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: Some fields that are not edited by the ACH Operator are edited by the RDFI. If the entry cannot be processed by the RDFI, the field(s) causing the processing error must be identified in the addenda record information field of the return. The code also allows, but does not require, an RDFI to return any transaction believed to be questionable or potentially fraudulent.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R20: Non-Transaction Account (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: The ACH entry destined for a non-transaction account. This would include either an account against which transactions are prohibited or limited.
What to Do: Contact your customer to obtain authorization to charge a different bank account.
Ask for a different form of payment.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R21: Invalid Company Identification (Vericheck ACH return code)

entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R22: Invalid Individual ID Number (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: In CIE and MTE entries, the Individual ID Number is used by the Receiver to identify the account. The Receiver has indicated to the RDFI that the number with which the Originator was identified is not correct.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R23: Credit Entry Refused by Receiver (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: The Receiver may return a credit entry because one of the following conditions exists: (1) a minimum amount required by the Receiver has not been remitted; (2) the exact amount required has not been remitted; (3) the account is subject to litigation and the Receiver will not accept the transaction; (4) acceptance of the transaction results in an overpayment; (5) the Originator is not known by the Receiver; or (6) the Receiver has not authorized this credit entry to this account.

What to Do: Contact your customer to work out the problem, or ask them to work the problem out with their bank. Have your customer confirm that the refund will be accepted, then attempt to refund the transaction again.
Alternately, you can send your customer a paper check for the refund amount.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R24: Duplicate Entry (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: The RDFI has received what appears to be a duplicate entry; i.e., the trace number, date, dollar amount and/or other data matches another transaction. This code should be used with extreme care. The RDFI should be aware that if a file has been duplicated, the Originator may have already generated a reversal transaction to handle the situation.
What to Do: Contact Vericheck.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R29: Corporate Customer Advises Not Authorized (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: The RDFI has been notified by the Receiver (non-consumer) that the Originator of a given transaction has not been authorized to debit the Receiver's account.

What to Do: Immediately suspend any recurring payment schedules entered for this bank account. This will prevent additional transactions from being returned while you address the issue with your customer. Then contact your customer and resolve any issues that caused the transaction to be disputed or the schedule to be cancelled.
You can ask the customer for a different form of payment, or ask to debit a different bank account.
If you need to debit the same bank account, instruct your customer to call the bank and remove the block on transactions.

Unfortunately, there is no dispute resolution available to you within the ACH Network. If your customer continues to claim the transaction was not authorized, but you have proof that it was properly authorized, you will need to sue your customer in Small Claims Court to collect. If this action is taken, please contact Vericheck.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: R31: Permissible Return Entry (CCD and CTX only) (Vericheck ACH return code)
steps: The RDFI has been notified by the ODFI that the ODFI agrees to accept a CCD or CTX return entry in accordance with Article Seven, section 7.3 (ODFI Agrees to Accept CCD or CTX Return).

What to Do: In some cases, a business bank account holder, or the bank itself, may request a return after that 2-day window has closed. If the ODFI (your bank, or your ACH Processor) agrees to accept a late return, it is processed using the R31 return code.
You can ask for a different form of payment, or ask to debit a different bank account.
entries.note: ACH (bank account) payments through Vericheck on iPOSpays

entries.title: Active route not found (SPIn message between the register and the terminal)
steps: A terminal does not have an active SPIn Connection. The Connection is created, but is disabled.
On the Terminal Details page check that SPIn Proxy is activated for this terminal.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: shown when a POS or register drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: Not pars request (SPIn message between the register and the terminal)
steps: There is an error in the request message format.
Check a request format.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: shown when a POS or register drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: Route not found (SPIn message between the register and the terminal)
steps: A terminal does not have SPIn Connection. The Connection is not created.
On the Terminal Details page create a new SPIn Proxy connection.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: shown when a POS or register drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: Terminal not connected to SPIn proxy server (SPIn message between the register and the terminal)
steps: A terminal is not connected to the internet or it is inaccessible due to network settings.
The terminal might be just disconnected due to reconnecting to the network, a terminal restart, being in sleep mode, or being in SPIn bypass mode.
Check a terminal whether it works or not and be sure that terminal is on the SPIn mode screen and online.
Send a status request to get actual connection status to continue to work with a terminal. see Check Terminal Connection Status.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: shown when a POS or register drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: The operation has timed out (SPIn message between the register and the terminal)
steps: A request was sent to a terminal, but the terminal did not provide a response at a proper time. Probably the terminal lost a connection, was switched off, a discharged battery, some bug on a terminal, a terminal not in the IDLE screen and busy by some process e.g. a terminal menu is open and a transaction not in focus.

Possible that the terminal will respond to this transaction after a timeout event, a transaction will be performed and approved on a host side and added to a settlement report. But SPIn Proxy cannot guarantee a delivery on this POS request and a timeout is the best response in this case.
Default timeout 120 seconds.
Check a terminal whether it works or not and be sure that terminal is on the SPIn mode screen and online.
Do Status request to check transaction Status.
Repeat the transaction with the same parameters if the transaction was already performed you will get an error “Duplicated ReferenceID”.
Continue to perform transactions.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: shown when a POS or register drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: This terminal handles a different query (SPIn message between the register and the terminal)
steps: A terminal operates another request.
Wait when the previous request is completed and repeat a new request to a terminal.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: shown when a POS or register drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: Terminal in use (SPIn message between the register and the terminal)
steps: Register/Server/Host will get this error if it attempts to send a second request before the full time out period of previous request.
Wait for transaction timing out before attempting another transaction.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: shown when a POS or register drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: Invalid Reference ID (SPIn message between the register and the terminal)
steps: Reference Id value sent from Register/POS/Server will have to be unique per transaction within the batch.
Change the reference id value and retry the transaction.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: shown when a POS or register drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: Reconnected (SPIn message between the register and the terminal)
steps: Terminal was reconnected after receiving the request and before providing the response.
Do Status request to check transaction Status.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: shown when a POS or register drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: Service busy (SPIn message between the register and the terminal)
steps: If the terminal is not ready to receive a transaction for any reason (usually because it is not on the idle screen to receive the request, is busy processing another operation, or has not yet completed a previous transaction).
Try once the existing transaction is completed.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: shown when a POS or register drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1010: Missing Reference ID (SPIn status code)
steps: The reference ID is missing in a request that requires it.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1011: Duplicate Reference ID (SPIn status code)
steps: A transaction with a requested reference ID already exists in the batch.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1012: Cancelled (SPIn status code)
steps: User cancelled the transaction, or it was interrupted for an unknown reason.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1014: Communication Error (SPIn status code)
steps: Communication error with a third-party host occurred.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1015: Declined (SPIn status code)
steps: Load Key or Delete Key request failed.
Settlement requested with no payment applications installed.
A transaction is declined offline or by the host.
A settlement request is declined by the host.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1016: Payment Type Mismatch (SPIn status code)
steps: Payment type of the transaction is not applicable for the card.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1017: Incorrect Merchant ID (SPIn status code)
steps: Invalid merchant ID specified in request.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1018: PINpad Communication Error (SPIn status code)
steps: A communication error with the PINpad device occurred.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1019: No Debit Keys Loaded (SPIn status code)
steps: An encrypted PIN was requested by the transaction, but the terminal has no keys loaded.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1020: No Open Batch (SPIn status code)
steps: No application has an open batch during a settlement request.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1021: Pending SnF Transaction (SPIn status code)
steps: Settlement has been requested, but the terminal is in SnF mode and has pending transactions to upload.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1022: Untipped Transactions Remain (SPIn status code)
steps: Settlement has been requested, but the terminal is in restaurant mode and has untipped transactions.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 1023: Open Tab (SPIn status code)
steps: Settlement has been requested, but the terminal has an open tab.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2001: Terminal not connected to SPIn Proxy server (SPIn status code)
steps: Need to check that the terminal has a connection to the Internet and to SPIn proxy, and shows that it is ready for transaction.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2002: Active AuthKey not found (SPIn status code)
steps: AuthKey in request is wrong or does not exist. Usually this means a misprint in AuthKey.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2003: Register not found (SPIn status code)
steps: TPN wrong or does not exist.
Possible that the request goes to the wrong server (test instead of prod, or vice-versa).
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2004: Route not found (SPIn status code)
steps: TPN does not have configuration for SPIn proxy.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2005: Active route not found (SPIn status code)
steps: Connection was blocked on the server side.
Terminal is not active.
Two or more devices used the same TPN.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2006: Not pars request (SPIn status code)
steps: Invalid request; it may happen if there's extra space in some values.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2007: The operation has timed out (SPIn status code)
steps: Terminal did not provide a response during the timeout time. Default timeout is 120 seconds. Settlement default timeout is 420 seconds.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2008: Terminal in use (SPIn status code)
steps: Terminal is operating on a previous request; in this case the API returns DelayBeforeNextRequest in GeneralResponse as a recommendation of the time until the timeout will happen.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2009: Transaction not found (SPIn status code)
steps: The source lists this status only as: Transaction not found. It gives no further description.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2010: Communication error (SPIn status code)
steps: The source lists this status only as: Communication error. It gives no further description.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2011: Terminal is not available (SPIn status code)
steps: The source lists this status only as: Terminal is not available. It gives no further description.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2101: Callback Url was not specified (SPIn status code)
steps: The source lists this status only as: Callback Url was not specified. It gives no further description.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2102: Invalid XML document (SPIn status code)
steps: The source lists this status only as: Invalid XML document. It gives no further description.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: 2110: Internal exception (SPIn status code)
steps: The source lists this status only as: Internal exception. It gives no further description.
entries.note: SPIn semi-integration: returned to the POS or register that drives a Dejavoo terminal

entries.title: Set up the DejaPayPro register: power, paper, switch on
steps: Take the register out of its packaging.
Plug the power supply into the port marked DC IN and the other end into a power outlet. The guide recommends a surge protector.
Press the button to the left of the paper cover to open it.
Pull the receipt paper through and shut the paper cover over it.
Press the green lit power button on the right-hand side to turn the unit on.
entries.note: The guide calls the unit the CHD register. From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Register is beeping
steps: The guide says the unit beeps when the paper has not been pulled through the paper cover.
Open the paper cover with the button to the left of it.
Pull the receipt paper through and shut the cover over it.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Add items to a customer's cart in DejaPayPro
steps: Tap the department the item is in.
Tap the item to add it to the cart. The line appears on the right.
To change a quantity, highlight the item and tap +1 or -1.
To type a quantity, tap MANUAL, enter the new quantity and tap ENTER.
To add a note to an item, highlight it, tap COMMENT, type the comment and press SAVE.
Continue until all items are in the cart.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Apply a discount to the cart in DejaPayPro
steps: Tap the DISCOUNT button.
Tap the discount amount you want for the cart.
Tap DOUBLE DISCOUNT to double it, or NORMAL for a normal discount.
The discount now shows in the cart Subtotal and Total Due.
Discount and Double Discount options must be pre-set before you can use them.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Take a cash payment in DejaPayPro
steps: When the cart is complete, tap ENTER.
Tap CASH.
Enter the cash amount received from the customer and tap ENTER.
Tap CLOSE to finish. It also closes by itself after several seconds.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Take a credit card payment in DejaPayPro
steps: When the cart is complete, tap ENTER.
Tap CREDIT/DEBIT.
The Dejavoo payment terminal wakes up and asks for Credit or Debit. Have the customer select Credit.
Chip card: insert it into the terminal's EMV reader.
Contactless: tap on the terminal's display.
No chip: swipe the card on the terminal.
Card cannot be read: enter the card number.
Tap CLOSE to finish. It also closes by itself after several seconds.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Take a PIN debit payment in DejaPayPro
steps: The Dejavoo terminal must have its PIN pad encrypted to use this payment method.
When the cart is complete, tap ENTER.
Tap CREDIT/DEBIT.
When the terminal asks for Credit or Debit, have the customer select Debit.
Insert, tap or swipe the card on the terminal.
Have the customer enter their PIN on the terminal and press OK.
Tap CLOSE to finish.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Take an EBT payment in DejaPayPro
steps: The Dejavoo terminal must have its PIN pad encrypted to use this payment method.
When the cart is complete, tap ENTER.
Tap EBT.
Select EBT FOOD, EBT FOOD VOUCHER or EBT CASH BENEFIT.
Swipe the EBT card or enter it manually.
Have the customer enter their PIN on the terminal and press OK.
Tap CLOSE to finish.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Take a check payment in DejaPayPro
steps: When the cart is complete, tap ENTER.
Tap CHECK.
Enter the check number and press CONFIRM.
Tap CLOSE to finish.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Take a gift card payment in DejaPayPro
steps: When the cart is complete, tap ENTER.
Tap GIFT.
Tap CLOSE to finish.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Send an email invoice for an order in DejaPayPro
steps: When the cart is complete, tap ENTER.
Tap INVOICE.
Enter the recipient's email address when prompted and press ENTER.
Tap CLOSE to finish.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Split a bill across several payments (partial payment) in DejaPayPro
steps: When the cart is complete, tap ENTER.
Tap Partial Payment.
Enter the partial amount and press ENTER.
On the payment selection screen, choose the form of payment taken for that amount and confirm or pay.
Repeat with other payment methods until the balance is paid.
When the full balance is paid, tap CLOSE.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Add a tip during a payment in DejaPayPro
steps: The payment terminal must be programmed with TIP MODE: ON for a tip prompt at the time of sale.
Select the payment type on the register. It shows Processing Transaction and sends the sale to the Dejavoo terminal.
The terminal asks the customer to pick a pre-programmed tip or enter their own amount, then press OK.
The customer inserts, taps or swipes the card, or the card number is entered.
Tap CLOSE to finish.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Cannot add a tip after the sale on a retail DejaPayPro setup
steps: Both the retail and restaurant software can add a tip during a transaction.
Only the restaurant software can add a tip after a transaction is completed.
If the tip prompt is missing at the time of sale, the terminal must be programmed with TIP MODE: ON, which is a terminal programming change.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Print the X report (X Tape) in DejaPayPro
steps: From the main screen, press the MORE icon in the upper right corner.
Tap X/Z Tape.
Tap PRINT X TAPE.
Tap PRINT.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: View sales charts by day or month in DejaPayPro
steps: From the main screen, press the MORE icon in the upper right corner.
Tap REPORTS.
Tap CHARTS to bring up the sales summary reports and charts.
Choose daily or monthly with the option in the left corner of the screen.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Search for an item in DejaPayPro
steps: With the customer cart open, press the SEARCH icon at the top left.
Type the item name. A picture of the item appears below the search bar.
Press the picture to add it to the cart. Each press adds one more.
Press the X beside the search bar to close the search.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Ring up an item that is not in the inventory (manual item) in DejaPayPro
steps: With the customer cart open, press the +MANUAL icon at the top of the screen.
Key in the price of the item.
Press ADD, then CLOSE.
To describe it, select the item on the right side, press COMMENT, type the description and press SAVE.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Change how many items show per line on the DejaPayPro screen
steps: With the customer cart open, press the MORE icon at the top of the screen.
Press MANAGE ITEMS.
Press EDIT ITEMS and choose how many items to view per line.
The inventory syncs and the cart window changes.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Add a category on the DejaPayPro register
steps: With the customer cart open, press the MORE icon.
Press REGISTER SETTINGS, then SETTINGS.
Tap INVENTORY on the left side.
In the INDUSTRY EDITOR tap CATEGORIES.
Press CREATE CATEGORY and enter the category name.
Optionally tap CHOOSE IMAGE and pick an image from the gallery or camera.
Press SAVE.
Use the back arrow at the top left until the cart screen returns.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Add an item on the DejaPayPro register
steps: With the customer cart open, press the MORE icon.
Press REGISTER SETTINGS, then SETTINGS.
Tap INVENTORY on the left side.
In the INDUSTRY EDITOR tap ITEMS.
Press CREATE ITEM.
Enter the item name, retail price, cost price and a PLU code. The PLU code can be typed or scanned with the barcode scanner.
Assign the item to a category. This is required.
Optionally tap CHOOSE IMAGE to add a picture.
Press SAVE.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Process a return in DejaPayPro
steps: With the customer cart open, press the MORE icon at the top of the screen.
Press the RETURN button.
Enter your OPERATOR number when asked.
Select the type of return, for example CREDIT.
Key in the amount of the return and press ENTER.
Choose the terminal to apply it to.
The return is processed automatically. Press the X at the top left until you are back at the cart screen.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Void a cart in DejaPayPro
steps: With the customer cart open, press the MORE icon at the top of the screen.
Press the VOID button.
Select Void Cart.
Enter the Manager PIN and confirm with the password.
Choose yes to close the cart.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Add an external Bluetooth printer (kitchen or counter) in DejaPayPro
steps: With the customer cart open, press the MORE icon.
Press REGISTER SETTINGS, then SETTINGS.
Tap PRINTERS on the left side.
Press ADD PRINTER.
Choose the printer type from the options shown.
Select the preset terminal profile number (TPN) for your Bluetooth terminal. The register then looks for available Bluetooth devices.
Select the printing device from the list.
Press ADD to save the printer. You will be asked to pair the Bluetooth device.
Go back to the cart screen. You can now select this printer when printing receipts.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Change the DejaPayPro default password or an employee's PIN
steps: Log in to the DeNovo Back Office portal.
Open the inventory and use the edit operator function.
Set a new password. It must be four digits. You can type one or have a random code generated.
Click save.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Turn employee time tracking on or off in DejaPayPro
steps: Open Settings and go to the Set Up Wizard.
Select GENERAL SETTINGS.
Turn EMPLOYEE TIME TRACKING to ON to enable it, or OFF to disable it.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Clock in, clock out or take a break in DejaPayPro
steps: Time tracking must be enabled first.
On the DejaPayPro start screen select IN to clock in, OUT to clock out, or BREAK for a break.
Enter your own 4 digit PIN.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Add a tip after the payment (tip adjust) in DejaPayPro Restaurant
steps: When no tip was entered during payment, the receipt prints a blank tip line for the customer to fill in.
On the register select MORE.
Select X/Z Tape.
Select the connected terminal from the list.
Find and select the transaction.
When the receipt shows, select TIP ADJUST.
Enter the tip amount the customer wrote and select ENTER.
The tip posts on the receipt copy in DejaPayPro.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Void a tab in DejaPayPro Restaurant
steps: With the customer tab open, press the MORE icon at the top of the screen.
Press the VOID button.
Select Void Tab.
Enter the Manager PIN and confirm with the password.
Choose yes to close the tab.
entries.note: From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Create, edit or delete restaurant tables for DejaPayPro
steps: This is done in the DeNovo back office, not on the register. Log in with the credentials your merchant services provider gave you.
Go down to the TABLES option.
Click CREATE NEW TABLE, or the EDIT or DELETE icon next to a table.
Fill in the number, name, number of seats, format (for example round or square), colour and the operator (server) assigned.
Repeat for each table.
entries.note: The guide gives the DeNovo login address as https://dvmms.com/denovo/account/login. From the 2018 DejaPayPro user guide; screens on a current D1 may differ

entries.title: Create a new inventory in DeNovo (first-time DejaPayPro setup)
steps: In the DeNovo portal find Inventory on the left side bar and click the + symbol.
Enter the inventory name, usually your company name.
Select the currency.
Select the business type: Retail, Restaurant and Cafe (adds table management) or Service (adds a schedule).
Enter any taxes.
Select the payment types you will use and whether each needs a terminal.
Create any cart discounts you want.
Press Save.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: What each DejaPayPro payment tool does
steps: Credit / Debit: the payment terminal asks the customer to choose Credit or Debit (PIN).
EBT: pay EBT Food or EBT Cash eligible sales with an EBT card or voucher.
Cash: cash payment.
Check: payment by personal check.
Invoice: creates an email invoice of the order.
Gift: payment by gift card.
Partial Payment: allows partial payments toward the cart balance.
Precheck: prints a receipt before payment.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: Set the inventory location and pair the register in DeNovo
steps: In DeNovo click INVENTORY on the left side panel.
Select the inventory from the list.
Click More at the top right and choose Locations.
Select the location. One is created by default with every inventory.
Click Save.
POS devices pair automatically after you enter the Inventory and Location on the device.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: Add an employee (operator) and their login PIN in DeNovo
steps: In the DeNovo portal open the inventory and scroll down to Operators.
Select Create New Operator.
Set the Location to match the device the person will use, and fill in the remaining fields including Position.
Create a four digit numerical password for their login.
Make sure the status is Active and set their access options.
Save.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: Remove an employee in DeNovo
steps: In the DeNovo portal open the inventory and scroll down to Operators.
Click the X next to the employee.
In the confirmation box choose YES CONTINUE.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: Add or edit a supplier in DeNovo
steps: In DeNovo click INVENTORY on the left side panel.
Click the inventory and scroll to the bottom of the page.
Fill in the supplier form: name, description, tax ID, taxes, country, state, city, address and ZIP, email, phone, lead time in days and preferred shipping method.
Press Save.
To edit a supplier later, click the Edit icon near the Phone column on the Inventory Suppliers page.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: Create or edit a product category (department) in DeNovo
steps: In DeNovo click INVENTORY on the left side panel and select the inventory.
Scroll down to Categories and click Create New Category.
Enter the category name, pick a colour and optionally an image.
Click Save.
To edit a category, click the Edit button near the Items column.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: Create or edit an item in DeNovo
steps: Create at least one category first. An item cannot exist without a category.
In DeNovo click INVENTORY, click the inventory and scroll down to Items.
Fill in the form: inventory, name, type (goods or service), category, description, optional External ID (a short name), bar code, cost, price and optional supplier.
Add the quantity on hand, minimum and maximum quantity, whether it uses a weighing scale, which taxes apply and any modifiers.
Click SAVE.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: Export items from DeNovo to Excel
steps: In DeNovo click INVENTORY and select the inventory.
Scroll down to Items and click Export to File.
Choose to Excel File.
Open the downloaded file. You can edit it and import it back into DeNovo.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: Import items into DeNovo from Excel
steps: In DeNovo click INVENTORY and select the inventory.
Scroll down to Items and click Import From File.
Click Select File to Import Items For Inventory and choose the Excel file.
If your column names differ from DeNovo's, use the File Map option to match them.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: Imported spreadsheet columns do not match DeNovo (create a File Map)
steps: In DeNovo open the inventory, scroll to Items and click Import From File.
Click the + symbol to the right of the File Map line.
In the New/Edit File Map window, type your own column name in the property line next to the matching DeNovo category. For example type PLU next to Barcode.
Click SAVE.
Select your mapping from the File Map drop down in the import window and select IMPORT.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: View sales history in DeNovo
steps: In the DeNovo portal click SALES HISTORY on the left side panel.
Click the > icon under the date of a transaction to see its details.
Use the search filters to narrow by date, subtotal, discount, taxes or TPN.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: View X and Z reports in DeNovo
steps: X reports can be checked at any time. Z reports are only available after a shift is closed.
Open your inventory and click X/Z Reports on the left side bar.
Click the icon at the right end of a report line to view the full report. You can export it as a PDF.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: View summary reports (sales, timesheets, categories, items) in DeNovo
steps: Open your inventory and click Summary Page on the left side bar.
Use the four options at the top right to group data by Day, Week, Month or Year.
Click the > button on a section to open the Timesheet summary, Summary by Category or Summary by Item.
entries.note: DeNovo back office for DejaPayPro; manual dated 2018

entries.title: DeNovo services must be switched on for the terminal's TPN
steps: DeNovo services are activated per TPN by the ISO in STEAM, under the Managed Services icon next to the TPN number.
After the change is saved, the terminal picks it up with a partial download or at its scheduled autoload.
A merchant cannot make this change. Ask support to check that DeNovo is activated on the TPN.

entries.title: Where to log in to DeNovo
steps: DeNovo is reached at https://dvmms.com/denovo/account/login.
The ISO guide says the login uses the same username and password as the STEAM account.
Once logged in, TERMINALS on the left toolbar lists the TPNs enabled with DeNovo services.
entries.note: Written for ISO users; a merchant login is provided by the merchant services provider

entries.title: Log in to the iPOSpays portal / virtual terminal
steps: Go to www.ipospays.com.
Type your username and password to log in.
entries.note: Our sheets give portal.ipospays.com as the address; the Dejavoo manual says www.ipospays.com

entries.title: Run a virtual terminal (CloudPOS) sale on a Dejavoo pinpad
steps: Log in to the iPOSpays portal and click CloudPOS.
Click Card Payments and select Pinpad.
Enter the amount and select Process.
The sale appears on the POS device. Follow the standard transaction procedure there.

entries.title: Link a Dejavoo terminal to the virtual terminal (CloudPOS TPN)
steps: On the POS device select the Favourites icon.
Click the Upgrade App button.
Enter the current TPN password.
Enter the newly created CloudPOS enabled TPN.
Click No.
The SPIn screen appears on the POS device.
This needs the TPN password and a CloudPOS TPN created by the ISO, so it is normally done with support.

entries.title: Virtual terminal cannot send sales to the pinpad: SPIn Cloud must be enabled on the TPN
steps: The pinpad option needs the TPN's Integration section set to Spin with Spin Mode set to Cloud.
This is set in S.T.E.A.M, Edit Parameters, by the ISO.
Ask support to check the TPN integration setting.

entries.title: Virtual terminal (CloudPOS) is missing from the portal
steps: CloudPOS is a module the ISO enables under Modules & Privileges when the merchant is onboarded.
A CloudPOS TPN is created by choosing CloudPOS as the manufacturer when adding a device.
A merchant cannot enable it. Ask support to enable the CloudPOS module.

entries.title: iPOSpays portal username and activation email
steps: The merchant's email address is used as the portal username.
That address receives an activation email.

entries.title: What the iPOSpays portal modules do (STEAM, CloudPOS, My Customer)
steps: STEAM lets the merchant view and edit TPN parameters.
CloudPOS lets the merchant accept virtual (online) payments.
My Customer lets the merchant view and add customers and invoices.
Modules are enabled by the ISO to suit the merchant.

entries.title: Sales with a fee added are declined (With Fee / Without Fee MID profiles)
steps: iPOSpays supports two MIDs on one device, under a With Fee profile and a Without Fee profile.
A sale run with a cash discount fee or custom fee uses the MID under With Fee.
If only the Without Fee profile is configured and a sale is run with a fee added, the transaction is declined.
This is a profile setting on the TPN. Ask support to check the profile.
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: Tip adjust from the iPOSpays portal depends on the Tips setting
steps: In the TPN parameters under Tips & Taxes, Tip set to yes allows merchants to do tip adjust from the portal.
Tip suggestion on Paper prints tip choices on the customer's receipt.
Tip suggestion on POS lets the customer choose and pay a tip on the device.
If tip adjust is not available, ask support to check the Tips setting on the TPN.
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: Manual versus automatic settlement on iPOSpays terminals
steps: With Manual Settlement the merchant must settle from the POS device.
With Automatic Settlement a mode and time are chosen in the TPN parameters.
If the automatic settlement is POS initiated, a print receipt choice is also set.
To change the mode or time, ask support to edit the TPN's Settlement parameters.
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: Transaction types, entry modes and card types are switched on per TPN
steps: The TPN's Transaction section selects the allowed transaction types, card entry modes and card types.
AVS, Signature Line, Cash Back, Pin Prompt and PinBypass Debit are also enabled there.
If a transaction type or card type is not offered, ask support to check the TPN's Transaction parameters.
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: A pinpad paired to a Dejavoo terminal uses the same TPN as the main terminal
steps: The same TPN number must be entered on both the Slave (pinpad) and Master devices.
The Master device's parameters are then assigned to the Slave automatically.
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: Consumer choice fee setting
steps: With Consumer choice selected in the TPN's Fee section, customers can choose whether to pay with cash or card.
The fee percentage is entered in the same place.
Changes to the fee are made in the TPN parameters by support.
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: D1 accepts chip, tap and mobile wallets
steps: The D1 has Smart IC (chip) and NFC readers with EMV certification.
It is compatible with Apple Pay, Google Wallet and Samsung Pay.

entries.title: Software the D1 runs
steps: Dejavoo says the D1 runs DejaPayPro and connects to DeNovo for business management.
Its compatible software is listed as iPOSpays and SPIn.
It works with Dejavoo PIN pads as an add-on.

entries.title: iPOSpays portal users and permissions
steps: Unlimited users can be added to iPOSpays.
Role based permission settings are available.
entries.note: Tier 2 (PayCompass)

entries.title: When iPOSpays creates a customer record after a payment
steps: A new customer record is created when payment is made by invoice, payment link or itemized billing.
The Quick pay feature does not create a customer profile.
entries.note: Tier 2 (PayCompass)

entries.title: iPOSpays stores cards as tokens
steps: Card vaulting is available, but only as a token, not raw card data.
Multiple payment methods per customer are kept through tokenization and the My Customers module.
entries.note: Tier 2 (PayCompass)

entries.title: Payment methods and features in iPOSpays
steps: iPOSpays accepts cash, credit/debit and ACH.
It offers invoicing, recurring billing, payment pages, scheduled payments, QR code payments and text to pay.
It does not send automated payment reminders to customers.
entries.note: Tier 2 (PayCompass)

entries.title: First Data North: which Dejavoo devices are supported
steps: On First Data North, the QD series is not supported.
iPOSGo! is not supported.
The Z and P series are supported.
entries.note: Tier 2 (PayCompass). applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: Dejavoo 2024 advisory: terminals processing without the P2PE key
steps: In 2024 Dejavoo found some gateway terminals with Point to Point Encryption disabled or not activated because of incorrect TPN parameters.
Most were fixed automatically through Auto Download and Auto RKL.
A few terminals need manual intervention to complete encryption. Dejavoo contacts the partner about those merchants.
A merchant cannot fix this alone. Contact support if told the terminal needs encryption.
entries.note: applies to all Dejavoo terminals on iPOSpays

entries.title: What the icons on the idle screen do
steps: The idle screen shows the payment screen plus a set of icons.
One icon opens the FAVORITES menu.
One icon opens the CORE menu.
One icon is the CALL ME feature.
One icon downloads the quick reference guide.
entries.note: The PDF version of the same guide labels the second icon 'Access to other sales features' instead of the CORE menu.

entries.title: Run a credit card sale
steps: Enter the sale amount and press Ok.
Review the amount and tap Proceed.
Tap Cash Payment or Card Payment. The price is based on the payment type.
Have the customer tap (contactless only), swipe or insert the chip card.
Depending on how the terminal is set up, choose how to send the customer copy: SMS, email, paper print or no receipt.
The transaction is processed and the sales receipt prints.
entries.note: The guide is written for the whole P line; steps that mention printing apply only to models with a printer.

entries.title: Why the terminal asks Cash Payment or Card Payment
steps: During a sale the terminal asks you to choose Cash Payment or Card Payment.
Tap the one the customer is using.
The price charged is based on the payment type you choose.

entries.title: Receipt choices after a sale: SMS, email, paper or none
steps: After a sale the terminal can offer to send the customer copy by SMS, by email, as a paper print, or not at all.
Which choices appear depends on how the terminal's TPN is configured.

entries.title: Run a debit sale
steps: Enter the sale amount and press Ok.
Review the amount and tap Proceed.
Tap Cash Payment or Card Payment. The price is based on the payment type.
Tap the Debit icon, then have the customer tap (contactless only), insert or swipe the card.
The customer enters their PIN on the terminal or on the PIN pad and presses Enter.
The transaction is processed and the sales receipt prints.
entries.note: The guide is written for the whole P line; steps that mention printing apply only to models with a printer.

entries.title: Key in a card number by hand (card not present)
steps: Enter the sale amount and press Ok.
Review the amount and tap Proceed.
Tap Card Payment. The price is based on the payment type.
Tap Enter Card under other options.
Type in the card number.
Follow the prompts, such as expiry date and ZIP code. Which prompts appear depends on the terminal's configuration.
Depending on how the terminal is set up, choose how to send the customer copy.
The transaction is processed and the sales receipt prints.
entries.note: The guide is written for the whole P line; steps that mention printing apply only to models with a printer.

entries.title: A void does not need the customer's card
steps: You can void a transaction without the card being present.
Find the transaction by its transaction number or by the last 4 digits of the card.

entries.title: Ask for a call back from the help desk (Call Me)
steps: This feature must be enabled on your terminal.
Tap the phone icon.
Tap Call Me under the Support Menu and choose a reason.
Enter your call back number.
The terminal notifies the help desk and a representative calls you back.

entries.title: Settling shows a prompt about untipped transactions
steps: When you tap Settle, a prompt may appear if some transactions have no tip.
Answer Yes or No to continue with the settlement.
To add the tips first, use Adjust Tip in the Favorites menu before settling.

entries.title: Print a report (open batch or closed batch)
steps: Tap the star icon to open the Favorites menu.
Tap Reports.
Choose Open Batch or Closed Batch.
Tap the report type you want and choose how the report groups your transactions (summary report or daily report).
Tap Next.
Swipe left to go from the summary to the details report, then tap the print icon.
The report prints.
entries.note: The guide is written for the whole P line; steps that mention printing apply only to models with a printer.

entries.title: Power off or reboot the terminal
steps: Press and hold the button on the side of the terminal until a menu appears on the screen.
The menu offers Power Off and Reboot.
Tap the one you want.

entries.title: Wi-Fi icon is blinking
steps: A blinking Wi-Fi icon means the terminal is not connected to Wi-Fi.
When the terminal is connected, the icon stays still.

entries.title: Connect by Ethernet cable
steps: Plug the terminal into power first.
Then plug an Ethernet cable into the terminal's Ethernet port.
entries.note: Applies only to P-line models that have an Ethernet port.

entries.title: Idle screen icons (PDF version of the quick reference guide)
steps: The idle screen shows icons for the FAVORITES menu, for other sales features, and for the CALL ME feature.
entries.note: The web version of the same guide calls the second icon 'Access to the CORE menu'. The two versions disagree on the label.

entries.title: Debit sale: receipt options appear after the PIN is entered
steps: After the customer enters the PIN and presses Enter, the terminal may offer to send the customer copy by SMS, email, paper print or no receipt, depending on the TPN configuration.
Then the transaction is processed and the sales receipt prints.
entries.note: The PDF lists this receipt step for debit; the web page version omits it.

entries.title: Pair a P terminal as a PIN pad to a main terminal
steps: On the main screen, tap the red gear at the bottom left corner.
Enter your password to open settings.
Tap PinPad.
Follow the pairing instructions shown on that screen.

entries.title: PIN pad will not pair or connect to the main terminal
steps: Make sure both terminals are connected to the same network.
If the site has extenders and routers, select the same one on both devices.
For example, if the main terminal is on the main router, the PIN pad cannot be on the extender.

entries.title: Which P terminals can act as a PIN pad or main terminal
steps: Dejavoo states that all P terminal hardware combinations can be used as PIN pads and as master terminals.
entries.note: PayCompass (tier 2) says the P5 and P8 do not support external PIN pads; the two sources differ.

entries.title: Load a paper roll in the P3
steps: Hold the device in both hands.
Pinch the sides of the top of the device, next to the card tap section.
Flip the top away from the device screen.
Put the receipt paper into the slot of the printer. The guide says the paper size should be about 50 ft.
Pull out some paper so the end is left outside, then close the top.

entries.title: Turn the P3 on or off
steps: Press and hold the POWER button on the side of the terminal until a menu appears.
The menu offers POWER OFF, REBOOT, AIRPLANE MODE and SILENT MODE.
Select the option you want.

entries.title: Register a SIM card for 4G service (Dejavoo Systems portal)
steps: Open the Dejavoo Systems portal.
Select your monthly plan. An AT&T SIM needs an AT&T plan; a Verizon SIM needs a Verizon plan.
Choose your subscription plan from the drop-down menu.
Enter your email address and create a password.
Enter your credit card details.
Enter your billing address, or tick the box if it is the same as your postal address.
Enter your billing contact phone number.
Tick the box to agree to the terms and conditions.
When everything is filled in, the INCOMPLETE button changes to SIGN-UP. Click SIGN-UP.
A window confirms the account was created.
Check your email for instructions on setting up your service.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P3 guide. SIM plans carry a monthly charge; ask before signing up.

entries.title: Chip credit sale on the P3 (PaymentCloud's steps)
steps: Tap CREDIT.
Tap SALE.
If asked, enter the clerk ID and press OK.
Enter the sale amount and press OK.
Have the customer tap (contactless only) or insert the chip card.
If asked, confirm the sale amount by tapping OK or NO.
The transaction is processed and the receipt prints.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P3 guide. It describes a build with CREDIT/DEBIT menus and manager password 1234, which differs from Dejavoo's own P-line guide (last 4 digits of the TPN); the merchant's software build may not match.

entries.title: Manual entry credit sale on the P3 (PaymentCloud's steps)
steps: Tap CREDIT.
Tap the SALE icon.
If asked, enter the clerk ID and press OK.
Enter the sale amount and press OK.
Type in the card number.
If asked, follow the prompts such as expiry date and ZIP code.
The transaction is processed and the receipt prints.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P3 guide. It describes a build with CREDIT/DEBIT menus and manager password 1234, which differs from Dejavoo's own P-line guide (last 4 digits of the TPN); the merchant's software build may not match.

entries.title: Debit sale on the P3 (PaymentCloud's steps)
steps: Tap DEBIT.
Tap SALE.
If asked, enter the clerk ID and press OK.
Enter the sale amount and press OK.
Have the customer tap or insert the chip card.
If asked, confirm the sale amount by tapping OK or NO.
The customer enters their PIN on the terminal or the external PIN pad and presses OK.
The transaction is processed and the receipt prints.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P3 guide. It describes a build with CREDIT/DEBIT menus and manager password 1234, which differs from Dejavoo's own P-line guide (last 4 digits of the TPN); the merchant's software build may not match.

entries.title: Change the date and time on the P3 (PaymentCloud's steps)
steps: From the idle screen, press OK to open the Core Menu.
Tap UTILITY.
Tap SETTINGS.
Tap DATE AND TIME.
If the date shown is correct press OK. If not, clear it with the yellow backspace key and enter the date as MM/DD/YY.
If the time shown is correct press OK. If not, clear it with the yellow backspace key and enter the time in 24-hour format.
The terminal returns to the settings menu.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P3 guide. It describes a build with CREDIT/DEBIT menus and manager password 1234, which differs from Dejavoo's own P-line guide (last 4 digits of the TPN); the merchant's software build may not match.

entries.title: Reboot the P3 (troubleshooting tip)
steps: Find the small button on the side of the P3 marked with a dash inside a circle and press it.
The screen offers POWER OFF or REBOOT.
Select REBOOT.
entries.note: From the Troubleshooting & Tips section of PaymentCloud's P3 guide.

entries.title: Factory reset the P3 (erases everything)
steps: Do not start this without support: the guide warns a factory reset erases all data on the device, including transaction history and customized settings.
The guide's steps are: swipe down from the top of the screen and open the Android settings gear.
Select About Device at the bottom of the screen.
Tap Custom Build Version 6 times.
Select the Dialer.
Enter *#87#.
Select Factory Reset.
entries.note: PaymentCloud's P5 guide adds that if a factory reset is done incorrectly Dejavoo will not be able to reinstall the app. Treat as a tech-support procedure.

entries.title: Who PaymentCloud's P3 guide says to contact about the terminal
steps: For customer service issues with the terminal, the guide says to contact Dejavoo directly by email (support@dejavoo.io) or by phone (877-358-6797).
entries.note: This is the maker's line as given by a reseller; our own tech support is the first contact for our merchants.

entries.title: The P5 has no printer and takes no paper
steps: The P5 has no built-in receipt printer, so there is no paper roll to load.
It cannot print or reprint customer receipts, and it cannot print reports.
Send receipts by email or text instead.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Reprinting a receipt is not possible on the P5
steps: The P5 has no built-in printer, so it cannot print or reprint customer receipts.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Turn the P5 on or off
steps: To turn it on, press and hold the power button until the device activates.
To turn it off, press and hold the power button until the device powers off.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: The P5 cannot use Ethernet
steps: The P5 is not compatible with an Ethernet connection.
Connect it by Wi-Fi instead.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Chip credit sale on the P5
steps: Select the SALE icon on the home screen.
Enter the sale amount, then confirm.
If asked to choose between CASH PAYMENT and CARD PAYMENT, select CARD PAYMENT.
Have the cardholder insert the chip card or tap.
Remove the card when prompted.
The transaction is approved or declined. The cardholder may be asked to sign.
Send the cardholder a receipt by email or text if wanted.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Tip prompt during a sale on the P5
steps: Before the transaction is approved or declined, the cardholder may be asked to leave a tip (for example 15% or 20%).
The guide says this mainly applies to restaurant and service businesses.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.
