entries.title: Manual entry credit sale on the P5
steps: Select the SALE icon on the home screen.
Enter the sale amount, then confirm.
When the terminal asks for the card, select ENTER CARD #.
Type in the card number, the expiration date and the billing zip code.
The sale is approved or declined.
Send the cardholder a receipt by email or text if wanted.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ. The guide notes a manual entry sale depends on the terminal's configuration.

entries.title: Debit sale on the P5
steps: Select the SALE icon on the home screen.
Enter the sale amount, then confirm.
If asked to choose between CASH PAYMENT and CARD PAYMENT, select CARD PAYMENT.
When prompted, select DEBIT.
Have the cardholder swipe, insert or tap their card.
The customer enters their PIN on the P5.
Send the cardholder a receipt by email or text if wanted.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Cash sale on the P5
steps: Select the SALE icon on the home screen.
If asked to choose between CASH PAYMENT and CARD PAYMENT, select CASH.
Enter the sale amount, then confirm.
Enter the cash received from the customer under CASH IN. The CHANGE display shows any balance.
Confirm the cash transaction.
Send the customer a receipt by email or text if wanted.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Credit card return on the P5
steps: Open the MENU on the P5.
If asked, enter the manager password.
Select the REFUND icon.
Enter the return amount, then confirm.
Insert or tap the card used for the original transaction.
Send the cardholder a receipt by email or text if wanted.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Debit card return on the P5
steps: Open the MENU on the P5.
If asked, enter the manager password.
Select the REFUND icon.
Enter the return amount, then confirm.
Insert, swipe or tap the card used for the original transaction.
The PIN is entered on the P5 to verify the return.
Send the cardholder a receipt by email or text if wanted.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Cash return on the P5
steps: Open the MENU on the P5.
If asked, enter the manager password.
Select the REFUND icon.
When asked for the refund method, select CASH. If prompted, select SALE.
Enter the return amount, then confirm.
Send the customer a receipt by email or text if wanted.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Void a credit transaction on the P5 (card present or not)
steps: Open the MENU on the P5.
Select VOID.
Enter either the last four digits of the card used or the transaction number.
If asked, enter the manager password.
The void is processed, with the option to send a receipt by text or email.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ. The guide gives the same steps for card present and card not present.

entries.title: Change the date and time on the P5
steps: Open the MENU on the P5.
If asked, select UTILITY.
Select SETTINGS.
Select DATE AND TIME.
If the date and time shown are right, leave them. If not, clear them and re-enter.
Enter the date as MM/DD/YY.
Enter the time in 24-hour format.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Change menu security settings on the P5
steps: Open the MENU on the P5.
If asked, select UTILITY.
Select SECURITY.
Select MENU UTILITY.
Choose the security option you want.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Adjust the display contrast on the P5
steps: Open the MENU on the P5.
If asked, select UTILITY.
Select SETTINGS.
Select DISPLAY.
Tap + to increase contrast or - to decrease it.
Save your settings.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Factory reset on a P-line terminal: do not do it without support
steps: Do not factory reset the terminal on your own.
The guide warns that if a factory reset is performed incorrectly, Dejavoo will not be able to reinstall the app on the device.
It also says that if the terminal is then sent back for repair, Dejavoo reserves the right not to swap it.
Contact support for help instead.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ. The guide names the P1, P3 and P5 as examples of P line terminals.

entries.title: Factory reset the P5 from Android settings (guide's steps)
steps: This is a support procedure; see the warning entry before attempting it.
On the P5 screen, select ANDROID SETTINGS.
Select ABOUT DEVICE at the bottom of the screen.
Tap HARDWARE VERSION or CUSTOM BUILD VERSION 6 to 8 times, depending on the terminal.
Select the DIALER.
Enter *#87#.
The device begins its factory reset.
If prompted, download the TPN.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Factory reset from Android Recovery mode (guide's alternative)
steps: This is a support procedure; see the warning entry before attempting it.
Press and hold the POWER and VOLUME buttons together for about ten to fifteen seconds.
The device may go into Android Recovery mode.
Select WIPE DATA/FACTORY RESET, then confirm.
The device begins its factory reset.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: Reboot the P5 (troubleshooting tip)
steps: Find the small button on the side of the P5 marked with a dash inside a circle and press it.
The screen offers POWER OFF or REBOOT.
Select REBOOT.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's P5 guide (tier 2); the merchant's software build may differ.

entries.title: The P17 is powered over USB from the P1
steps: Dejavoo describes the P17 as USB-powered through the P1 terminal.
A single USB connection means the pad needs no power adapter of its own.

entries.title: P17 Wi-Fi is 2.4GHz
steps: Dejavoo's product page lists the P17's connectivity as Wi-Fi 2.4GHz, a USB Type-C port and an audio jack.
entries.note: Our sheet says the P17 flyer names no Wi-Fi band; the product page names 2.4GHz only.

entries.title: Card types the P17 reads
steps: The P17 supports chip (IC), contactless (NFC) and magstripe cards.
Listed contactless methods are Paypass (Mastercard), Paywave (Visa), Expresspay (AMEX) and D-PAS (Discover).

entries.title: The P17 works with CloudPOS
steps: Dejavoo lists CloudPOS compatibility for the P17.

entries.title: The P12 charging cradle is a separate purchase
steps: The P12's cradle is sold separately.

entries.title: Card types the P12 reads: chip, tap and QR code
steps: Dejavoo's P12 flyer lists its payment readers as an IC (chip) card reader, an NFC (tap) reader and QR code.
It works with digital wallets including Apple Pay, Google Wallet and Samsung Pay.
entries.note: The flyer does not list a magnetic stripe reader for the P12. Our sheet calls the P12 a 'swiper'.

entries.title: What the P12 is: a standalone Android mPOS / PIN pad
steps: Dejavoo describes the P12 as an Android mPOS/PIN Pad with a 4-inch touchscreen.
It runs an Android-based system and is compatible with iPOSpays, SPIn and DeNovo.
entries.note: Our sheet describes the P12 as a reader paired to the merchant's phone through an app; the maker's page describes a touchscreen Android terminal.

entries.title: How the P12 connects: dual-band Wi-Fi, cellular, Bluetooth
steps: The P12 has dual-band Wi-Fi (2.4GHz and 5GHz).
It supports 2G/3G/4G cellular networks.
It has Bluetooth 4.2.

entries.title: Cellular on the P12 is an optional configuration
steps: The P12 can support cellular data, but PayCompass notes this is an optional configuration.
If a P12 will not connect over cellular, check whether the unit was ordered with cellular.

entries.title: Receipts on the P12: email, SMS or none; paper only with a separate printer
steps: The P12 offers email, SMS or no receipt.
A paper receipt is available only when the P12 is paired with a separate printer.

entries.title: Optional PIN pad for the P12: the P17
steps: PayCompass lists the Dejavoo P17 as the optional PIN pad for the P12.

entries.title: The P12 does not capture signatures
steps: PayCompass lists signature capture as not available on the P12.
Tips are supported.

entries.title: How the P18 connects: Ethernet, 4G/LTE, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth
steps: The P18 supports Ethernet, 4G/LTE, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth 5.2.
It takes a Nano SIM.

entries.title: The P18 runs Android 13
steps: Dejavoo lists the P18's software as Android 13.

entries.title: The P18's second screen shows the amount to the customer
steps: The P18 has a hidden second screen that displays transaction amounts to the customer.

entries.title: Payment types the P18 accepts
steps: The P18 supports chip (IC), contactless (NFC), magstripe cards, QR code, digital wallets and Apple Pay.

entries.title: The P18 has no built-in printer; use an external one
steps: The P18 does not have a built-in printer.
Receipts can go by email, SMS or digital link.
An external printer can be connected by Bluetooth, Wi-Fi or Ethernet cable.

entries.title: Optional PIN pad for the P18: the P17
steps: PayCompass lists the Dejavoo P17 Android PIN Pad as the optional PIN pad for the P18.

entries.title: Fleet cards on the P18 need to be set up first
steps: The P18 does not take fleet cards out of the box.
PayCompass says it has to be configured by the processor to accept WEX, Voyager, Fuelman, Comdata and Fleet One.
If a fleet card will not go through, ask whether fleet acceptance was set up on the account.
entries.note: PayCompass is describing its own accounts; whether we offer this must be confirmed.

entries.title: Receipts on the P5: email and SMS only
steps: The P5 has no built-in receipt printer.
Receipts are sent by email or SMS.

entries.title: The P5 does not take an external PIN pad (per PayCompass)
steps: PayCompass states the P5 does not support external PIN pads.
entries.note: Dejavoo's own pin pad page says all P terminal combinations can be used as PIN pads and master terminals; the sources differ.

entries.title: The P8 does not take an external PIN pad (per PayCompass)
steps: PayCompass states the P8 does not support external PIN pads.
entries.note: Dejavoo's own pin pad page says all P terminal combinations can be used as PIN pads and master terminals; the sources differ.

entries.title: Receipt options on the P8
steps: The P8 can give a paper receipt, an email receipt, an SMS receipt or no receipt.
PayCompass lists signature capture as not available on the P8.

entries.title: P1 receipt options and optional PIN pad
steps: The P1 can give a paper receipt, an email receipt, an SMS receipt or no receipt.
Its optional PIN pad is the P17.
It connects by Ethernet and Wi-Fi.

entries.title: The P3 has no Ethernet; it uses cellular and Wi-Fi
steps: PayCompass lists the P3's connectivity as USB charger, cellular and Wi-Fi, with no Ethernet.
Its optional PIN pad is the Dejavoo P17.
entries.note: PaymentCloud's P3 guide titles its network section 'Ethernet or Wifi'; PayCompass says the P3 has no Ethernet.

entries.title: Dejavoo's own tech support line
steps: Dejavoo's tech support page gives the number 1-877-358-6797, option 2.
entries.note: For issues only the maker can resolve; our tech support is the first contact.

entries.title: Changing the TPN on the terminal needs a one-time passcode
steps: A one-time passcode (OTP) is required to change the Terminal Profile Number (TPN) on a terminal.
This is not something to do yourself; contact support if the terminal is asking to change or re-enter its TPN.

entries.title: Incremental Auth: raise the amount of a pre-auth
steps: On gateway-powered terminals, Incremental Auth lets you increase the amount first authorized in a Pre-Auth.

entries.title: "Spring Framework" error during Incremental Auth
steps: This error appeared on Dejavoo payment terminals during an Incremental Auth.
Dejavoo fixed it in a software update.
If you still see it, contact support so the terminal's software can be updated.

entries.title: See untipped and server reports for other terminals in the same store
steps: From one terminal, you can view untipped and server reports of the other TPNs within the same store.

entries.title: Tip Adjust by Store: adjust tips for several terminals from one device
steps: Merchants can adjust the tip for multiple TPNs from a single device or batch.
All the TPNs must be within the same store.

entries.title: Two settlement report emails arrived for one batch
steps: In some instances merchants received duplicate settlement reports by email after settling a batch.
Dejavoo says a software update addresses this.

entries.title: What the batch settlement report shows
steps: Batch settlement reports include Card Brand, Subtotal and Fee details.

entries.title: Tip screen: tapping a suggested tip moves straight to the next screen
steps: On gateway-powered terminals, when the customer taps one of the tip choices the app goes to the next screen.

entries.title: PIN pad transactions ask before printing the customer copy
steps: When the Customer Copy Print option is enabled, the merchant is asked to confirm printing the customer copy during PIN pad transactions.

entries.title: Comm Error: check the connection icon in the status bar
steps: Check the status bar at the top of the terminal screen.
Look for the Wi-Fi symbol (three curved lines coming out of one dot) or the Ethernet symbol (three dots between outward-facing arrows).
Connect with the type your model supports: Stax lists Wi-Fi for the QD2, and Wi-Fi or Ethernet for the QD4.
A Comm Error is often, but not always, resolved by checking connectivity.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Comm Error: run the terminal's network self-check
steps: Go to the home screen.
Select Settings.
Select Self-Check.
Select Network.
Select WiFi Network or Ethernet Network, whichever you want to check.
The check ends in either success or failure.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Comm Error: run a ping test from the terminal
steps: Go to the home screen and select Settings.
Select Self-Check, then Network, then WIFI Network, then Test WIFI.
Write down the IP Address and the public IP Address if there is one.
Go back twice with the left arrow at the bottom of the terminal.
Select Advance, then PingTool.
Enter the IP address and select Ping.
A few lines of data in the Ping Result means the test passed.
The word timeout in the Ping Result means the test failed.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Wi-Fi works but Ethernet does not (QD4)
steps: Make sure the Ethernet cords are plugged in properly and securely.
Plug one end into an Ethernet port on the wall, router or switch.
Plug the other end into the terminal's Ethernet port.
Check that the port is glowing green.
Try a different Ethernet cord.
If the port is not glowing green, the port has a problem and the terminal needs replacing.

entries.title: Terminal keeps turning off and on (reboot loop)
steps: Leave the terminal plugged in to a wall outlet, not a computer, for a few hours, preferably overnight.
The cause given: a nearly empty battery has enough power to turn on but not enough to stay on, so the terminal loops.
If it still has battery trouble after charging overnight, contact support because a replacement may be needed.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: What the red charging light means
steps: A flashing red light means damage to the charging port.
A solid red light while plugged in means the terminal is charging.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Red light is flashing
steps: A flashing red light means damage to the charging port.
Contact support: Stax lists a battery that is not charging among the hardware issues that go to Dejavoo Support.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: QD2 shows a solid red light, is plugged in, but will not power on
steps: The battery may not be charging.
Remove the terminal's back cover to find the battery, which has a wire plugged into the terminal.
Carefully unplug the battery from the terminal, then firmly plug it back in.
Let it charge for 30 minutes.
Try turning the terminal back on.

entries.title: Troubleshooting step 1: check the time zone, date and time
steps: Go to the home screen and select Settings.
Select Date & Time.
Turn off Automatic time zone and pick the time zone by hand (Stax lists PST = GMT -07:00, MST = GMT -06:00, CST = GMT -05:00, EST = GMT -04:00).
Turn off Automatic date & time and set the date and time by hand.
Turn both Automatic time zone and Automatic date & time back on.
Turn on Use 24-hour format.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Terminal keeps freezing or shows a spinning wheel
steps: It may have too many apps running at once.
Press and hold the home button (the circle at the bottom middle of the terminal) to see all open apps.
Swipe left on each window to close the app.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Update the Market and DvPay (Aura) apps on a black QD terminal
steps: Go to the terminal's home screen and select Market.
Market should start updating by itself. If it does not, select Install or Update if shown. If it only says Open, it is already on the latest version.
Check DvPay next. If there is an Update or Install button, select it and let it run.
Batch out.
The batch should prompt an automatic download. If it does not, or no batch is open, a full download is needed.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Update the DVStore and DvPay (Aura) apps on a white QD terminal
steps: Go to the terminal's home screen and select DVStore.
Select the menu (three lines) in the top left.
Select Update DVStore.
If the update fails, make sure the date and time are correct.
DvPay (Aura) updates automatically when DVStore updates.
Batch out. The batch should prompt an automatic download; if not, a full download is needed.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Error: Bad BIN / Host Disconnect
steps: Stax lists this error among the issues the merchant cannot clear on the terminal.
Contact support to have it resolved.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically. The page lists the message under 'Level 3: Partner Support Needed' with no further explanation.

entries.title: Error: Invalid Merchant
steps: Stax lists this error among the issues the merchant cannot clear on the terminal.
Contact support to have it resolved.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically. The page lists the message under 'Level 3: Partner Support Needed' with no further explanation.

entries.title: Error: Re-Enter
steps: Stax lists this error among the issues the merchant cannot clear on the terminal.
Contact support to have it resolved.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically. The page lists the message under 'Level 3: Partner Support Needed' with no further explanation.

entries.title: Error: Term ID
steps: Stax lists this error among the issues the merchant cannot clear on the terminal.
Contact support to have it resolved.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically. The page lists the message under 'Level 3: Partner Support Needed' with no further explanation.

entries.title: Not connected to the SPIn Proxy server
steps: This needs support to resolve; it is not something to fix on the terminal.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Change the automatic batch time
steps: Stax lists updating the batch time as something that needs support to do.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically. 'Update batch time.' is in the page's Level 3 list.

entries.title: Hardware problems that go to Dejavoo Support
steps: These go to Dejavoo Support at 877-358-6797, ext. 2: battery not charging; factory reset; terminal not powering on even after charging; terminal not accepting a tapped transaction; terminal missing applications such as DvPay or DvStore/Market.
Dejavoo will advise and refer you back to your processor if a new terminal is needed.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Terminal will not accept a tapped (contactless) transaction
steps: Stax treats this as a hardware-specific issue.
Contact Dejavoo Support at 877-358-6797, ext. 2.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: DvPay or DvStore/Market app is missing from the terminal
steps: Stax treats this as an issue for Dejavoo Support.
Contact Dejavoo Support at 877-358-6797, ext. 2.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Terminal will not power on even after charging
steps: Stax treats this as a hardware-specific issue.
Contact Dejavoo Support at 877-358-6797, ext. 2. They will say whether a new terminal is needed.
entries.note: Stax wrote this for 'your QD terminal' and names the QD2 and QD4 specifically.

entries.title: Register busy error (terminal integrated with a POS)
steps: The terminal is not on the "POS Online" screen, so the POS software cannot talk to it.
It can also mean the terminal is still processing a previous request.
entries.note: Stax's wording refers to its own Stax Pay software.

entries.title: Manually batch out
steps: On the terminal main page, select the Aura app.
Select the menu (3 horizontal lines).
Select Settlement.
Select Settle Daily Batch.

entries.title: Generate a custom report with Report Generator
steps: Open the DvPay (Aura) app.
Select Favourites (the star at the bottom centre of the screen), then Report.
Select Report Generator.
Choose the report type: Daily, Summary, Detailed Report or History Report.
Choose the payment type: All, Credit, Debit or EBT.
Choose the transaction type: All, Sale, Return, Void, Authorization, Ticket or Cash Advance.
Choose what to sort by: EDC, Transaction #, Transaction Type or Card Type.
Answer Yes or No when asked Save as Custom Report?
The report prints.

entries.title: Thermal paper size for the QD terminal
steps: Stax gives the paper dimensions as 2 1/4" x 50'.
Search for thermal paper in that size at your preferred retailer.

entries.title: Change the sleep-mode setting
steps: Go to the home screen and select Settings.
Tap the Menu icon (3 horizontal lines) at the top right.
Select Display, then Sleep.
Set it to your preference.

entries.title: Change the screen font size
steps: Go to the home screen and select Settings.
Select the Menu (3 horizontal lines).
Select Display, then Font Size.
Change it to the size you want.

entries.title: Turn silent mode on or off
steps: Press and hold the power button on the left-hand side of the terminal.
Select Silent mode.

entries.title: What is in the QD4 box
steps: Check the box contains: the QD4 terminal, a power adapter, a USB power cable, a connector box (used for Ethernet) and a connector box adaptor.

entries.title: Power on the terminal for the first time
steps: Connect the USB power cable to the power adaptor and plug it into an outlet.
On a QD2, plug the other end into the terminal.
Press and hold the power button on the left-hand side of the terminal.
Wait for the home screen.

entries.title: Connect to Wi-Fi
steps: From the home screen, tap the Settings icon in the top left-hand corner.
Select WLAN.
Tap your Wi-Fi network name.
If asked, enter the Wi-Fi password and press Connect.
The network should show CONNECTED.
If the terminal is integrated with another device, both must be on the same Wi-Fi network.
entries.note: Stax's tutorial is written around the QD4 and QD2.

entries.title: Connect to Ethernet with the base port
steps: Connect the provided base port to the QD terminal.
Connect the Ethernet cable to the base port.
Connect the other end of the Ethernet cord to your router or wired Ethernet outlet.

entries.title: Load receipt paper
steps: Paper loads at the top of the device.
Find the indents on the side of the machine and open the door.
Put the roll in with the top portion facing up.
Close the door with some paper hanging out.

entries.title: Receipts come out blank: test the paper and flip the roll
steps: On the home screen, select the Settings icon.
Tap the Self-Check icon.
Tap the Printer icon.
If the paper is in correctly the receipt prints with ink.
If it prints blank, flip the roll around and test again.

entries.title: Set the date, time and time zone
steps: On the home screen, select the Settings icon.
Select the three horizontal bars in the top right-hand corner.
Select Date and Time.
Recommended: keep automatic date, time and time zone turned on.
To set it by hand, turn off automatic date and time and automatic time zone, then use Set Date, Set Time and Time Zone.

entries.title: Run a sale from the Aura app
steps: Open the Aura app on the terminal's home screen.
Tap the screen and select Credit or Debit.
Select Sale.
Enter the sale amount.
Insert, swipe or tap the card.
If it goes through, the device says Approved and the receipt prints.

entries.title: Refund a card
steps: Open the Aura app.
Tap Credit or Debit, then Return.
Enter the refund amount and press OK.
Tap, insert or swipe the card, or enter the full card number by selecting the three horizontal bars icon.
The terminal flashes an approval and prints a receipt.
Refunds typically process within 3-5 business days depending on the customer's bank.

entries.title: Connect to Wi-Fi on a non-touch Z terminal
steps: From the main screen, select F1.
Select Comm Status.
Select Wi-fi.
Enter the Wi-Fi password when asked. Press 0 on the keypad for special characters if needed.
Press the green button to connect.
The IP address should show with no zero, and it will show connected.

entries.title: Connect to Wi-Fi on a touch-screen model
steps: From the home screen, tap the Settings icon in the top left-hand corner.
Select WLAN.
Select Scan Network.
Tap your Wi-Fi network name.
Select Configure.
If asked, enter the Wi-Fi password and press Connect.
If the terminal is integrated with another device, both must be on the same Wi-Fi network.

entries.title: Connect a non-touch Z terminal to Ethernet and test it
steps: Unplug the machine.
Connect one end of the Ethernet cable to the LAN port on the back and the other to your modem or router.
Power the machine on.
From the main credit/sale screen press F1, then Comm Status, then Ethernet. If it shows LAN Active, look for your network IP address.
Press F1, Comm Status, then the down arrow twice for Ping.
Press 2 on the keypad for Ping Google.
Ping Success means you are ready to process. Run a test sale.
Ping Fails means check your network: reset your router and try again, or contact support.

entries.title: Terminal shows Ping Fails
steps: Check your network configuration.
Reset your router and try the ping again.
If it still fails, contact support.
entries.note: The page says it applies to Z1, Z8, Z9, Z11 and the QD models.

entries.title: Connect a touch-screen model to Ethernet
steps: The device can be on or off.
Connect the provided base port to the terminal.
Connect the Ethernet cable to the base port.
Connect the other end to your router or wired Ethernet outlet.
entries.note: Stax says the page covers the Z1, Z8, Z9, Z11, QD1, QD2, QD3, QD4 and QD5; the base-port steps are worded for the QD terminal.

entries.title: Check the Wi-Fi connection with a ping (touch screen)
steps: Tap the Wi-Fi symbol on the terminal.
Tap Ping.
Press 2 to ping Google.
The terminal shows whether the ping succeeded or failed. A successful ping shows an IP address.

entries.title: Check the connection with a ping (non-touch Z8)
steps: Press F1.
Press F3.
Press 2 to ping Google.

entries.title: Connect a Dejavoo PIN pad to the terminal by USB
steps: Unplug the power from the terminal before connecting the PIN pad.
Connect the straight USB end to the PIN pad.
Connect the L-shaped end to USB port 1 on the terminal (upside down, cord over the top).
Plug the power back into the terminal.
The terminal shows "Press OK when PIN Pad displays Welcome". Wait for the PIN pad to show Welcome, then press OK on the terminal.
The PIN pad loads its parameters automatically. Setup is complete when both devices show their ready screens.
entries.note: Stax files this under Z Series Terminals and does not name the PIN pad model.

entries.title: Run the first sale through a connected PIN pad
steps: Enter the amount on the terminal's Credit Sale screen.
The terminal shows "waiting on PIN Pad".
The PIN pad shows "Tap, Insert, Swipe, and Enter Amount".
Process the card on the PIN pad.
The receipt prints when the sale succeeds.
entries.note: Stax files this under Z Series Terminals and does not name the PIN pad model.

entries.title: Connecting a QD5 PIN pad to a QD4 terminal
steps: Stax publishes this as a video only: it shows how to connect a QD4 terminal to a QD5 PIN pad. No written steps are given on the page.

entries.title: Run a debit sale on a Z-series terminal
steps: On the main screen, press the down arrow until debit is selected.
Press OK. The screen now says Debit Sale.
Enter the amount and press the green OK button.
Swipe the card and have the customer enter the PIN.
A receipt prints after the transaction is processed.

entries.title: Edit tip amounts by transaction number
steps: From the main screen press F3 for the favourites menu, or tap the star symbol on touch-screen models.
Select Edit All Trans# and press the green key.
Enter the transaction number from the original printed receipt.
Enter the tip amount. The base amount is shown too.
Press Yes with the green key to confirm.
Press the red X until you are back at the main screen, or go on to the next transaction number.

entries.title: Batched out without entering the tips
steps: Tips must be added by hand before you batch out for the day.
Tips cannot be adjusted after the batch has closed.
Contact your processor's support so the tip amounts can still be collected; Stax describes re-keying the sales from scanned receipts or creating a new sale for the tips.
entries.note: The recovery process and phone numbers on the page are Stax's own.

entries.title: Reset the Favorites menu to default on a Z8
steps: From the main screen, press F1 for the Service menu.
Select Core, then Utility, then Favorites.
Select Reset.
When asked Reset to Default, choose Yes.

entries.title: Print a report broken down by card type
steps: From the main screen press F1 and CORE (non-touch models), or tap the 3 lines at the bottom of the screen (touch models).
Select Applications, then CR/DB/EBT, then Report.
Select Report Generator, then Summary.
Select All for payment type and All for transaction type.
Sort by card type.
To save the report type press F2 (or Yes on a touch screen), name the report and press OK. To skip saving press F4 (or No).

entries.title: Set the date and time on a Z-series terminal
steps: From the main screen, select F1 or the three bars.
Select Utility, then Settings, then Date and Time.
If the date shown is right press the green OK key; otherwise type the date as MM/DD/YY.
If the time shown is right press the green OK key; otherwise type the 24-hour time as HH:MM:SS.
Press the red X until you are back at the main screen.

entries.title: Clock is an hour off after daylight saving time
steps: The machine does not update for daylight saving time automatically.
Set the time by hand: F1 or the three bars, Utility, Settings, Date and Time.
The date and time must be correct to avoid processing problems.

entries.title: CARD SWIPE ERROR
steps: It means the magstripe card reader is not functioning.
PaymentCloud's Z11 guide adds that the sale may need to be entered manually.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: COMM ERROR
steps: It means a communication error.
Check the network connection and run a ping test.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: QD # or RB # (rejected or failed batch)
steps: It means the batch was rejected or failed.
Settlement failures are often the result of a duplicate batch number; the guide gives steps to set a new batch number under Applications, Credit/Debit/EBT, Host Utility, Batch Features, Set Batch #.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Settlement Failed
steps: The settlement did not go through.
SETTLEMENT FAILED responses have a number of causes but are often the result of a duplicate batch.

Change the batch number: from the core menu select Applications, Credit/Debit/EBT, Host Utility, Batch Features, Set Batch #, clear the current number with the yellow backspace key, enter a new one and confirm with the green OK button.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Blank screen or freeze during "System Initializing"
steps: PaymentCloud reports that in 2019-2020 Dejavoo terminals froze with a blank screen during System Initializing, partly because of corrupt Linux software, and that Dejavoo has since worked with Castles Technology on it.
No merchant fix is given.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: PED TAMPERED or TAMPER DETECTED
steps: Do not try to fix it yourself.
Contact support. The terminal will likely need to be replaced.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: CARD SWIPE ERROR
steps: It means the magstripe reader is not functioning.
The sale may need to be entered manually.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: COMM ERROR
steps: It means a communication error.
Check your network connections.
If that fails, contact support.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's. The guide's phone number is 1-800-787-4105, which it calls Dejavoo Client Services.

entries.title: EMV OFFLINE ERROR
steps: It means the EMV chip is not communicating with the bank server.
The sale may need to be entered manually.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: SETTLEMENT FAILED, RETRY
steps: The settlement failed; the guide calls it self-explanatory.
Retry the settlement. The same guide's Batch Host Error steps set a new batch number under Applications, Host Utility, Batch Features, Set Batch #.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: TERMINAL ID ERROR
steps: The guide lists it as a standard error message and calls it self-explanatory; it gives no fix.
Contact support.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: PED TAMPERED or TAMPER DETECTED
steps: Do not try to fix it yourself.
Contact support. The terminal will likely need to be replaced.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Unplug Ethernet before power to avoid a TAMPER ERROR
steps: When power cycling, unplug the Ethernet cord before the power cord.
Doing it in the wrong order can make a TAMPER ERROR more likely.
If a TAMPER ERROR appears, contact support immediately.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Z11 clock does not update itself
steps: The Z11 date and time do not update automatically.
Adjust them regularly, especially after a daylight saving time change.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Sales that need a signature require signature capture to be enabled
steps: A sale that requires the cardholder to sign needs signature capture enabled.
Signature capture can be turned off at the file level, which is a change support makes.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Comm Error on a Z9: start with a ping test
steps: Press F1.
Go to Comm Status.
Press the Down Arrow twice or the Up Arrow once.
Tap OK on PING.
Tap Google.com, then OK.
If the ping fails there is an internet issue: restart the router or modem.
If the ping succeeds, check the terminal's date and time next.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Comm Error on a Z9 when the ping test succeeds
steps: Check the date and time on the terminal. A wrong date can cause a comm error.
If it is wrong, fix it and run a test transaction.
If the time is right and nothing else has worked, contact your internet service provider and verify that port 443 is open (whitelisted).
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Z9 and Ethernet
steps: PaymentCloud says the Z9 is not compatible with Ethernet connectivity.
The same guide describes downloading over Ethernet through the Z9 docking station.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Date and time prompt at power-on
steps: When the terminal is powered on it asks you to confirm the date and time.
Press F2 if it is correct, or F4 if it is wrong, and follow the prompts.
Time is always entered as a 24-hour clock. Date is MM DD YY and time is HH MM SS, both without spaces.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: COMM ERROR on a QD2
steps: It means there is a communication issue to fix.
Run a ping test to see whether the connection is stable.
Check the date and time: some Dejavoo terminals show COMM ERROR when the date and time are wrong.
To check the network without a ping: select Settings, then WLAN; or select Self Check, then Network, then WIFI or ETH.
After fixing it, run a test transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Factory reset on a QD2
steps: A factory reset erases all data on the device, including transaction history and customized settings.
Do not factory reset unless a member of the Dejavoo support team advises it.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Reboot a QD2
steps: Press and hold the power button on the side of the terminal.
After a few moments a menu appears with POWER OFF, REBOOT, SILENT MODE and other options.
Select REBOOT and wait.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Before powering on a QD2
steps: Make sure the device is connected by a power cable and the power source is working.
Make sure the device is sufficiently charged before powering it on.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: The Z6 has no printer
steps: The Z6 has no built-in receipt printer, so it cannot print or reprint receipts or reports and takes no paper.
Receipts and reports print from the terminal or point-of-sale printer it is connected to.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: The Z6 does not connect to Wi-Fi
steps: PaymentCloud says the Z6 cannot connect to Wi-Fi; it uses Ethernet.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Z6 operating modes: DISPATCH and SIMPLE PIN PAD
steps: The Z6 has two operating modes, DISPATCH and SIMPLE PIN PAD.
In one it works as a straightforward PIN pad terminal; in the other it is a secure card reader that gets authorization through other Dejavoo terminals.
Which mode is set is part of the terminal's configuration.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Connecting a Z6 to a Z8
steps: PaymentCloud says a POS cable connects the Z6 to the Z8 so the pin pad works with the Z8.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's. Our sheet says the Z3/Z6-to-Z8/Z11 adapter cable is needed and is ordered separately.

entries.title: Reboot a Z6
steps: First option: press the power button; a menu appears with POWER OFF, REBOOT, AIRPLANE MODE and SILENT MODE. Select REBOOT.
Second option: press and hold the power button until the screen flashes.
Start with the first option and use the second as the alternative.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's. The guide describes a Z6 touchscreen; our sheet calls the Z6 a non-touch unit.

entries.title: The QD3 has no printer
steps: The QD3 has no built-in printer, so receipts cannot be printed or reprinted on it.
Receipts can be sent by text or email from the Dejavoo app, or printed from a separate main terminal.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: QD3 and Ethernet
steps: PaymentCloud says the QD3 is not compatible with Ethernet connectivity.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's. Xplor Pay's QD page lists the QD3 PIN pad with Ethernet, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, so the two processor sources disagree.

entries.title: Where the QD3 can be used
steps: PaymentCloud says the QD3 is a portable pin pad that can be used anywhere with Wi-Fi, 4G or Bluetooth connectivity.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Factory reset on a QD3: do not do it on your own
steps: A factory reset wipes all data from the device, including customized settings and transaction history.
Dejavoo does not recommend users perform it on their own, because it completely erases the device's Market application and there is a considerable margin for error.
Contact support instead.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Factory reset on a QD4: do not do it on your own
steps: A factory reset wipes all data from the device, including customized settings and transaction history.
Dejavoo does not recommend users perform it on their own, because it completely erases the device's Market application and there is a considerable margin for error.
Contact support instead.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Factory reset on a QD5: do not do it on your own
steps: A factory reset wipes all data from the device, including customized settings and transaction history.
Dejavoo does not recommend users perform it on their own, because it completely erases the device's Market application and there is a considerable margin for error.
Contact support instead.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: PaymentCloud says the QD5 has a built-in receipt printer
steps: PaymentCloud's QD5 guide states that the receipt printer is built into the terminal and gives paper-loading steps for 2" x 50' thermal paper.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's. This conflicts with our sheet and with Dejavoo, which list the QD5 as a PIN pad. Treat with caution.

entries.title: Debit card returns may ask for the original date and time
steps: For a debit card return, the terminal may ask for the date and time of the original transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: QD4 connection options
steps: PaymentCloud lists the QD4's connection options as Ethernet, USB to Ethernet, or Wi-Fi.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Wi-Fi password advice for the Z line
steps: Merchants are discouraged from using special characters in their network password.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Ask for a call back with the Call Me feature
steps: From the main menu, press the F4 key or tap the CALL ME icon.
The terminal sends the request to technical support.
A technician from Dejavoo or your service provider calls the phone number linked to your account.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: No Paper Mode
steps: Setting the print options to 0 lets some Dejavoo models run in No Paper Mode.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide (V.122024), not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: No number shows after TPN: during a download
steps: Do not type one in.
Call technical support; Dejavoo gives 1 (877) 358-6797.

entries.title: Wi-Fi network requirements for Z-line terminals
steps: The Wi-Fi network must support WPA2 security.
The router must support 2.4 GHz.
The Wi-Fi network name must not contain special characters such as * - @ # !

entries.title: Z-line terminal will not join the Wi-Fi network
steps: Check the network uses WPA2 security.
Check the router offers 2.4 GHz.
Check the network name has no special characters (* - @ # ! and similar); rename the network if it does.
Then set Wi-Fi up again from Core Menu, Utility, Communications, Local Parms, WiFi.

entries.title: Always close the batch before a download
steps: Always close any open batch before downloading a device.
FULL download updates the application software. PARTIAL download updates parameters only.

entries.title: What the terminal does after a download
steps: The terminal downloads and installs the software and reboots.
It asks you to confirm the date and time, in 24-hour clock format.
Back at the idle prompt it automatically communicates to process a Key Exchange.

entries.title: Typing the TPN: pause between repeated digits
steps: The TPN is a 10-12 character alphanumeric number.
When typing the same digit twice in a row, pause between presses so the key does not scroll to letters.

entries.title: Downloading over GPRS uses SIM data
steps: A download over GPRS uses SIM data.
Dejavoo recommends a USB download or a download through the docking station instead.
A GPRS download also needs the SIM APN set in the terminal and in the terminal's STEAM profile, which support sets up.

entries.title: Install software from a USB key
steps: The .TAR software file goes on the USB key in a folder named download (no spaces) on the root directory. It does not need to be uncompressed.
Find the Mini B male USB to female A USB adaptor in the terminal packaging.
Turn the terminal over and plug the smaller end into the Mini USB 1 port on the underside.
Turn the terminal right side up and make sure it is powered on.
Insert the USB key into the larger end of the adaptor. The terminal reads the USB directory.
The TPN file from the download folder appears on the display; select it and apply updates.
The terminal installs, reboots and asks you to confirm the date and time.

entries.title: Z9 docking station gives Ethernet and dial connections
steps: The Z9 docking station gives the Z9 an Ethernet (IP) and a modem (dial) connection.
Connect the cable to the matching port: CAT5 cable into the LAN port, or phone cable into the LINE port.
Place the Z9 on the docking station.

entries.title: Insert the SIM chip into a Z9 4G terminal
steps: Remove the large SIM chip from the SIM card, keeping the small chip intact inside it as the sheet shows. If the chip is removed wrongly it will not fit and a replacement card must be bought.
With the gold contact facing down and the bevelled edge outward, insert the chip into SIM slot #1, following the diagram on the back of the terminal.
Push the chip in as far as it will go.
SIM slot #1 is the default and should be used unless you are told otherwise.

entries.title: SIM chip will not fit in the terminal
steps: The chip has to be removed from the SIM card properly or it will not fit.
If it was removed wrongly, a replacement card needs to be purchased.

entries.title: Activate a SIM subscription in the Dejavoo My Account portal
steps: Log in to the Dejavoo My Account portal.
In My Services and Equipment, click the arrow under the name of your subscription plan.
Enter the ICCID (SIM card number) and the IMEI number.
Click the ACTIVATE button.
entries.note: Whether the merchant or the processor holds this account depends on who bought the SIM.

entries.title: A SIM card can be suspended and reactivated with no fee
steps: In the My Account portal the SIM card can be deactivated, suspended or reactivated at any time with no fee.
To deactivate it, click the SUSPEND button.

entries.title: SIM plan must match the SIM's carrier
steps: An AT&T SIM card needs an AT&T monthly plan.
A Verizon SIM card needs a Verizon monthly plan.
The terminal's profile must also carry the matching carrier and APN, which support sets.

entries.title: Find the terminal's IMEI number
steps: The IMEI number is on the back of the Dejavoo terminal.
It can also be printed from the terminal's system menu, which uses a system password; ask support to walk you through that.

entries.title: Store and Forward (offline mode): how it works and the risk
steps: Store and Forward takes transactions offline. There is no authorization at the point of sale.
Authorization happens at batch time, when communication is available.
Take a manual card imprint of each offline transaction in case it later fails (the card is declined), so it can be re-entered.

entries.title: Batch will not close after Store and Forward transactions
steps: All failed (declined) Store and Forward transactions have to be deleted from the batch before the batch can close.
Get support's help identifying and deleting them.

entries.title: Store and Forward mode settings
steps: The mode can be set to ON, OFF, or ON only when no other communication is available (for example outside GPRS coverage).

entries.title: On-screen help key
steps: At any time during a transaction or in any menu, press the "•" key at the bottom right of the keypad.
The screen explains the feature and gives the next step.
Press the green OK key or the red X key to go back.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Call Me must be an active service
steps: Call Me asks a technical support representative to call you.
It only works if the service has been made active in your terminal beforehand.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Debit cards cannot be keyed in by hand
steps: A debit card cannot be manually entered; it must be read at the terminal.
You must be set up to accept debit and have a PIN-encrypted keypad on the terminal or a PIN-encrypted external PIN pad.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: A debit sale cannot be voided
steps: A debit card sale cannot be voided.
To refund a debit sale, process a RETURN to the debit card.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: When a void works
steps: A void only cancels a transaction that is still in the current batch.
The void amount must be exactly the same as the original transaction amount.
Sales, returns and ticket-only transactions can be voided.
Whether a debit transaction can be voided depends on the host; check with your processor.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Authorization Only is not a sale
steps: An Auth Only verifies funds and gets an approval code. It does not charge the card; it places a hold for the amount.
To actually charge the account, run a Ticket Only sale later with that approval code.
Only a merchant copy of the receipt prints for an authorization.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Ticket Only sale
steps: A Ticket Only sale is used when an authorization number has already been obtained.
The authorization code on the receipt is the number obtained earlier.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: A presale ticket is not a sale
steps: The presale ticket prints with the sale amount so the customer can write in a tip.
It is not a sale: a sale transaction still has to be run with the cardholder's card afterwards.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Retail tips cannot be added later
steps: For retail-with-tip transactions the sale amount and the tip are authorized together as one amount in the original sale.
Retail tips cannot be added at a later time, unlike a restaurant tip adjustment.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: EBT food benefit sales cannot be voided
steps: A void is not allowed for EBT Food Benefit transactions.
Process a return instead.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Date and time prompt at power-on
steps: When the terminal powers on it asks you to confirm the date and time.
Press F2 if correct, or F4 if not, then follow the prompts.
Time is always 24-hour format. Date is MM DD YY and time is HH MM SS, entered without spaces.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Forgot the customized password
steps: Use Retrieve Password on the Core Menu.
It asks the security question that was chosen (one of 3) when the password was changed.
If the question cannot be answered, contact support.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Password-protect menu items and transaction types
steps: The security menu can password-protect menu items or transaction types so employees do not have general access.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: If automatic batch is turned off
steps: Automatic batch can settle at a set time, or be turned off completely.
If it is turned off, the merchant has to batch manually.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Delete Open Batch is permanent
steps: Delete Open Batch deletes the current open batch and every open transaction in it.
It is permanent and not reversible. Those transactions will not be sent for settlement.
Only do it with your technical support help desk on the line; the terminal flashes a warning saying the same.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Screen blinks TRAINING MODE
steps: Training Mode is on. Everything done in Training Mode is fictitious and not real.
Receipts and reports print with a training mode reminder at the bottom.
Turn Training Mode OFF to process live transactions.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Print options and No Paper Mode
steps: Print Options sets how many receipts and reports print per request.
Setting print options to 0 makes the terminal run in No Paper Mode.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Detailed Report can use a lot of paper
steps: The Detailed Report prints a full receipt for each transaction in the current batch.
With many transactions it is lengthy; check the paper supply first.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Check with your processor before changing AVS settings
steps: AVS and card code prompts during a keyed sale depend on the terminal's settings.
Check with your merchant bank before changing AVS settings.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: Reading the card is best practice over keying it
steps: It is always best practice to run the card through the terminal's reader rather than typing the number.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's all-models manual V525.15, written for the V and Z series before the Aura software; menu wording on an Aura terminal can differ.

entries.title: What the CREDIT icon opens
steps: Press the CREDIT icon on the terminal home screen.
A screen appears with SALE, RETURN, VOID, AUTH, TICKET and BALANCE.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's Aura manual for Android terminals, Transactions section (March 2022).

entries.title: Debit cards cannot be keyed in by hand
steps: A debit card cannot be manually entered.
You must be set up to accept debit and have a PIN-encrypted keypad on the terminal or a PIN-encrypted external PIN pad.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's Aura manual for Android terminals, Transactions section (March 2022).

entries.title: A debit sale cannot be voided
steps: A debit card sale cannot be voided.
To refund a debit sale, process a RETURN to the debit card.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's Aura manual for Android terminals, Transactions section (March 2022).

entries.title: Retail tips cannot be added later
steps: Retail tips cannot be added at a later time; the tip is authorized with the sale.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's Aura manual for Android terminals, Transactions section (March 2022).

entries.title: A presale ticket is not a sale
steps: A presale ticket is not a sale.
A sale transaction still has to be completed afterwards.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's Aura manual for Android terminals, Transactions section (March 2022).

entries.title: Authorization Only is not a sale
steps: An Authorization Only verifies funds and gets an approval code; it is not a sale.
The amount is held against the cardholder's available credit until a sale is completed.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's Aura manual for Android terminals, Transactions section (March 2022).

entries.title: A void must match the original amount
steps: The void amount must be exactly the same as the original transaction amount.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's Aura manual for Android terminals, Transactions section (March 2022).

entries.title: EBT food benefit sales cannot be voided
steps: A void is not allowed for EBT Food Benefit transactions.
Process a return instead.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's Aura manual for Android terminals, Transactions section (March 2022).

entries.title: Keyed sale: card present or not present
steps: On a manually entered sale the terminal asks whether the card is present: press YES or NO.
If the card is not present, follow the prompts for AVS and card code security information.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's Aura manual for Android terminals, Transactions section (March 2022).

entries.title: Where the card security code is
steps: The code is three digits on the back of a Mastercard or Visa.
On American Express it is found above the card number.
entries.note: From Dejavoo's Aura manual for Android terminals, Transactions section (March 2022).

entries.title: Turn a Z9 on and off
steps: To turn on, press the POWER key.
To turn off, tap the STAR icon for the FAVORITES menu, then tap POWER OFF.
entries.note: From Xplor Pay's copy of the Dejavoo Z9/Z11 and Z8 quick reference guides. Dejavoo's own Z9/Z11 guide says to reach Power Off from the Services menu.

entries.title: What the Wi-Fi icon tells you
steps: The Wi-Fi icon blinks when the terminal is not connected.
It stays still when the terminal is connected.
entries.note: From Xplor Pay's copy of the Dejavoo Z9/Z11 and Z8 quick reference guides.

entries.title: Changing payment type and transaction type on a Z8
steps: The idle screen shows CREDIT and SALE and a prompt for the SERVICES menu (F1).
To change payment type, use the down arrow key.
To change transaction type, press the YELLOW BACK key until the type you want appears.
entries.note: From Xplor Pay's copy of the Dejavoo Z9/Z11 and Z8 quick reference guides.

entries.title: How Xplor Pay describes the QD models
steps: QD4: desktop Android, Ethernet and Wi-Fi, internal PIN pad and contactless, supports an external QD3 PIN pad.
QD2: mobile wireless Android, 4G and Wi-Fi, battery powered, internal PIN pad and contactless.
QD3: integrated standalone Android, Wi-Fi, internal PIN pad and contactless.
QD3 PinPad: compact Android PIN pad with Ethernet, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, used with the QD4 desktop.
entries.note: Xplor lists both a standalone QD3 and a QD3 PIN pad; our sheet treats the QD3 as a PIN pad.

entries.title: The QD3 PIN pad is used with the QD4
steps: Xplor Pay lists the QD3 PinPad as a compact Android PIN pad with Ethernet, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, used with the QD4 desktop terminal.
entries.note: Our sheet pairs the QD5 with the QD4 and calls the QD3 the flexible pad; this source pairs the QD3 pad with the QD4.

entries.title: DvPay / Aura app is corrupted or obsolete
steps: This is a technician procedure: it uses an administrator login in the Android settings to uninstall DVPAY/AURA, clear the Market app's data, let Market update, reinstall DvPay and then run a full download of the terminal's TPN.
Contact support to have it done.
entries.note: From PayCompass's internal support notes: a technician procedure, not a merchant one.

entries.title: PIN pad shows MISSING CL CONFIG File
steps: Run the PIN pad update from the terminal it is attached to.
Press the F1 key on a Z8, or the 3-line key on a Z11 or QD4.
Select Applications, then Credit/Debit, then Setup, then PinPad, then Update.
entries.note: From PayCompass's support notes, titled for Z8/Z11/QD4 with a PIN pad. Our Z6 sheet describes the same fix for a pad whose tap stopped working.

entries.title: QD3 PIN pad uses an AndroidPP TPN
steps: The QD3 PIN pad is loaded with a TPN of the form AndroidPP plus the terminal software version, for example AndroidPP143.
entries.note: From PayCompass's internal support notes: a technician procedure, not a merchant one.

entries.title: Technician setup sequence for a QD-line terminal
steps: Connect to Wi-Fi: Settings, Wifi, Scan Network, choose the network, Configure, Set Password, Connect.
Set the date and time: Settings, the 3 lines in the top right corner, Date and Time.
Open Market and choose DvPay (AURA) or DvPayLite, whichever the file calls for. Do not press the big red update button.
Press the 3 lines to go to settings and enter the TPN. Make sure keys load during the TPN download, then apply updates.
Run a $0.50 test sale, void it, then press the star and Settle Daily Batch.
entries.note: From PayCompass's internal support notes: a technician procedure, not a merchant one.

entries.title: Pull a partial download on a Z8 after a change to the file
steps: Press the F1 key.
Press the down arrow to highlight Core Menu and select it.
Go to Utility, then Software Download, then Connect.
Select the communications option, then Partial.
Press OK on the Enter TPN screen.
entries.note: From PayCompass's support notes.

entries.title: QD series is not supported on First Data North
steps: PayCompass's notes say the QD series cannot be used on the First Data North platform; the Z and P series can.
entries.note: From PayCompass's support notes; applies to that processor's platforms.

entries.title: Debit (PIN) keys need loading: remote key injection (RKL)
steps: Loading encryption keys remotely (RKL) has to be set up by Dejavoo first: Dejavoo sets up the RKL request in its system and invoices for it, from the terminal's serial number and the encryption key.
The injection itself is a technician procedure run from Core Menu, Applications, then the security menus, with logins that Dejavoo emails to the reseller.
Contact support to arrange it.
entries.note: Dejavoo's RKL page is written for resellers, not merchants.

entries.title: Certificate Already exists (during key injection)
steps: This shows during remote key injection when the terminal already has its certificate.
The technician can skip ahead to the Download Debit Keys step.

entries.title: Messages shown when remote key injection works
steps: "Terminal Signing: Loaded" shows after the terminal has created its certificate.
"Key Loading Succeeded" shows when the debit keys have loaded.

entries.title: Manually Entered Sale (QD Terminal Line, EMV Retail)
steps: From the idle screen, tap on the Credit icon.
Tap on the Sale icon.
Input the Sale Amount and press Ok.
Tap on the credit card icon on the Credit Sale screen. (Insert, Swipe or Enter Card #.)
Manually input Card #.
Follow the CNP prompts (input exp. Date, zip code etc). Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
The transaction is processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.

entries.title: Chip Credit Sale (QD Terminal Line, EMV Retail)
steps: From the idle screen, tap on the Credit icon.
Tap on the Sale icon.
Input the Sale Amount and press Ok.
Tap (contactless only) or insert chip card.
The transaction is processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.

entries.title: Debit Sale (QD Terminal Line, EMV Retail)
steps: From the idle screen, tap on the Debit icon.
Tap on the Sale icon.
Input the Sale Amount and press Ok.
Tap (contactless only) or insert chip card.
Customer enters PIN on encrypted terminal PIN pad or encrypted external PIN pad and presses Ok.
The transaction is processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.

entries.title: Terminal Power Off/Reboot (QD Terminal Line, EMV Retail)
steps: Press the button on the side of the terminal and hold until a menu appears on the screen, with the following options: Power Off, Reboot, Airplane Mode and Silent Mode.
Select the option you desire by tapping on the screen.
entries.note: Where a step says 'the icon' or 'the key', the printed guide shows a picture; Xplor Pay's text copy of these guides names them (star = Favorites, three lines = Core/Services menu, phone = Call Me, yellow back key to change transaction type on a Z8). Dejavoo prints the same steps in its guides for: EMV Restaurant; EMV Retail with Dual Pricing; EMV Restaurant with Dual Pricing; EMV Retail with True Cash Discount; EMV Restaurant with True Cash Discount.

entries.title: Manually Entered Sale (QD Terminal Line, EMV Restaurant)
steps: Tap on the Credit icon.
Tap on the Sale icon.
Enter the Server ID # and press Ok. Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
Enter the Sale Amount and press Ok.
If configured, terminal will prompt to Select or Enter Tip amount.
Tap on the credit card icon on the Credit Sale screen. (Insert, Swipe or Enter Card #)
Manually enter Card #.
Follow the CNP prompts (enter exp. date, zip code, etc). Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
The transaction is processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.

entries.title: Credit Card Sale (QD Terminal Line, EMV Restaurant)
steps: Tap on the Credit icon.
Tap on the Sale icon.
Enter Server ID# and press Ok. Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
Enter the Sale Amount and press Ok.
If configured, terminal will prompt to Select or Enter Tip amount.
Tap (contactless only) or insert chip card.
The transaction is processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.

entries.title: Debit Sale (QD Terminal Line, EMV Restaurant)
steps: Tap on the Debit icon.
Tap on the Sale icon.
Enter the Server ID# and press ok. Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
Enter the Sale Amount and press Ok.
If configured, terminal will prompt to Select or Enter Tip amount.
Tap (contactless only) or insert chip card.
Customer enters PIN on terminal or PIN pad and presses Ok.
The transaction is processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.

entries.title: Manually Entered Sale (QD Terminal Line, EMV Retail with Dual Pricing)
steps: Enter the Sale Amount and press Ok.
The default transaction will be Sale.
Choose the payment type the customer will use. Options are Card (credit/debit), EBT Food, EBT Cash and Cash.
Tap on the credit card icon on the Credit Sale screen. (Insert, Swipe or Enter Card #)
Manually enter Card #.
Follow the CNP prompts (enter exp. date, zip code, etc).Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
Transaction will be processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.
entries.note: Dejavoo prints the same steps in its guides for: EMV Retail with True Cash Discount.

entries.title: Credit Card Sale (QD Terminal Line, EMV Retail with Dual Pricing)
steps: Enter the Sale Amount and press Ok.
The default transaction will be Sale.
Choose the payment type the customer will use. Options are Card and PIN Debit.
When prompted, tap or insert the card. If required (debit), enter PIN number.
Transaction will be processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.
entries.note: Dejavoo prints the same steps in its guides for: EMV Retail with True Cash Discount.

entries.title: Manually Entered Sale (QD Terminal Line, EMV Restaurant with Dual Pricing)
steps: Enter the Sale Amount and press Ok.
The default transaction will be Sale.
Choose the payment type the customer will use. Options are Card (credit/debit) and Cash.
Enter Server # and press Ok. Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
If configured, terminal will prompt to Select or Enter Tip amount.
Tap on the credit card icon on the Credit Sale screen. (Insert, Swipe or Enter Card #)
Manually enter Card #.
Follow the CNP prompts (enter exp. date, zip code, etc). Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
The transaction will be processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.

entries.title: Credit Card Sale (QD Terminal Line, EMV Restaurant with Dual Pricing)
steps: Enter the Sale Amount and press Ok.
The default transaction will be Sale.
Enter Server # and press Ok. Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
Choose the payment type the customer will use. Options are Card and PIN Debit.
If configured, terminal will prompt to Select or Enter Tip amount.
If prompted, confirm the sale amount by tapping Ok or No. Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
When prompted, tap or insert the card. If required (debit), enter PIN number.
The transaction will be processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.

entries.title: Manually Entered Sale (QD Terminal Line, EMV Restaurant with True Cash Discount)
steps: Enter the Sale Amount and press Ok.
The default transaction will be Sale.
Choose the payment type the customer will use. Options are Card (credit/debit) and Cash.
Enter Server # and press Ok. Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
If configured, terminal will prompt to Select or Enter Tip amount.
Tap on the credit card icon on the Credit Sale screen. (Insert, Swipe or Enter Card #)
Manually enter Card #.
Follow the CNP prompts (enter exp. date, zip code, etc). Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
Transaction will be processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.

entries.title: Credit Card Sale (QD Terminal Line, EMV Restaurant with True Cash Discount)
steps: Enter the Sale Amount and press Ok.
The default transaction will be Sale.
Choose the payment type the customer will use. Options are Card and PIN Debit.
Enter Server # and press Ok. Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
If configured, terminal will prompt to Select or Enter Tip amount.
When prompted, tap or insert the card. If required (debit), enter PIN number.
Transaction will be processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.

entries.title: Manually Entered Credit Sale (Non-touch screen Z8, EMV Retail)
steps: Enter the Sale Amount and press Ok.
Prompt to insert card appears, press Ok.
Manually enter Card #.
Follow the CNP prompts (input exp. date, ZIP code etc). Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
The transaction is processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.

entries.title: Credit Card Sale (Non-touch screen Z8, EMV Retail)
steps: Enter the Sale Amount and press Ok.
Tap (contactless only) or insert chip card.
If prompted, confirm the Sale Amount by pressing F2 (YES) or F4 (CANCEL). Conditional on the terminal’s configuration.
The transaction is processed. Sales receipt will print with details of the transaction.

entries.title: Debit Sale (Non-touch screen Z8, EMV Retail)
