Enter the RETURN AMOUNT and press OK to confirm.
Return the amount by pressing F2 (YES) or F4 (CANCEL).
Enter the manager password when prompted.
Tap, insert, swipe, or manually enter card number.
The transaction is processed. Return receipts will print with details of the transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Void Sale: Void Credit Transaction (Card Present)
steps: Press the key on the terminal home screen until VOID appears.
Enter VOID AMOUNT and press OK to confirm.
Select the VOID AMOUNT by pressing F2 (YES) or F4 (CANCEL).
Enter the manager password when prompted.
Processes the credit card.
Confirm the VOID AMOUNT by pressing F2 (YES) or F4 (NO).
After the transaction is processed, the voided receipts will print.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Void Sale: Void Credit Transaction (Card Not Present)
steps: At the main menu, press F1 to access the SERVICES MENU.
Use the arrow keys to highlight FAVORITES and click OK.
Use the arrow keys to highlight VOID CR/DB TRANS and press OK.
Use the arrow keys to select BY TRANSACTION NUMBER and press OK.
Enter the TRANSACTION NUMBER to be voided and press OK.
Approve the VOID AMOUNT by PRESSING F2 (YES) or F4 (NO).
Enter the manager password when prompted.
The void is processed. Void receipts will print with details of the transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Change Batch Time
steps: Press the green key to be directed to the core menu.
Select SETTLEMENT.
Enter default manager password if prompted.
If prompted, select BATCH SETTINGS.
Use the keypad to adjust time details as needed in military time format.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Change Batch Number
steps: From the core menu, select APPLICATIONS.
Select CREDIT/DEBIT/EBT.
Select HOST UTILITY.
Select BATCH FEATURES.
Select SET BATCH #.

Use the keypad to either clear the current batch number or enter a new one. Clearing the batch number can be done using the yellow backspace key, while entering a new one requires use of the green OK button.
Confirm when ready.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Settle the Daily Batch Report
steps: Starting at the main menu, press F1 to access the SERVICES menu.
Use the arrow keys to highlight SETTLEMENT and press OK to confirm.
With the arrow keys, highlight SETTLE DAILY BATCH and press OK to confirm.
Enter the manager password when prompted.
Establish the terminal’s communication with the host.
Settlement Receipt Report prints.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Manually Settle the Daily Batch Report
steps: On the main menu, there are two primary options: CREDIT and SALE.
Press the green key to be directed to the core menu.
Select SETTLEMENT.
Select SETTLE DAILY BATCH.
When prompted, enter the manager password, then press the green key to confirm. Your terminal will then display this information to the host.
If necessary, adjust tips before continuing. If there are no tips to settle and no errors to correct, press F2.
After processing, a receipt will then be printed with details of the settlement report.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Reprint Settlement Receipt
steps: Press F1.
Select FAVORITES.
Select REPRINT RECEIPT.
You will be presented with a series of options for organizing receipts: BY TRANSACTION #, BY CARD NUMBER, or for the last settlement or transaction (LAST).
Select the relevant option and proceed.
You will be asked if you wish to reprint a MERCHANT COPY or a CUSTOMER COPY. Select the relevant option and proceed.
The settlement receipt will then be reprinted.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Change Detail Batch Report to Summary
steps: Press F1.
Select APPLICATION.
Select DEBIT/CREDIT, then REPORT.
Enter the manager password when prompted.
Select REPORT GENERATOR, then SUMMARY.
Select ALL twice.
Select EDC, then YES to confirm.
Select ENTER, then SAVE AS DEFAULT.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Clear Batch
steps: From the home screen, select APPLICATIONS.
Select the relevant option for which batch you wish to clear: CREDIT, DEBIT, or EBT.
Select HOST UTILITY. Enter default password if prompted.
Select BATCH FEATURES.
Select DELETE OPEN BATCH, then confirm to delete. Merchants may be asked to confirm this process twice.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. Deleting an open batch is permanent; Dejavoo's manual says to do it only with the help desk.

entries.title: Change the Date and Time
steps: Access the core menu from the device’s main menu.
Locate the UTILITY option.
Enter the manager password when prompted.
Select the SETTINGS option.
Next, choose DATE AND TIME.
If the date is correct, click OK. If not, use the yellow backspace key to clear it, then enter the correct date in MM/DD/YY format. Time should be entered in 24-hour military format.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Turn the Beep Off on your Dejavoo Z8
steps: Press OK to access the core menu.
Select UTILITY.
Select SETTINGS.
Select KEYBOARD.
Select YES or NO to turn the beep on or off.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Adjust Tips
steps: Select F3 to access the FAVORITES menu.
Scroll down and select EDIT TIP.
You will see a menu with two options: UNTIPPED and ADJUST TIPPED.
If you want to adjust an existing tip, select ADJUST TIPPED.
You will then be directed to an ADD TIP BY menu with three primary options: SERVER ID, TRANSACTION #, and LAST 4 DIGITS.
Select the relevant option. If you selected TRANSACTION #, enter transaction number.
Edit tip as needed and then CONFIRM ADJ. TIP.
Press F2 to confirm.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Print Reports
steps: From the main menu, press F1 to access the SERVICES menu.
Use the arrow keys to highlight REPORTS and click OK.
Use the arrow keys to highlight your report type (DAILY REPORTS, HISTORY REPORTS, SUMMARY REPORTS, etc.) and click OK.
Enter the manager password when prompted.
REPORT prints.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Download Terminal Software: Download via USB
steps: Plug the USB key into a laptop or desktop.
Locate the USB key on your drive list.
Access it via the USB drive.
Add a new folder on your USB directory titled DOWNLOAD (no spaces).
Place the downloaded Terminal Profile File into the DOWNLOAD folder.
Locate the Mini B Male USB and link to Female A USB adapter.
Link the Male USB with the Mini USB 1 port located on the back of the terminal.
Confirm device is powered on.
Flip your Dejavoo Z8 right-side up.
Remove the USB key from your laptop or desktop.
Plug the USB key into the Female A adapter.
Terminal will read “READING USB DIRECTORY.”
Press and hold the green button to select the TPN on their Dejavoo display, then press F2 to confirm and apply updates.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Download Terminal Software: Partial Download
steps: Start by ensuring all open batches have been settled.
Access the core menu.
Select UTILITY. Enter default password when prompted.
Select SOFTWARE DOWNLOAD, then CONNECT.
Select ETHERNET.
Select PARTIAL.
You will be presented with a TPN number. If the number is correct, press the green OK to confirm.
When presented with the option to APPLY UPDATES, select YES to confirm.
Your terminal may reboot upon downloading and installing new software.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Retrieve Information From a USB Drive
steps: Insert the USB drive, find it in your list of drives, and select it.
In the main directory of your USB drive, create a new folder and name it “Download.”
If you haven’t done so yet, download the Terminal Profile from the STEAM system. Save the Terminal Profile (TPN) in the “Download” folder on the USB drive’s main directory.
Find the Mini B USB to A USB adapter in the packaging for your Z series terminal.
Flip the device over, then connect the Mini B USB end to the Mini A USB 1 port on the bottom of the terminal.
Set the terminal upright, and make sure it is powered on before continuing.
Remove the USB drive from your computer and connect it to the A end of the adapter. The device will then show “Reading USB Directory.”
When the TPN file from the Download folder appears on the terminal display, tap TPN on the screen.
The terminal will ask if there are any updates. Click YES to confirm.
The terminal will begin downloading the software, restart, and prompt you to confirm the date and time.
After the terminal returns to the main screen, it will automatically start a key exchange.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Do a Factory Reset
steps: Start by accessing the MENU on your Z8, i.e. the three horizontal bars on the bottom half of your screen.
Select UTILITY.
Select SOFTWARE DOWNLOAD.
Select DELETE APPS.
Manually select the apps you wish to delete.
At this point, the terminal will start to reboot.
If necessary, repeat steps 1-7.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. The guide warns a factory reset erases all data, including transaction history and settings.

entries.title: Reboot Your Dejavoo Z8
steps: Press and hold down the power button until your screen begins to flash.
You may see a display that reads SYSTEM INITIALIZING.
Terminal will begin a reboot/reset.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Load a paper roll in the printer
steps: At the top of the terminal, locate the black tab and pull it towards you.
The paper cover will pop open.
Place the thermal paper into the holder.
The paper roll size merchants should use is 2” x 50”.
Close the top of the case by snapping it into place.
The paper should feed from the terminal screen.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Turn On/Off: Turn On
steps: Press the POWER button to turn on the terminal.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Turn On/Off: Turn Off
steps: Press the STAR key to access the FAVORITES menu.
Press POWER OFF to turn off.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Set Up an Ethernet or Wifi Connection: Connect to WiFi
steps: From the main menu, press the Green Button to access the Core Menu.
Press 4 for UTILITY.
Press 3 for “Communications.”
Press 2 for “Local Params.”
Press 3 for “WiFi.”
Press 1 for “Scan Network.”
Tap on the network from the list to which you’d like to connect.
Press 2 for “Configure.”
Press 1 for “Set Password.”
Use the keypad to input the network’s password. Click the Green Key when complete.
Press the yellow back button and select “Connect.”
Press F2 to confirm the network connection.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Do a Full Download or Partial Download: Via Modem
steps: Press the Green Key to access the Core Menu from the idle prompt.
Tap UTILITY.
Tap SOFTWARE DOWNLOAD.
Tap DIAL PPP communication method.
Tap either FULL or PARTIAL.
Enter the unique 10-12 digit alphanumeric TPN.
Press the Green Key (Note: When inputting a repeated digit, pause between entries to avoid scrolling to letters as this entry is alphanumerically capable.)
Terminal will ask, “Apply Updates?” Tap YES.
The terminal will download and install your software, reboot, and prompt you to confirm the date and time, then return to the idle prompt.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Do a Full Download or Partial Download: Via Ethernet
steps: From the idle prompt, press the Green Key to access the Core Menu.
Tap UTILITY.
Tap SOFTWARE DOWNLOAD.
Tap ETHERNET communication method.
Tap either FULL or PARTIAL.
Enter the unique 10-12 digit alphanumeric TPN.
Press the Green Key (Note: When inputting a repeated digit, pause between entries to avoid scrolling to letters as this entry is alphanumerically capable.)
Terminal will ask, “Apply Updates?” Tap YES.
The terminal will download and install your software, reboot, and prompt you to confirm the date and time, then return to the idle prompt.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Do a Full Download or Partial Download: Via GPRS
steps: Tap UTILITY
Tap SOFTWARE DOWNLOAD
Tap GPRS communication method
Tap either FULL or PARTIAL
Enter the unique 10-12 digit alphanumeric TPN
Press the Green Key (Note: When inputting a repeated digit, pause between entries to avoid scrolling to letters as this entry is alphanumerically capable.)
Terminal will ask, “Apply Updates?” Tap YES
The terminal will download and install your software, reboot, and prompt you to confirm the date and time, then return to the idle prompt.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Do a Full Download or Partial Download: Via WiFi
steps: From the idle prompt, press the Green Key to access the Core Menu.
Tap UTILITY.
Tap SOFTWARE DOWNLOAD.
Tap WiFi communication method.
Tap either FULL or PARTIAL.
Enter the unique 10-12 digit alphanumeric TPN.
Press the Green Key (Note: When inputting a repeated digit, pause between entries to avoid scrolling to letters as this entry is alphanumerically capable.)
Terminal will ask, “Apply Updates?” Tap YES.
The terminal will download and install your software, reboot, and prompt you to confirm the date and time, then return to the idle prompt.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Do a Full Download or Partial Download: Via USB
steps: Insert the USB key into your computer.
Find the USB key (removable disk) on your list of drives, and click on it to access the USB drive.
Create a new folder on your USB root directory and name it “download.” without any spaces.

Place the .TAR File (Terminal Profile) you downloaded from the STEAM system into a folder you just created named download on the root directory of your USB key. *Note: The .TAR file does not need to be uncompressed.
In Your Z Series Terminal Packaging, find the Mini B Male USB to Female A USB adaptor.
Plug the smaller male USB end into the Mini USB 1 port found on the underside of the terminal. (Turn the terminal over)
Turn over the Dejavoo terminal so it is right side up, make sure it is powered ON.
Eject your USB key from your Computer and insert the USB key into the larger Female end of the adaptor you connected to the terminal.
The terminal will display “Reading USB Directory.” The TPN file(s) you placed in the download folder will appear on the terminal display.
Tap the TPN on the terminal display.
Terminal will ask, “Apply Updates?” Tap YES.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Do a Full Download or Partial Download: Via Docking Station
steps: Connect the desired communication option to the appropriate port.
Place the Z9 onto the docking station.
For Ethernet: a. Plug CAT5 IP Cable into LAN Port. b. Place Z9 on Dock. c. Follow instructions to download software via Ethernet.
For Modem: a. Plug Phone Cable into LINE Port. b. Place Z9 on Dock. c. Follow instructions to download software via Modem.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Chip Credit Sale
steps: On the terminal home screen, press CREDIT.
Press SALE.
(If used in a restaurant): Enter SERVER # and press OK.
Enter the SALE AMOUNT. Press OK.
Tap (contactless only) or insert your chip card.
If asked, confirm the sale amount by selecting YES or NO.
You’ve processed the transaction.
Sales receipts will print with details of the transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Manual Entry Credit Sale
steps: On the terminal home screen, press CREDIT.
Touch the SALE icon. a. (If used in a restaurant): Enter SERVER # and press OK.
Enter the SALE AMOUNT and press OK.
Manually enter card #.
Follow the CNP prompts (enter exp. date, ZIP code, etc).
You’ve processed the transaction. Sales receipts will print with details.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Debit Sale
steps: On the terminal home screen, press DEBIT.
Press SALE a. (If used in a restaurant): Enter SERVER # and press OK.
Enter the SALE AMOUNT and press OK.
Tap, swipe, or insert chip card.
When asked the sale amount, confirm by tapping YES or NO.
Get cardholder to enter their PIN and press OK.
The transaction is processed. Sales receipts will print with details.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Cash Sale
steps: On the terminal home screen, press CREDIT.
Tap CASH.
Enter SALE AMOUNT and press OK.
The terminal will print the cash receipts and return to the idle prompt.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Refund: Credit Card Return
steps: On the terminal home screen, press CREDIT.
Press RETURN. a. (If used in a restaurant): Enter SERVER # and press OK.
Enter the RETURN AMOUNT and tap OK.
Tap swipe, insert chip card, or manually enter card.
If asked, confirm the sale amount by pressing YES or NO.
The return is processed. Sales receipts will print with details.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Refund: Cash Return
steps: On the terminal home screen, press CREDIT.
Press CASH in the menu list.
Press SALE.
Press RETURN.
Enter RETURN AMOUNT and press OK.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Toggle Off Sleep Mode
steps: Go to Menu.
Tap UTILITY.
Tap SETTINGS.
Tap POWER MANAGEMENT.
Tap MODE.
Tap OFF.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Do a Factory Reset: Access Core Menu
steps: Tap UTILITY.
Tap SOFTWARE DOWNLOAD.
Tap DELETE APPS.
Individually select the listed apps.
The terminal will Reboot.
Repeat the process if needed.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. The guide warns a factory reset erases all data, including transaction history and settings.

entries.title: Reboot
steps: Press and hold the POWER button on the keyboard.
Release once the terminal starts the reboot process.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Load Paper Roll
steps: Open the paper compartment by lifting the black tab.
Remove any old or excess paper.
Using Dejavoo-specified Z11 thermal paper (2.25-inch-wide), place the roll so the edge feeds from the bottom toward the screen.
Snap the cover back down to secure. If the paper appears blank, flip it over, as thermal paper needs to be loaded with the correct side facing the print head.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Turn On/Off
steps: Power On: Press and hold the green OK button. When connected to a power source, the terminal should power on automatically and be ready for transactions.
Power Off: To power down, access the FAVORITES menu by tapping the STAR icon on the main screen. Select POWER OFF. Confirm if prompted.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Set Up an Ethernet or Wi-Fi Connection: Connect to Ethernet
steps: Link your Ethernet cable from your router to the LAN port on the back of the Dejavoo Z11.
Power on the terminal. Once it initializes, the main SALE screen should appear, indicating a successful connection​.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Set Up an Ethernet or Wi-Fi Connection: Connect to WiFi
steps: To connect, press the green OK button on the terminal to access the main menu.
Select UTILITY.
Select WIFI.
Select your WiFi network. When prompted, enter the network password, then CONFIRM.
Once connected, a WiFi icon will display on the screen, and the terminal will be ready to process transactions wirelessly.​
If you are having trouble connecting to WiFi, try restarting your router. Alternatively, you can also try restarting your Dejavoo Z11.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Add Servers
steps: To add servers, access the CREDIT menu.
Select SALE.
When prompted, enter the server ID. This feature helps individual employees or business sections ​manage sales.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Chip Credit Sale
steps: From the home screen, select CREDIT.
Select SALE.
Enter the total sale amount, then confirm.
Insert the customer’s chip card with the chip facing toward the terminal. Cardholders can also tap to exercise the contactless pay option.
Confirm the amount if prompted.
Once processed, the terminal will print a receipt.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Manual Entry Credit Sale
steps: From the home screen, select CREDIT.
Select SALE.
Enter the total sale amount, then confirm.
The merchant will then manually enter card details, including expiration date, billing ZIP code, etc.
Confirm any prompts as needed; a receipt will print automatically once completed.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Debit Sale
steps: From the home screen, select DEBIT.
Select SALE.
Enter the total sale amount, then confirm.
Customers will then insert, swipe, or tap their card and enter their PIN to confirm the sale.
Once processed, the terminal will print a receipt.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Gift Card Sale
steps: From the home screen, select GIFT.
Select REDEEM.
Enter the total amount for the gift card purchase, then confirm.
Swipe gift card using the Dejavoo Z11’s magstripe reader.
Merchants will have the option to print both customer and merchant receipts.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Forced Sale
steps: Enter the total amount for the sale.
Press the yellow key with the arrow pointing to the left.
Scroll up to the TICKET option.
Press OK to confirm.
After entering the total amount of the sale again, press OK.
Enter the default password, then press OK to proceed.
Enter AUTH CODE.
Swipe, tap, insert, or manually enter card number details.
Press OK to confirm.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Add Tips or Perform a Tip Adjustment
steps: From the home screen, tap the STAR icon to open the FAVORITES menu.
Select ADD/EDIT TIP.
If prompted, enter the default/manager password. When prompted, select ALL.
Select TRANSACTION #.
Enter the TIP AMOUNT when the transaction amount appears, then press OK.
If prompted, confirm the tip amount by tapping YES or NO (this will depend on the terminal’s settings).
Repeat steps 5 and 6 for any additional tips.
When finished, press the final key to save changes.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Reprint Receipt
steps: Tap the STAR icon to access the FAVORITES menu.
Select REPRINT RECEIPT.
If prompted, enter the default/manager password.
Select the option for which receipt you’d like to reprint (LAST, BY TRANSACTION #, or BY CARD NUMBER).
Follow prompts and transaction receipt prints.

Note: If your Dejavoo Z11 is not printing, ensure the paper is loaded correctly and the thermal paper is appropriately oriented. The printer may not function if the cover is not securely closed or if there is a malfunction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Refund: Credit Card Return
steps: From the home screen, select CREDIT.
Select RETURN.
Enter the total amount for the refund, then confirm.
Swipe, tap, or insert the card to proceed with the refund.
The return will be processed, and a receipt will be printed​.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Refund: Debit Card Return
steps: From the home screen, select DEBIT.
Select RETURN.
Enter the total amount for the refund, then confirm.
Swipe or insert the card to proceed with the refund. Cardholders may be asked to verify their PIN information to verify the return.
The return will be processed, and a receipt will be printed​.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Void Transaction: Void Credit Transaction (Card Present)
steps: From the home screen, select CREDIT.
Select VOID.
Enter the amount you wish to void and confirm.
If prompted, enter the default/manager password.
Tap (for contactless) or insert the chip card.
The void will be processed, and a receipt detailing the voided transaction​will be printed.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Void Transaction: Void Credit Transaction (Card Not Present)
steps: Tap the icon on the idle screen to access the FAVORITES menu.
Select VOID TRANSACTION.
If prompted, enter the default/manager password.
Select BY TRANSACTION # to search for the specific transaction you want to void.
Enter the transaction number that needs to be voided. Confirm when ready. Some merchants may be asked to confirm twice.
Re-enter the default/manager password if required.
The void will be processed, and a receipt detailing the voided transaction​will be printed.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Settle a Daily Batch
steps: From the home screen, select the STAR icon.
Select SETTLE DAILY BATCH.
Enter the manager password when prompted.
A receipt will be printed for the merchant’s record.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Fix a Batch Host Error
steps: Start by accessing the MENU on your Z11, i.e. the three horizontal bars on the bottom half of your screen.
Select APPLICATIONS, then HOST UTILITY.
Select BATCH FEATURES.
Select the option that allows you to determine your batch number (SET BATCH #).
Enter a unique batch number that is not in the system yet.
Try settling this batch to test the efficacy of these instructions.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Change the Date and Time
steps: Start from the idle screen and press the green OK key. Alternatively, tap the three horizontal lines at the bottom left of your home screen.
Select UTILITY.
Enter default/manager password.
Select SETTINGS.
Make sure to enter the time accurately in the 24-hour format to ensure correct processing of transactions.
Select DATE & TIME.
Clear the current date and enter the correct one in the MM/DD/YY format. For a time, input it in a 24-hour format (HHMMSS). Finally, press the green OK key to save your changes.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Print Reports
steps: Press the F1 key to access the SERVICES MENU.
Select REPORTS.
You will be asked to select between the DAILY REPORT and SUMMARY REPORT. Select an option to proceed.
If prompted, enter the default/manager password.
After confirming your selection, the report will print automatically.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Download Terminal Software: Partial Download
steps: Start by ensuring all open batches have been settled.
Access the core menu.
Select UTILITY. Enter the default password when prompted.
Select SOFTWARE DOWNLOAD, then CONNECT.
Select ETHERNET (select PPP to download via phone line and WIFI to download via Wifi).
Select PARTIAL.
You will be presented with a TPN number. Confirm if the TPN number is correct.
When presented with the option to APPLY UPDATES, select YES.
Your terminal may reboot upon downloading and installing new software.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Reboot Your Dejavoo Z11
steps: Press and hold the green key to start.
If prompted, select POWER OFF or POWER DOWN.
You should see the message ‘SYSTEM INITIALIZING’ displayed on your terminal’s screen. This indicates that the startup process has begun. This process generally takes a few minutes.
Release once the terminal begins to reboot.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Do a Power Cycle
steps: If you are connected via Ethernet, unplug your Dejavoo Z11 from its Ethernet cord.
Remove connection cable and power cord.
Leave your Z11 unplugged for at least ten seconds.
After this time window has elapsed, your Z11 should power on and begin the power cycle process. This may take a few minutes.
Upon successfully powering the device back on, plug your Ethernet cord and connection cable back into your Z11.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Do a Factory Reset
steps: Start by accessing the MENU on your Z11, i.e. the three horizontal bars on the bottom half of your screen.
Select UTILITY.
Select SOFTWARE DOWNLOAD.
Select DELETE APPS.
Manually select the apps you wish to delete.
At this point, the terminal will start to reboot.
If necessary, repeat steps 1-7.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. The guide warns a factory reset erases all data, including transaction history and settings.

entries.title: Load Paper Roll
steps: Pinch both sides of the printer latch located at the top of your QD2 device (near where the receipts are dispensed posttransaction).
Load 2-1/4″ thermal receipt paper into the open slot.
Leave a small length of receipt paper extending outward from the latch.
Close the latch. Your device is now able to start printing.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Turn On/Off
steps: Power On: Press and hold the power button until the terminal turns on.
Power Off: Press and hold the power button until the terminal powers off. You may see a prompt to power off the device. If so, select this prompt.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Set Up a Wifi Connection: Connect to WiFi
steps: Start by pressing the circle button located at the bottom of your Dejavoo QD2.
Select SETTINGS.
Select WLAN.
Select your home WiFi network, then enter your personalized network password.
Select CONNECT to proceed.
Your QD2 will indicate that you are successfully connected to WiFi.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Chip Credit Sale
steps: From the home menu, select CREDIT.
A new menu will appear with the following options: SALE, RETURN, BALANCE, etc. Select SALE.
Enter the total amount for the chip card sale, then select OK to confirm.
The merchant will then be asked to tap, swipe, insert, or manually enter card number details. Since this is an EMV chip sale, cardholders will insert their card into the QD2’s chip card reader.
A prompt will appear on your screen reading PLEASE REMOVE CARD. After removing card from the chip reader, cardholders may be prompted to sign for their purchase.
After signing using the QD2’s screen capture capabilities, select OK.
If approved, the sales receipt will be printed with transaction details. If asked if you wish to print a customer copy of the receipt, select either YES or NO.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Manual Entry Credit Sale
steps: From the home menu, select CREDIT.
A new menu will appear with the following options: SALE, RETURN, BALANCE, etc. Select SALE.
Enter the total amount for the manual sale, then select OK to confirm.
You will be presented with on-display text that prompts you to tap, swipe, insert, or manually enter the card number details. Select the text that reads ENTER CARD # to proceed.
Enter the credit or debit card number into the text box on your QD2 display.
When prompted, enter the expiration date and any other relevant card details (CVV, billing code, etc.)
If approved, the sales receipt will be printed with requisite transaction details. If asked if you wish to print a customer copy of the receipt, select either YES or NO.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Debit Sale
steps: From the home menu, select DEBIT.
A new menu will appear with the following options: SALE, RETURN, BALANCE, etc. Select SALE.
Enter the total amount for the debit sale, then select OK to confirm.
The merchant will then be asked to tap, swipe, insert, or manually enter card number details. Swipe or insert debit card and follow on-screen instructions for entering PIN information.
Enter your PIN on the QD2 PIN pad, then confirm.
Cardholders may be prompted to sign for their purchase. Follow on-screen instructions.
If approved, the sales receipt will be printed with transaction details. If asked if you wish to print a customer copy of the receipt, select YES or NO.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Cash Sale
steps: From the home menu, select CASH.
Select SALE.
Enter the total amount for the cash sale, then press OK to confirm.
Enter the amount of cash received from the customer under CASH IN. The balance will be shown under CHANGE.
Authenticate the cash sale and provide change, if necessary. Select OK to proceed.
If approved, the sales receipt will be printed with requisite transaction details. If asked if you wish to print a customer copy of the receipt, select YES or NO.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Reprint Receipt
steps: Select the STAR icon on your device.
If prompted, select REPRINT or REPRINT RECEIPT.
Enter the default password.
By default, the most recent transaction will be selected. You can select from several options, including BY TRANSACTION # or BY CARD NUMBER.
To select a prior transaction, enter either the TRANSACTION ID or the last four digits of the card used in the original transaction.
Select which type of receipt you’d like to print: MERCHANT COPY or CUSTOMER COPY.
Follow the prompts to reprint.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Refund: Credit Card Return
steps: Select CREDIT.
Select REFUND or RETURN.
Enter the total amount for the refund, and select OK to confirm.
If prompted, enter the default password.
Insert your EMV chip card into the QD2’s EMV chip card reader to initiate the return.
Verify transaction details, and press OK to confirm the return.
If approved, the receipt will be printed with requisite return details.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Refund: Debit Card Return
steps: Select DEBIT.
Select REFUND or RETURN.
Enter the total amount for the refund, and select OK to confirm.
If prompted, enter the default password.
Swipe or insert your debit card and follow any on-screen instructions relating to the input of PIN information.
Verify transaction details, and press OK to confirm the return.
If approved, the receipt will be printed with return details.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Void Transaction: Void Credit Transaction (Card Present)
steps: Select the star icon to access FAVORITES.
Select VOID or VOID TRANSACTION.
Enter the total amount for the void, then press OK.
If prompted, enter the default password.
At this point, the merchant or cardholder will tap, swipe, or insert the card used in the original transaction in order to proceed with authenticating the void.
You will receive a prompt on your display letting you know that the void has been APPROVED, and a receipt will be printed.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Void Transaction: Void Credit Transaction (Card Not Present)
steps: Select the star icon to access FAVORITES.
Select VOID or VOID TRANSACTION.
If prompted, enter the default password.
Narrow down options for the transaction you wish to void by selecting BY TRANSACTION #.
Enter the transaction number for the transaction you wish to void, then select OK.
Confirm that the transaction is correct by pressing OK.
If prompted, enter the default password again.
The merchant will have the option to print a receipt with details of the voided transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Print Reports
steps: Select the star icon to access FAVORITES.
Select REPORTS.
If prompted, enter the default password, then select OK.
Select the relevant report type: DAILY REPORT or SUMMARY REPORT (merchants may also have the option to select alternatives such as DETAILED REPORT, UNTIPPED REPORT, etc).
Merchants may also have the opportunity to select TRANSACTION TYPE or give unique names to CUSTOM REPORTS.
When ready, select the relevant report.
The terminal will print a copy of the report.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Change the Date and Time
steps: From the home menu, select SETTINGS.
Select the three horizontal bars located in the upper right-hand corner of your QD2.
Scroll down until you see the DATE & TIME option.
Turn the toggles for AUTOMATIC DATE & TIME and AUTOMATIC TIME ZONE off. This turns off automated date and time settings.
On the same menu, select SELECT TIME ZONE. Select your regional time zone to continue.
Following this, you can toggle the AUTOMATIC DATE & TIME and AUTOMATIC TIME ZONE settings back on.
Press the circle button at the bottom of your device to be returned to the home menu.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Turn On/Off
steps: Power On: Press and hold down the power button on your device until your Dejavoo QD3 activates.
Power Off: Press and hold down the power button on your device until your Dejavoo QD3 powers off.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD3 running sales by itself; our sheet treats the QD3 as a PIN pad working off a master terminal.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Chip Credit Sale
steps: Select the CREDIT icon on your home screen.
You will be presented with SALE, VOID, BALANCE, etc. Select SALE.
Enter SALE amount, then confirm.
The cardholder will be prompted to swipe, insert, or tap their card. Cardholders should insert their card with the EMV chip facing up or exercise the contactless tap option.
The transaction will either be approved or declined. The cardholder may be prompted to sign for the purchase.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD3 running sales by itself; our sheet treats the QD3 as a PIN pad working off a master terminal.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Manual Entry Credit Sale
steps: Select the CREDIT icon on your home screen.
You will then be presented with SALE, VOID, BALANCE, etc. Select SALE.
Enter the total SALE amount, then confirm.
The cardholder will be asked to swipe, insert, tap their card, or enter the card details manually. Select ENTER CARD #.
Enter the card number and confirm.
If prompted, enter the card’s expiration date, then confirm.

Press YES if this is a card-present transaction. Press NO if this is a card-not-present transaction. Merchants performing a manual entry for a card-not-present transaction may be asked to enter the AVS or card code security details.
If this is a card-present transaction, the merchant must use the keypad on their QD3 device to enter a zip code, billing address, and CID number.
The sale will either be approved or declined.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD3 running sales by itself; our sheet treats the QD3 as a PIN pad working off a master terminal.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Debit Sale
steps: Select the DEBIT icon on your home screen.
You will then be presented with SALE, RETURN, BALANCE, etc. Select SALE.
Enter the SALE amount, then confirm.
The cardholder will be prompted to swipe, insert, or tap their card.
The total amount will be confirmed after the cardholder has swiped, tapped, or inserted their card. Customers will be prompted to enter PIN details on the QD3’s encrypted PIN pad before confirming.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD3 running sales by itself; our sheet treats the QD3 as a PIN pad working off a master terminal.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Cash Sale
steps: Press the CASH icon on your home screen.
When prompted, select SALE.
Select the appropriate amount for CASH SALE, then confirm.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD3 running sales by itself; our sheet treats the QD3 as a PIN pad working off a master terminal.

entries.title: View Reports
steps: Access your device’s CORE MENU.
Select REPORTS.
In the OPEN/CLOSED batch, select REPORT to proceed.
Select a report type: Daily, Non-Cash, Summary, Tipped, or Un-Tipped.
Select NEXT and the report will appear.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD3 running sales by itself; our sheet treats the QD3 as a PIN pad working off a master terminal.

entries.title: Change the Date and Time
steps: Access your device’s CORE MENU.
If prompted, select UTILITY.
Select SETTINGS.
Find and select the DATE AND TIME option.
If the listed date and time are accurate, leave them as is. If they are incorrect, clear them before re-entering the correct details.
Enter the relevant information in the MM/DD/YY format
Enter the appropriate regional time zone in the 24-hour clock/military time format
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD3 running sales by itself; our sheet treats the QD3 as a PIN pad working off a master terminal.

entries.title: Reboot Your Dejavoo QD3
steps: Press the small button on the side of your QD3 that features a dash inside a circle.
Hold down the button until you see a MENU display on the screen of your QD3.
Select from a series of options: AIRPLANE MODE, POWER OFF, REBOOT, or SILENT MODE.
Select REBOOT.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD3 running sales by itself; our sheet treats the QD3 as a PIN pad working off a master terminal.

entries.title: Reset the Password for the Dejavoo QD3 Terminal
steps: Access your device’s CORE MENU.
If prompted, select UTILITY.
Select SECURITY.
Select EDIT PASSWORD.

Use the keypad on your Dejavoo QD3 to create your new password. You may or may not be prompted to enter your old password before proceeding with the new one. If this is the case, confirm your old password before setting up a new one.
Re-enter your NEW PASSWORD to confirm.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD3 running sales by itself; our sheet treats the QD3 as a PIN pad working off a master terminal.

entries.title: Load Paper Roll
steps: Hold the device in both hands.
Pinch the sides of the top of the device up next to the credit card tap section.
Flip the top away from the device screen.
Insert the receipt paper into the slot. The paper size should be about 50ft.
Roll out some of the receipt paper so that the top is closed and the end of the paper is left out.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Turn On/Off
steps: Press and hold the POWER button on the left-hand side of the terminal when the screen is facing up.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Connect to Wi-Fi or Ethernet
steps: Tap on the top right corner of the screen and swipe down.
Select the Wi-Fi icon.
Wait for the list of networks to load.
Tap on your network.
Enter your Wi-Fi password.
Tap CONNECT to finish WiFi setup.
How to connect to Ethernet.
Plug an ethernet cord into the port at the bottom of the device.
Connect the other end to the modem or router.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Chip Credit Sale
steps: Press the CREDIT icon on the home screen. A new screen will display the following options: SALE, RETURN, VOID, AUTH, TICKET, and BALANCE.
Press SALE.
Input the SALE amount and press OK.
Customer will be prompted to tap, insert, swipe, or enter their card number manually. They will need to tap or insert chip card.
The sale will be processed. The transaction will be declined or approved.
The customer will be prompted to sign. Once signed, press OK.
Sales receipts will be printed with details.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Manual Entry Credit Sale
steps: Press the CREDIT icon on the home screen. A new screen will display the following options: SALE, RETURN, VOID, AUTH, TICKET, and BALANCE.
Press SALE.
Input the SALE amount and press OK.
Customer will be prompted to tap, insert, swipe, or enter their card number manually. Tap on ENTER CARD NUMBER.
Enter the card number and press OK.
Enter the expiry date and press OK.
When asked if the card is present, press YES if it is and NO if it is not.

If the card is present, you will be prompted to enter the CID number, ZIP CODE, and ADDRESS. If the card is not present, enter AVS (Address Verification Service) and card’s code security information. (Note: Code is 3 digits on the back of MasterCard or Visa found in the signature line, and 4 digits on the front right of American Express found above card number).
The sale will be processed. The transaction will be declined or approved.
Sales receipts will be printed with details.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Debit Sale
steps: Press the DEBIT icon on your terminal home screen. A new screen will display the following options: SALE, RETURN, and BALANCE.
Press SALE.
Input the SALE amount and press OK.
Customer will be prompted to tap, insert, or swipe their card. Select the appropriate option.
If prompted, select your chosen application.
If prompted, confirm the SALE AMOUNT by tapping YES.
Customer will be prompted to enter PIN on the encrypted terminal PIN Pad or encrypted external PIN Pad. The customer should then press OK.
The terminal will flash the host response and print the sales receipt. Once finished, the terminal will return to idle prompt.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Cash Sale
steps: Press CASH on the home screen.
Press SALE.
Input the CASH SALE amount and press OK.
The sale will be processed. Sales receipts will be printed with details.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Print Reports
steps: Choose REPORT from OPEN/CLOSED Batch.
Tap on the desired report type (Summary, Daily, Un-Tipped, Tipped, Non Cash).
Tap on NEXT and then tap on PRINTER.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Run a Cash Discount
steps: Tap CREDIT.
Tap SALE.
Enter SALE AMOUNT.
Terminal will prompt you to confirm the cash discount amount and the non-cash adjustment. If the amount is correct, press OK.
Customer will be prompted to tap, insert, swipe, or enter their card number manually. Choose the appropriate option.
Transaction will process and the sale receipt will print with details.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's.

entries.title: Load Paper Roll
steps: Use thermal paper (2 ” x 50’).
Locate the paper compartment on your Dejavoo device.
Insert thermal paper roll into the open compartment with paper feeding from the bottom.
Leave a few inches of paper hanging out over the top of the roll.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: Turn On/Off
steps: Power On: Press and hold down the power button on the side of your device until your Dejavoo QD5 activates.
Power Off: Press and hold down the power button on the side of your device until your Dejavoo QD5 powers off.
If prompted, confirm that you want to turn your Dejavoo QD5 off.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: Set Up an Ethernet or Wi-Fi Connection: Connect to Ethernet
steps: Before getting started, ensure your ethernet cable is functional and securely plugged into the open port on your Dejavoo device.
Access the Core Menu on your Dejavoo QD5.
When prompted, select the UTILITY option.
Select COMMUNICATIONS.
Select LOCAL PARAMS.
You will then be asked to select a connection option, such as WIFI or ETHERNET. When prompted, select ETHERNET.
For Mode: select MODE to confirm.
For Static IP: select STATIC to confirm.
Use the device’s touchscreen to select your desired configuration option, then confirm.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: Set Up an Ethernet or Wi-Fi Connection: Connect to Wi-Fi
steps: Access the SETTINGS menu on your Dejavoo device.
Select either COMM SETUP or WLAN.
At this point, you will be presented with a series of available connection options: WIFI, ETHERNET, BLUETOOTH, etc. Select WIFI.
Following this, select the network of your choosing.
Enter your network password and select the CONNECT option when prompted.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Chip Credit Sale
steps: To begin, select the CREDIT ICON.
Select SALE.
Enter and confirm the Sale Amount.
Insert EMV Chip Card into Dejavoo QD5. When prompted, confirm sale total.
Terminal will notify the merchant when the transaction has been approved. The cardholder may also be asked to sign for their purchase. Sales receipts will be printed with details of the transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Manual Entry Credit Sale
steps: To begin, select the CREDIT ICON.
Select SALE.
Enter and confirm the Sale Amount.
When prompted, select ENTER CARD #.
Manually enter the card number into your Dejavoo device, then confirm.
Your terminal may display a notification reading “EXP DATE [MMYY].” If so, enter the card’s expiration date when prompted, then confirm.

You may be asked to confirm whether the transaction in question was a card-present or card-not-present (CNP) transaction. Confirm the correct selection when prompted. Cardholders for card-present transactions may be asked to provide billing address information. Cardholders for card-not-present transactions may be prompted to enter AVS and card code security details.
Terminal will notify the merchant when the transaction has been approved. Sales receipts will be printed with details of the transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Debit Sale
steps: Select DEBIT to begin.
Select SALE.
Enter and confirm the Sale Amount for the transaction.
Insert or swipe debit card.
The customer inputs the PIN information and confirms the sale. Authorization for the purchase will commence upon confirmation.
Terminal will notify the merchant when the transaction has been approved. Sales receipts will be printed with details of the transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: Process a Sale: Cash Sale
steps: Select CASH to begin.
Select SALE.
Enter and confirm the Sale Amount for the transaction.
Terminal will notify the merchant when the transaction has been approved. Sales receipts will be printed with details of the transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: Process a Refund: Credit Card Return
steps: To begin, select the CREDIT ICON.
When prompted, select the RETURN option.
Enter the return amount, then confirm.
At this point, merchants will insert or swipe the card needing a refund. If the transaction was completed via contactless payment, the merchant will have the opportunity to tap.
Press YES to confirm your return.
Terminal will notify the merchant when the transaction has been approved. Sales receipts will be printed with details of the transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: Process a Refund: Cash Return
steps: To begin, select the CASH ICON.
Select RETURN. When prompted, enter and confirm the total amount for the return in question. If prompted, enter the manager password.
Press YES to confirm transaction.
Terminal will notify the merchant when the transaction has been approved. Sales receipts will be printed with details of the transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: Void Transaction: Void Credit Transaction (Card Not Present)
steps: Press the STAR ICON on your QD5’s touchscreen.
When prompted, select VOID TRANSACTION.

Your most recent transaction will be selected by default. Dejavoo QD5 users can select which transaction they want to void based on several criteria, including Transaction Number and CInvoice Number. To view a list of all transactions, select VIEW ALL.
Select and confirm the transaction in question.
Terminal will notify the merchant when the transaction has been approved. Sales receipts will be printed with details of the transaction.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: Print Reports
steps: Access your device’s Core Menu.
Select REPORT.
Select the report type: Daily, Summary, etc. and tap to print.
A copy will be printed.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: Reboot your Dejavoo QD5
steps: Press the power button on the side of the QD5. Hold until a menu appears on your screen. You will then be presented with a series of power options: POWER OFF, REBOOT, etc.
Select REBOOT.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's own guide, not Dejavoo's. It describes the QD5 as a standalone terminal with a printer; our sheet and Dejavoo list the QD5 as a PIN pad paired to a QD4.

entries.title: FD150: which cable goes in which port (colour codes)
steps: The telephone port is blue.
The Ethernet port is yellow.
The USB ports are black.
The RS-232 port is green.
Port positions can vary by terminal model, but the colour codes are the same on all terminals.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: what connection the terminal needs
steps: The terminal needs a connection such as DSL, cable or dial-up.
If you use dial-up, a dedicated phone line is recommended.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: load a paper roll (user guide)
steps: Open the printer cover's latch.
Put the roll of paper into the printer.
Make sure the leading edge of the paper comes out at the bottom edge of the printer.
Close the cover and tear off any extra paper.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: connect power and check it starts
steps: Plug the power cord into the power adapter.
Connect the small end of the power plug to the terminal.
Turn the plug so the cord points toward the back of the terminal and lies flat underneath it.
Plug the power cord into a surge protector (recommended) or a standard outlet.
The screen lights up and shows the home screen.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: what you need for Wi-Fi
steps: You need a wireless access point, modem or router that supports 802.11 b/g/n.
You also need broadband internet service.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: set up Wi-Fi from the Tool icon
steps: Touch the Tool icon on the home screen.
Touch Wi-Fi, then Security.
Check that the security mode matches your Wi-Fi system's settings.
Make sure the network name (SSID) and the password (key) match your Wi-Fi system settings.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: Wi-Fi will not connect: check the security mode
steps: Touch the Tool icon, then Wi-Fi, then Security.
Check that the security mode matches your Wi-Fi system (WPA1-TKIP, WPA1-AES or WPA2-AES).
To change it, touch the drop-down arrow and pick a new option.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: Wi-Fi network name is case sensitive; a USB keyboard can be used to type it
steps: The network name (SSID) is case sensitive and can be up to 32 bytes long.
Enter the SSID and the password (key) exactly as set on your Wi-Fi system.
A USB keyboard may be connected to the terminal to enter this information.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: check Wi-Fi signal strength
steps: Go back to the home screen.
Touch the Tool icon.
Touch Wi-Fi, then View Status.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: settle (close) the batch by hand (First Data user guide)
steps: From the home screen, select Other.
Select CLOSE or Close Batch (the wording depends on the terminal model).
Select OK on the touch screen.
The terminal completes the batch settlement.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: turn on automatic batch close
steps: The terminal can be set to auto-close the batch, or you can close it by hand.
Auto-close settings are set up by the help desk.
Call the help desk number on the sticker on the side of the device.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: the chip card must stay in the slot until prompted
steps: The customer inserts the chip card into the slot at the front of the terminal or PIN pad (the dip slot).
Leave the card in the slot until the device prompts the customer to remove it.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: PIN prompt during a sale
steps: Follow the on-screen prompts.
If prompted, the customer enters their PIN.
The customer can press Cancel X to bypass the PIN.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: customer receipt prompt, and how to skip it
steps: The device prints a receipt automatically or prompts for the customer receipt.
To skip the customer receipt, press ENTER or CANCEL (the red button).
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: refund a card (First Data user guide)
steps: From the home screen, select Other.
Select Refund.
Enter the amount.
Have the customer insert, swipe or tap their card.
Select Credit.
The device prints a receipt or prompts for the customer receipt.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: where the guide sends you for more help
steps: The guide covers only the most common transactions.
For more detail it points to businesstrack.com/terminalguides.
For questions, call the help desk at the number on the sticker on the device.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: what is in the box
steps: First Data FD150 terminal.
Thermal paper roll.
Telephone cord and/or Ethernet cable.
Two-piece AC power supply.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: what else you need for each connection type
steps: Cable internet: a router, a modem, an Ethernet cable and a coaxial cable.
DSL: a router, a modem and two Ethernet cables.
Dial-up: a splitter is optional.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: use a surge protector or UPS
steps: To prevent damage to the terminal and connected devices, plug it into a surge protector or a UPS with battery backup and phone/fax protection.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: where to put the terminal
steps: Place the terminal on a desk or tabletop.
Keep it away from direct sunlight and objects that give off heat.
Keep it away from heavy dust.
Keep it away from other electrical devices that can cause excessive voltage.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: load paper (quick set-up guide), and the recommended paper
steps: Pop the printer cover's latch and lift the cover.
Load a roll of paper into the printer. Appleton POS Grade Plus 600-2.4 is the recommended paper.
The thermal print side of the paper should feed out facing the operator.
Close the cover and tear off any extra paper.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: how long set-up takes
steps: Typical set-up time is 10 to 15 minutes.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: where an RP10 PIN pad or check reader plugs in
steps: An extra device such as the RP10 PIN pad or a MagTek MiniMICR check reader connects to either the USB or the RS-232 port.
Follow the instructions that came with that device.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: connect all accessories before plugging in power
steps: Connect all peripherals to the terminal first.
Connect the power supply last.
Plugging in power before the peripherals may damage the terminal or the connected devices.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: plug in the power (quick set-up guide)
steps: Connect the power cord to the power supply using the three-prong end.
Find the power input on the right side of the terminal and plug the single-pole adapter plug into it.
Turn the plug so the cord points toward the back of the terminal.
Plug the adapter into a surge protector (strongly recommended) or a standard 120V outlet.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: internal battery warning (CR2032)
steps: The terminal has a 3V CR2032 battery.
There is a risk of explosion if it is replaced with the wrong type.
Used batteries must be disposed of according to local regulations.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: swipe a card
steps: With the idle message on the screen, select the transaction type.
Put the card in the reader slot with the magnetic stripe in the slot and facing the terminal.
Slide the card through in either direction without stopping.
Follow the prompts on the display to finish.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: card swipe fails
steps: Check which way the magnetic stripe is facing and slide the card again.
If it keeps failing, the card's stripe may be damaged.
Enter the account number by hand on the keypad.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: insert a chip card
steps: Find the card slot at the front of the FD150.
Insert the card all the way, so the chip is no longer visible, with the front of the card facing up.
Leave the card in for the whole transaction.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: chip card reading has to be enabled on the terminal
steps: Chip (smart card) capability is optional and must be enabled.
Contact your sales or customer service representative to have it enabled.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: tap a contactless card or phone
steps: The customer taps their contactless card or device against the contactless icon on the FD150.
In some cases the terminal asks for a second tap to complete the transaction.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: type letters on the keypad
steps: Press ALPHA, then the number key that carries the letter. For A, press ALPHA then 2.
For the second letter on a key, press ALPHA twice, then the key. For B, press ALPHA twice then 2.
For the third letter, press ALPHA three times, then the key. For C, press ALPHA three times then 2.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: FD150: the touchscreen can be used as well as the keypad
steps: The FD150 has a touchscreen with a simplified menu.
Many functions can be selected on the touchscreen instead of the keypad.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted on a reseller's Shopify store)

entries.title: RP10: connect the PIN pad to the terminal
steps: Remove the bottom cover from the terminal, if needed.
Disconnect power from the terminal.
Plug the PIN pad's USB cable into one of the USB ports on the back of the terminal.
Once the cables are fully connected, reconnect power to the terminal.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted by TowneBank)

entries.title: RP10: what it shows when it starts
steps: The PIN pad starts up automatically when it is connected to the terminal.
It shows a status message until the terminal initializes it.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted by TowneBank)

entries.title: RP10: two ways to start a transaction
steps: The customer can start the transaction by swiping, tapping or inserting their card on the PIN pad.
Or start the transaction on the FD terminal; the PIN pad and terminal then prompt when the customer should present their card.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted by TowneBank)

entries.title: RP10: tap a contactless card or phone
steps: Only cards and devices marked with the contactless icon can tap.
The customer taps the card or device against the top of the RP10 screen.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted by TowneBank)

entries.title: RP10: swipe a card
steps: Find the card reader slot on the right side of the RP10.
Slide the card from the top of the device to the bottom, with the face of the card facing outward (to the right).
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted by TowneBank)

entries.title: RP10: insert a chip card
steps: Find the card reader slot at the front of the RP10.
Insert the card completely, with the front of the card facing up.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted by TowneBank)

entries.title: RP10: may not work with another processor's systems
steps: First Data equipment and software may not be compatible with another processor's systems.
entries.by: First Data / Fiserv (maker's guide; copy hosted by TowneBank)

entries.title: FD150: load receipt paper, step by step (Paysafe-posted guide)
steps: Gently pull the printer cover's latch and lift the cover away from the printer.
Load a roll of thermal paper.
Make sure the roll feeds out so the print side of the paper faces the operator.
Close the cover by pressing down evenly on both side tabs, or on the centre of the cover.
Tear off extra paper on the serrated bar.
entries.note: From a First Data guide written for Australia (EFTPOS, AUD) that Paysafe posts as its FD150 guide. Its menus differ from the US FD150 software, so only hardware-level points are kept.
entries.by: Paysafe Help Center (hosting a First Data Australia guide; treated as tier 2 because it describes a different software build from the US FD150)

entries.title: FD150: store and handle thermal paper carefully
steps: Store thermal paper in a dry, dark area.
Handle it carefully: impact, friction, temperature, humidity and oils can affect the paper.
entries.note: From a First Data guide written for Australia (EFTPOS, AUD) that Paysafe posts as its FD150 guide. Its menus differ from the US FD150 software, so only hardware-level points are kept.
entries.by: Paysafe Help Center (hosting a First Data Australia guide; treated as tier 2 because it describes a different software build from the US FD150)

entries.title: FD150: do not load a damaged paper roll
steps: Never load a roll that has folds, wrinkles, tears or holes at the edges of the print area.
entries.note: From a First Data guide written for Australia (EFTPOS, AUD) that Paysafe posts as its FD150 guide. Its menus differ from the US FD150 software, so only hardware-level points are kept.
entries.by: Paysafe Help Center (hosting a First Data Australia guide; treated as tier 2 because it describes a different software build from the US FD150)

entries.title: FD150: check the lights next to the Ethernet port
steps: Plug the Ethernet cable into the Ethernet port on the back of the terminal and the other end into the router.
The lights next to the Ethernet port should flash to show a connection.
If the lights do not come on, there is no connection between the terminal and the router.
Check the cable and the router.
entries.note: From a First Data guide written for Australia (EFTPOS, AUD) that Paysafe posts as its FD150 guide. Its menus differ from the US FD150 software, so only hardware-level points are kept.
entries.by: Paysafe Help Center (hosting a First Data Australia guide; treated as tier 2 because it describes a different software build from the US FD150)

entries.title: FD150: blue contactless lights mean the tap reader is working
steps: The contactless reader antenna is behind the display and PIN pad.
The reader's lights show blue when the terminal is powered on, to show the reader is working normally.
To take a tap payment, hold the card near the reader during a transaction.
entries.note: From a First Data guide written for Australia (EFTPOS, AUD) that Paysafe posts as its FD150 guide. Its menus differ from the US FD150 software, so only hardware-level points are kept.
entries.by: Paysafe Help Center (hosting a First Data Australia guide; treated as tier 2 because it describes a different software build from the US FD150)

entries.title: FD150: swipe fails: check the stripe position (Paysafe-posted guide)
steps: The magnetic card slot is on the right side of the terminal.
Slide the card through in either direction without stopping.
If the swipe fails, check the position of the magnetic stripe and slide the card again.
entries.note: From a First Data guide written for Australia (EFTPOS, AUD) that Paysafe posts as its FD150 guide. Its menus differ from the US FD150 software, so only hardware-level points are kept.
entries.by: Paysafe Help Center (hosting a First Data Australia guide; treated as tier 2 because it describes a different software build from the US FD150)

entries.title: FD150: privacy shield described as adhesive (Paysafe-posted guide)
steps: Remove the adhesive tab around the privacy shield.
Carefully place the shield's adhesive side around the keypad.
entries.note: From a First Data guide written for Australia (EFTPOS, AUD) that Paysafe posts as its FD150 guide. Its menus differ from the US FD150 software, so only hardware-level points are kept. Our sheets describe a snap-on privacy guard instead.
entries.by: Paysafe Help Center (hosting a First Data Australia guide; treated as tier 2 because it describes a different software build from the US FD150)

entries.title: FD150: what to do when a transaction is declined
steps: Check that the transaction is approved before completing the sale.
If it is declined, tell the customer the reason shown.
Advise them to contact their bank if required.
Ask for another form of payment.
entries.note: From a First Data guide written for Australia (EFTPOS, AUD) that Paysafe posts as its FD150 guide. Its menus differ from the US FD150 software, so only hardware-level points are kept.
entries.by: Paysafe Help Center (hosting a First Data Australia guide; treated as tier 2 because it describes a different software build from the US FD150)

entries.title: FD150: a void is only possible before settlement (Paysafe-posted guide)
steps: A transaction can only be voided before the terminal is settled.
If the terminal has already been settled, refund the incorrect transaction and process it again.
entries.note: From a First Data guide written for Australia (EFTPOS, AUD) that Paysafe posts as its FD150 guide. Its menus differ from the US FD150 software, so only hardware-level points are kept. The void steps in this guide are for the Australian menu and are not recorded here.
entries.by: Paysafe Help Center (hosting a First Data Australia guide; treated as tier 2 because it describes a different software build from the US FD150)

entries.title: Y1: offline approved
steps: The terminal approved the transaction without contacting the card issuer.
Approved offline transactions are forwarded to the issuer later.

entries.by: Paysafe Help Center (hosting a First Data Australia guide; treated as tier 2 because it describes a different software build from the US FD150)

entries.title: Z1: offline declined
steps: The terminal declined the transaction without contacting the card issuer.

entries.title: Y3: unable to go online and approved offline
steps: The terminal could not go online and approved the transaction offline.
Approved offline transactions are forwarded to the issuer later.

steps: The terminal could not go online and declined the transaction offline.

entries.title: B350: no lights at all after pressing the power button
steps: The battery is likely dead, so charge the reader.
Plug it into a wall outlet to charge, rather than a handheld battery pack or a computer.

entries.title: B350: blue light on steadily (light above the Bluetooth symbol)
steps: Nothing to fix: the reader is connected to your phone or tablet and ready to take a card payment.

entries.title: B350: blue light flashing (light above the Bluetooth symbol)
steps: The reader is in standby: it is waiting to be connected over Bluetooth, or Bluetooth has disconnected.
Start a sale in the SwipeSimple app so the app connects to the reader.

entries.title: B350: red light on steadily (light above the battery symbol)
steps: Nothing to fix: the battery is fully charged.

entries.title: B350: red light flashing slowly (light above the battery symbol)
steps: The reader is not charging, but the battery is not low.
Plug it in if you want it to charge.

entries.title: B350: red light flashing quickly (light above the battery symbol)
steps: The battery is low or critically low.
Charge the reader, ideally from a wall outlet.

entries.title: B350: where to plug the reader in to charge
steps: Charge the reader from a wall outlet.
Avoid charging from a handheld battery pack or a computer.

entries.title: B350: flashes blue and shows solid red when you hold the power button
steps: This is the normal power-on pattern for a B350.
Continue with pairing in the SwipeSimple app.

entries.title: B350: lights flash a series of colors after a reset
steps: This is normal after a reset.
Wait for the lights to return to normal standby; the reader is then reset.

entries.title: App shows "Tap, Dip, or Swipe" with the reader image
steps: Nothing to fix: the reader is connected and ready.
Have the customer tap, insert or swipe the card.

entries.title: B350: pair the reader for the first time
steps: Charge the reader with the included cable plugged into a power adapter; a full charge may take up to two hours.
Download the SwipeSimple app from the App Store or Google Play Store.
Turn Bluetooth on on your phone or tablet.
Press and hold the reader's power button until it flashes blue and shows solid red.
Open the SwipeSimple app, enter an amount and tap Checkout.
When asked if you will use a reader, choose Yes.
Grant all the permissions the app asks for.
Wait while SwipeSimple finds and pairs with the nearby reader on its own.
When the app says "Tap, Dip, or Swipe" with the reader image, the reader is ready.

entries.title: B350: do not pair the reader in the phone's own Bluetooth settings
steps: Pair the reader inside the SwipeSimple app, not in the phone or tablet's Bluetooth settings.
If this is the first time, follow the first-time pairing steps in the app.

entries.title: B350: the reader cannot be paired with a computer or laptop
steps: Use the reader with a phone or tablet only.
To take payments on a computer, use the SwipeSimple Virtual Terminal instead.

entries.title: SwipeSimple app: check which app version you are running
steps: Open the SwipeSimple app.
Tap the menu icon (three horizontal lines).
Look at the bottom left corner of the sidebar for the version number.
If an update is available, update the app from the App Store or Google Play Store.

entries.title: B350 will not connect: let the app check Bluetooth and permissions
steps: Open the SwipeSimple app; it checks Bluetooth and the other permissions it needs by itself.
If the app asks you to turn something on, follow those prompts before going further.

entries.title: B350 will not connect: it may already be paired to another phone or tablet
steps: A Bluetooth reader can only connect to one device at a time.
On the other device, open its Bluetooth settings and look for the reader in the paired devices list.
If it is there, tap it and choose "Forget This Device" or "Unpair".
Keep the reader powered on and close to your device, then connect it through the SwipeSimple app.

entries.title: B350 does not connect on an iPhone or iPad
steps: Make sure the reader is on and fully charged.
Make sure the reader is not paired in the device's own Bluetooth settings.
In SwipeSimple go to Settings > Device Pairing.
Make sure Use Bluetooth Reader is switched on.
Check that the reader appears in the list of available readers and tap it to pair.
Open the device Settings, scroll to the list of apps and choose SwipeSimple.
Make sure Bluetooth, Microphone and Local Network are enabled for SwipeSimple.
If the reader still does not appear during a transaction, reset the reader.

entries.title: B350 does not connect on an Android phone or tablet
