entries.title: Epson TM-U220II (Types A and B): return the autocutter blade to its normal position
steps: Open the roll paper cover using the tab.
With a ballpoint pen or tweezers, turn the autocutter knob in the direction of the arrow until you see a round shaft in the hole.

entries.title: Epson TM-U220II: remove jammed paper (user manual)
steps: Let the print head cool first; it gets very hot during printing.
Open the roll paper cover using the tab.
On a Type A printer, remove the take-up spool and open the unit with the unit open lever.
Remove the jammed paper.
Put the roll paper back in and close the roll paper cover.

entries.title: Epson TM-U220II: power switch is behind a cover
steps: The power switch is on the front of the printer.
If the power switch cover is fitted, insert a thin tool into one of the holes in the cover to work the switch.
If the printer will be stored or unused for a long time, turn it off with the power switch.

entries.title: Epson TM-U220II: printing stops part-way or the same line prints again and again (wrong power supply)
steps: Make sure the correct power supply unit is connected.
For the TM-U220II (Types A, B and D) the manual lists "AC adapter,C1", "PS-180" or "PS-190".

entries.title: Epson TM-U220II: do not open the cover while printing
steps: Do not open the roll paper cover during printing or paper feeding, or while the autocutter is working.
After feeding, cut the paper with the manual cutter.

entries.title: Epson TM-U220II: fit the ribbon cassette (user manual steps)
steps: Let the print head cool before replacing the ribbon.
Open the ribbon cassette cover using the tabs on its sides.
Turn the cassette knob two or three times in the direction of the arrow; never turn it the other way.
Put the ribbon in position and push the cassette down until it clicks; the ribbon must sit between the print head and the platen without wrinkles.
Turn the knob two or three times again and close the cover.
To remove a cassette, lift its left side first, then the whole cassette.
Use the EPSON ERC-38 ribbon cassette.

entries.title: Epson TM-U220II: loading 2-ply roll paper
steps: Note the direction the paper comes off the roll.
With 2-ply paper make sure the top and bottom sheets are aligned at the paper exit.

entries.title: Epson TM-U220II: self-test (user manual)
steps: Make sure all covers are closed.
Press and hold the FEED button while turning the power on, and keep holding until printing starts.
The printer status prints, then a self-test continuation guide prints and the PAPER OUT light blinks.

entries.title: Epson TM-U220II: what is in the box
steps: Printer, exclusive ribbon cassette ERC-38(B/R) and power supply switch cover.
Roll paper, AC adapter and locking wire saddle may not be included.
If any item is damaged, contact your dealer.

entries.title: Epson TM-U220II: smoke, strange smell, unusual noise, or liquid spilled inside
steps: Shut the printer down immediately and unplug it.
Do not keep using it.
Contact qualified service personnel; never try to repair it yourself.

entries.title: Union support: phone, text, email and hours
steps: Union Support is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.
Call or text 855-384-6839.
Or email support@getunion.com.
Support is at no charge.
entries.note: From Union's own support page; the phone number appears on the page as "PHONE or TEXT SUPPORT 855-384-6839".

entries.title: Union support: texting the support number
steps: You can text Union's support number instead of calling.
By texting it you agree to get text replies to that mobile number; reply STOP to cancel.

entries.title: Union: free weekly live training sessions
steps: Union runs free virtual training sessions open to operators, managers and staff.
Front-of-house sessions: every Monday at 12PM CST and every Friday at 2PM CST.
Back-of-house (owners, managers) session: every Tuesday at 1PM CST.
Join links are on Union's virtual training page.

entries.title: Union Pocket: get started with Tap to Pay on iPhone
steps: Download the Union Pocket Handheld POS app.
Complete the sign-up information.
Accept in-person contactless payments on the iPhone.
No card reader or other hardware is needed.
entries.note: Union's page gives only these three steps; existing merchants are told to "Get Activated".

entries.title: Union Tap to Pay on iPhone: requirements and limits
steps: Tap to Pay on iPhone needs the latest version of iOS.
Some contactless cards may not be accepted.
Transaction limits may apply.
It is not available in all markets.

entries.title: Union Tap to Pay on iPhone: what it can take
steps: It takes in-person contactless payments: physical contactless debit and credit cards, Apple Pay and other digital wallets.
The guest taps their card, smartphone or wearable on the iPhone.

entries.title: Union Pocket (POS on iPhone): which iPhones work
steps: Union Pocket works with any iPhone 12 or later.
Merchants can use their own compatible iPhones.
The app installs directly from the App Store.

entries.title: Union Pocket: taking payment without a card reader
steps: Tap to Pay on iPhone: the guest taps their card or phone on the iPhone.
Scan to Pay: the guest scans a QR code with their own phone.
Guest-led digital payment: the guest pays from their own phone.

entries.title: Union: local field support markets
steps: Union lists local field support in NYC, Austin, Dallas, Tampa, Charleston and Portland, OR.
Elsewhere, call or text Union's 24/7 support line.

entries.title: A920 will not hold a charge (new terminal)
steps: Turn the terminal off.
Remove the battery from the terminal.
Peel the protection sticker off the battery.
Put the battery back in.
Plug in the charger.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ says 'A920'; the A920 Pro and A920MAX guides describe the same battery tab.

entries.title: Apple Pay / contactless is not enabled
steps: Contactless has to be switched on in the terminal's file by the merchant service provider.
After it is enabled, power the terminal off and on so it downloads the change.

entries.title: Connect Error: run a ping test (Android terminal)
steps: A Connect Error can be a network problem or a host problem.
Open the payment app.
Press Func.
Choose Settings.
Choose Communication.
Choose Ping.
Confirm the address shown (google.com).
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Connect Error: run a ping test (traditional terminal)
steps: Go to Menu.
Go to Communication.
Enter the password.
Go to LAN Parameters or Wi-Fi Parameters.
Select Ping.
Press Enter on the server address shown (google.com).
The terminal says Ping Okay if it is connected to the internet.
entries.note: Traditional (non-Android) PAX terminal, i.e. the S920 that sits in this base.

entries.title: Module Check (traditional terminals)
steps: Module Check lets you test on the terminal whether the chip reader, magnetic reader, contactless reader and keys are working.
entries.note: Traditional (non-Android) PAX terminal, i.e. the S920 that sits in this base.

entries.title: NPM (No Paper Mode)
steps: NPM means No Paper Mode: the terminal has no receipt paper or the paper is not inserted correctly.
Load the paper correctly.
You can remove NPM from the screen, but then the terminal processes transactions without a receipt.

entries.title: Clear NPM / set No Paper Mode to Auto (Android terminal)
steps: Open the payment app.
Press Func.
Choose Settings.
Choose Operation Settings.
Choose No Paper Mode.
Choose Auto.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Clear NPM / set No Paper Mode to Auto (traditional terminal)
steps: Go to Menu.
Choose Operation Settings.
Choose No Paper Mode.
Select Auto.
entries.note: Traditional (non-Android) PAX terminal, i.e. the S920 that sits in this base.

entries.title: Reprint a receipt (Android terminal)
steps: Open the payment app.
Press Func.
Choose Reprint.
Select the option you want.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Reprint a receipt (traditional terminal)
steps: Press Func.
Choose Reprint.
Select the option you want.
entries.note: Traditional (non-Android) PAX terminal, i.e. the S920 that sits in this base.

entries.title: Terminal is locked after wrong password (traditional terminal)
steps: The lock means the password was entered incorrectly 3 times.
Power the terminal off and on again.
entries.note: Traditional (non-Android) PAX terminal, i.e. the S920 that sits in this base.

entries.title: Warning App Exception
steps: This message needs a firmware update.
PAX does firmware updates only over the phone with a Technical Support Analyst; it is not something to attempt on your own.
entries.note: PAX lists this message together with Warning App Exception / Error Lookup DNS / Error Lookup Firmware Entry / SO Open Error UAI. PAX support line in the source: 877-859-0099 option 4.

entries.title: Error Lookup DNS
steps: This message needs a firmware update.
PAX does firmware updates only over the phone with a Technical Support Analyst; it is not something to attempt on your own.
entries.note: PAX lists this message together with Warning App Exception / Error Lookup DNS / Error Lookup Firmware Entry / SO Open Error UAI. PAX support line in the source: 877-859-0099 option 4.

entries.title: Error Lookup Firmware Entry
steps: This message needs a firmware update.
PAX does firmware updates only over the phone with a Technical Support Analyst; it is not something to attempt on your own.
entries.note: PAX lists this message together with Warning App Exception / Error Lookup DNS / Error Lookup Firmware Entry / SO Open Error UAI. PAX support line in the source: 877-859-0099 option 4.

entries.title: SO Open Error UAI
steps: This message needs a firmware update.
PAX does firmware updates only over the phone with a Technical Support Analyst; it is not something to attempt on your own.
entries.note: PAX lists this message together with Warning App Exception / Error Lookup DNS / Error Lookup Firmware Entry / SO Open Error UAI. PAX support line in the source: 877-859-0099 option 4.

entries.title: Comm Err 1505, -400
steps: This is expected and normal on the latest applications.
It only says there is no RKI (Remote Key Injection) download for the terminal.
Tap the arrow to exit the message, or press Cancel.
Do not downgrade the application.

entries.title: Connect to Wi-Fi (Android terminal)
steps: Open Android Settings.
Choose WiFi.
Select your WiFi network.
Enter the WiFi password.
Confirm.

entries.title: Connect to Wi-Fi (traditional terminal)
steps: Go to Menu.
Choose Communication.
Choose WiFi.
Select the network name (SSID).
Enter the password.
Go back to the main screen.
entries.note: Traditional (non-Android) PAX terminal, i.e. the S920 that sits in this base.

entries.title: Your terminal SN does not exist in global marketplace estate list / Model Mismatched in PAXSTORE
steps: The serial number has to be sent to PAX so they can correct the PAXSTORE record.
Give support the terminal's serial number.

entries.title: Status Error / Authentication Error (First Data)
steps: This appears when the installed application is OMAHA/FDRCNV; Authentication Error relates to Datawire.
The terminal needs to be provisioned (self-registered), and the file build may need checking for accuracy.
Datawire may have to reset on their end before the terminal can be provisioned.
Provision path in the payment app: Func, Settings, Host settings, Host Register/Self register, Self-register/Provision.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Attacked
steps: The terminal has detected a hardware security problem and locked itself.
This can happen if the terminal was dropped or tampered with, or if the internal battery is damaged or needs replacing.
It cannot be fixed on site: the terminal must be sent in for repair (RMA).
Stop using the terminal and contact support.
entries.note: PAX answers 'Attacked, Triggered, or PED Tampered' as one question.

entries.title: Triggered
steps: The terminal has detected a hardware security problem and locked itself.
This can happen if the terminal was dropped or tampered with, or if the internal battery is damaged or needs replacing.
It cannot be fixed on site: the terminal must be sent in for repair (RMA).
Stop using the terminal and contact support.
entries.note: PAX answers 'Attacked, Triggered, or PED Tampered' as one question.

entries.title: PED Tampered
steps: The terminal has detected a hardware security problem and locked itself.
This can happen if the terminal was dropped or tampered with, or if the internal battery is damaged or needs replacing.
It cannot be fixed on site: the terminal must be sent in for repair (RMA).
Stop using the terminal and contact support.
entries.note: PAX answers 'Attacked, Triggered, or PED Tampered' as one question.

entries.title: Payment app update is not going through
steps: Close the batch on the terminal: in most cases an update to the payment app is blocked until the batch is closed.
Try the update again.
entries.note: Downgrades and firmware updates are covered separately by PAX and need support.

entries.title: Firmware update fails: version jump too large
steps: A firmware update should go to a version close to the current one.
PAX says about 5 to 7 versions ahead is safe; more than that will likely fail.
Firmware updates are done with technical support.

entries.title: Close the batch
steps: If the terminal is used with a point of sale, close the batch from the POS itself.
On a stand-alone terminal, press Function.
Select Batch.
Select Batch Close.
The terminal prints a batch report if it worked, or shows an error message if it did not.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Tips are not showing correctly
steps: Tips are switched on in the terminal's file build: tips enabled under the EDC tab and Tip 1 enabled under the Tip tab.
The rest depends on how the tips should be configured, so support has to set it.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Invalid Batch Seq
steps: It means the batch number on the terminal does not match the batch number the processor expects.
Press Function.
Choose Settings.
Choose Host settings.
Choose Batch number.
Increase it by 1 and confirm.
Repeat if the first number does not work.
The processor can also tell you the exact batch number.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Partial approval: what it is
steps: A partial approval happens when the card does not have enough funds for the full amount, so only the available amount is approved.
Take another form of payment for the difference.
For prepaid gift cards the remaining card balance prints on the receipt.
This is controlled by the host and required by the card brands; it cannot be disabled.

entries.title: Turn off Partial Approval
steps: Partial approval is controlled by the card issuer's bank and cannot be turned off.
The file build can be set to show a prompt asking whether to reverse a partially approved transaction instead of continuing (Reversal prompt for partial approval, under the Misc. tab).
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Remove or force the PIN prompt
steps: The terminal cannot force a PIN prompt: the card-issuing bank decides whether a PIN is required.
PIN bypass can be set in the file build (EMV tab) to User Bypass, Auto Bypass or Disabled.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Cannot void a transaction
steps: A void only works while the transaction is in the current open batch.
If the batch has been closed, process a Refund/Return instead.
To void: choose the transaction type Credit/Debit.
Select V/Sale.
Enter the transaction number.
Confirm or press Enter.
A receipt confirming the void prints.
entries.note: PAX's FAQ does not name the payment application; the Func/Settings menu it describes is PAX's own payment app (BroadPOS on our terminals). Another app may differ.

entries.title: Surcharge fee is not applied to a card
steps: Surcharge applies only to credit transactions made with a true credit card.
The chip reader identifies the card: if it has a Debit AID, no surcharge is applied.

entries.title: Questions about a transaction or batch
steps: PAX refers transaction and batch inquiries to the processor.

entries.title: APN questions (cellular)
steps: PAX refers APN questions to the SIM card provider.

entries.title: Warranty on PAX products
steps: Warranty details vary.
Contact your terminal service provider for warranty information.

entries.title: Email a receipt to the customer
steps: PAX payment applications do not email receipts.
Emailing depends on a third-party POS application in or connected to the terminal.

entries.title: Debit, EBT, FSA, HSA or eWIC
steps: Debit and EBT can be processed on an encrypted terminal.
FSA, HSA or eWIC payments work only when the terminal is attached to a POS that can send the authorization information for those payments.

entries.title: Sales tax on the terminal
steps: Sales tax is calculated separately on a point of sale, which sends the total to the payment application.
Some applications support a prompt for tax in the transaction; the tax then prints on the receipt and on the batch report.

entries.title: Connection options on a PAX Android terminal
steps: All PAX Android devices support Wireless and Wi-Fi.
LAN, dial or Bluetooth depend on the model's specifications or accessories.

entries.title: PAX repair (RMA) and warranty check
steps: PAX offers a warranty status check and a Return Material Authorization (RMA) repair request.
The request asks for the terminal number, the serial number and a description of the issue.

entries.title: PAX support hours
steps: PAX's own support is open Monday to Friday, 9am to 6pm Eastern, excluding US federal holidays.

entries.title: Something is missing from the box
steps: Check the box contents after unpacking.
If any component is missing, contact the dealer who supplied the terminal.

entries.title: Prepare the battery before first use (remove the white tab)
steps: Open the battery cover on the bottom of the terminal.
Take out the battery.
Find the white tab on the battery and peel it back carefully until it is fully removed and the POGO pins are visible.

entries.title: Swipe a magnetic stripe card
steps: Slide the card through the reader slot, left to right or right to left, with the magnetic stripe facing the body of the device.
Make sure the card is fully in the reader while swiping.

entries.title: Insert a chip card
steps: Insert the card fully into the reader with the metallic contacts facing up and towards the device.
Make sure the card is fully inserted.

entries.title: Tap a contactless card or phone
steps: Hold the card or device roughly within an inch of the contactless reader.
For best results hold it as close as possible and centred over the indicated area.

entries.title: Clean the device
steps: Do not use industrial strength or abrasive cleaner; it may damage or scratch the screen.
Do not immerse the device in water or liquid.
Do not spray water or cleaner into the card reader or ports.
To clean the screen, put distilled water or mild glass cleaner on a soft, lint-free cloth and wipe gently.

entries.title: Battery is deformed or damaged
steps: Stop using the battery immediately.
Replace it.

entries.title: Battery lasts only half as long as when new
steps: If the working time is only half that of a new battery, the battery may be at the end of its life.
Replace the battery.

entries.title: Battery charging rules
steps: Do not charge for more than 24 hours at a time.
If the battery is out of power, recharge it and then disconnect the device.
Recharge the battery at least once every 6 months.
Replace the battery every two years.
Use only the specified battery model and charger.

entries.title: A cable is damaged
steps: If any cable becomes damaged, get a replacement.

entries.title: Repairs
steps: Do not attempt repairs yourself.
If repairs are required, contact a professional technician.

entries.title: Tap on the A920MAX

entries.title: Tear off a receipt (A920MAX)

Do not touch the print head after printing.

Keep it away from heat sources, water, direct sunlight and dust.

steps: Switch off the printer's power before connecting or disconnecting any port.

steps: Replace the power cord immediately.

steps: Never carry out maintenance or repair work yourself.

entries.title: Elys Printer print quality is poor
steps: Dust, adhesive or other dirt on the print head or inside the printer can degrade print quality.
Turn the printer off and wait about 2 to 3 minutes for the head to cool.
Open the printer cover.
Clean the print head with the cleaning pen, from the centre of the head out to the edges.
Wait 1 to 2 minutes until the alcohol has evaporated and the printer is completely dry before using it.

entries.title: Elys Printer: paper not detected or print degraded (clean sensors, roller, paper path)
steps: Turn the printer off.
Open the printer cover and remove the paper.
Remove dust or foreign matter with a dry cloth or cotton swab.
Use a cloth or swab soaked in medical alcohol to remove sticky dirt.
Wait 1 to 2 minutes until the alcohol has evaporated and the printer is dry.
Clean these parts whenever print quality or paper detection gets worse.

steps: Switch off the printer's power supply when it will not be used for a long time.

entries.title: Connect the A35 to Ethernet
steps: Select the menu icon in the upper left corner.
Select DEVICE SETTINGS and enter the merchant password if prompted.
Select ETHERNET CONFIGURATION.
Choose your network and configure the settings.
Return to the Start screen when connected.

entries.title: Run a credit or debit sale (A35)
steps: Tap the CARD icon on the Start screen.
Enter the amount and confirm.
If tips are on, enter and confirm the tip in the second window.
The customer uses their card or contactless payment.
If the terminal declines the transaction, retry.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build. This flow (CARD icon, Start screen) is not the BroadPOS FUNC layout; it describes the reseller's build.

entries.title: Run a manual-entry sale (A35)
steps: Tap the CARD icon.
Enter the amount.
Use MANUAL ENTRY to key in the card number, expiration date and CVV.
Confirm the total with the GREEN button.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: A35 has no printer
steps: The A35 has no built-in printer; customer receipts cannot be printed or reprinted from it.

entries.title: Refund (A35)
steps: Tap the MENU icon and enter your merchant password.
Select CREDIT and enter the merchant password.
Enter the refund amount.
The customer presents the card or contactless method to be refunded.
For a keyed refund, select MANUAL ENTRY and enter the card number, CVV and validity period, then confirm the amount.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Void a transaction (A35)
steps: Use the payment method that was used for the payment.
Select the MENU icon.
Select CANCEL.
Enter your merchant password.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Close the batch (A35, Reports menu)
steps: Select the MENU icon.
Select REPORTS.
Select END OF DAY SETTLEMENT.
The day's transactions are sent and the display shows a confirmation.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Change the date and time (A35)
steps: Select the GEAR icon to open settings.
Scroll down to SYSTEM.
Tap DATE & TIME.
Turn off the automatic date and time toggle.
Tap SELECT TIME ZONE and choose your time zone.
Select SET DATE and set the date.
Select SET TIME and set the time.

entries.title: How the A35 gets its software and keys
steps: Over Wi-Fi the terminal connects to PAXSTORE, PAX's terminal management system.
It installs the necessary software and encryption keys automatically.
A brief sound indicates the installation is in progress, and the screen shows what is being downloaded.
entries.note: The source mentions a 'STEAM system' and TPN, which belong to a different reseller's set-up, not ours.

entries.title: Find the A35's IP address
steps: After setting up WiFi, select ADVANCED and scroll up.
The network settings are shown.
Write down the IP address.

entries.title: Change the A35 settings password
steps: In the Device section of settings, tap PASSWORD.
Follow the prompts.

entries.title: Find the A35 serial number
steps: Turn the device over and look for the sticker on the bottom.

entries.title: Transaction Error: Connect Error
steps: Switch to an Ethernet connection and try again.

Other causes sit in the BroadPOS settings: the POS register setting (communications tab) is not turned on, the protocol type is not TCP/IP, or the primary communication type is not LAN. Those need support.
entries.note: Message seen when the A35 is driven by a POS running BroadPOS (named in the source).

entries.title: Transaction Error: invalid card reader counter
steps: The PAX needs to be updated (the source says to v1.11).
entries.note: Message seen when the A35 is driven by a POS running BroadPOS (named in the source).

entries.title: Transaction failed: Fail to obtain approval for online transaction
steps: The terminal could not obtain approval for the online transaction.
The source gives no fix.
entries.note: Message seen when the A35 is driven by a POS running BroadPOS (named in the source).

entries.title: 000100 (Decline); Message: SEQ ERR PLS CALL
steps: The batch has to be forced through by the payment processor.
No need to purge the terminal; it already shows 0.00.
entries.note: Message seen when the A35 is driven by a POS running BroadPOS (named in the source).

entries.title: Invalid msg fmt
steps: This can appear if the card was swiped too fast, or the card's magnetic stripe is worn out: try the card again.
It can also mean a terminal ID or other VAR-sheet value was entered incorrectly in the configuration; that needs support.
entries.note: Message seen when the A35 is driven by a POS running BroadPOS (named in the source). If it keeps happening with different cards, escalate to tech (configuration cause).

entries.title: There is no default payment device
steps: Sync your register completely and try again.
If that does not solve it, press the I icon and tap RESTART.
entries.note: Message seen when the A35 is driven by a POS running BroadPOS (named in the source). This message comes from the POS register, not the A35 itself.

entries.title: PAX error - Check Lan Cable
steps: Check that a LAN cable is plugged into the PAX device.
The black connector cable from the PAX device may be defective.
entries.note: Message seen when the A35 is driven by a POS running BroadPOS (named in the source).

entries.title: PAX error - RECV ACK ERROR
steps: Do not open the PAX menu while a transaction is being sent.
It also appears when communication between the POS and the PAX cannot be established.
entries.note: Message seen when the A35 is driven by a POS running BroadPOS (named in the source).

entries.title: PED Tamper
steps: The terminal's tamper sensor was tripped, possibly during shipping.
The device must be returned to the provider and replaced.
entries.note: Message seen when the A35 is driven by a POS running BroadPOS (named in the source).

entries.title: PAX error - so open error uai
steps: The PAX device requires an update.
Contact support.
entries.note: Message seen when the A35 is driven by a POS running BroadPOS (named in the source).

entries.title: A35 is not turning on or not working
steps: Reboot: hold the red and green buttons together until the terminal turns off, and keep holding until it powers on.
Unplug the power cord and plug it back in.
Make sure the network cable is connected to the terminal and to a network jack or hub.
If it still does not work, contact support.
entries.note: The source also lists a LAN-type check via 'F and 1' which is a traditional-terminal menu; left to tech.

entries.title: Connect the A30 to Ethernet
steps: Connect an Ethernet cable from the LAN port on the terminal's back plate to your network.
With DHCP no other steps are needed; Ethernet with DHCP is on by default.

entries.title: Refund (A30)
steps: Open the payment application.
Tap CREDIT, DEBIT or CASH to match the original payment.
Tap REFUND.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build. The source gives only these three taps.

entries.title: Void a credit sale (A30)
steps: Open the payment application.
Tap CREDIT.
Tap VOID SALE.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: A30 has no printer
steps: The A30 has no built-in printer.
PAX sells the Elys printer, which can be paired with terminals through Bluetooth or Wi-Fi.

entries.title: Turn the Aries8 on or off
steps: To power on, hold the power button on the right side for three to five seconds; the screen lights up.
To power off, hold the same button for three to five seconds.

entries.title: Connect the Aries8 to Ethernet
steps: Plug the Ethernet cable into the terminal's LAN port and into the router (this uses the optional Ethernet charging base).
Select the BACK ARROW from the home screen.
Select SETTINGS.
Select WIRELESS & NETWORKS or NETWORK & INTERNET.
Select ETHERNET.
Select DHCP for automatic set-up (the default), or STATIC to enter the gateway, DNS and IP address.
Select CONNECT.

entries.title: Connect the Aries8 to Wi-Fi
steps: Select the BACK ARROW from the home screen.
Select SETTINGS (you may be asked for the Aries8 password).
Select WIRELESS & NETWORKS or NETWORK & INTERNET.
Select WIFI and make sure it is toggled on.
Select your network and enter its password.
Select CONNECT.

entries.title: Aries8 has no printer
steps: The Aries8 has no built-in receipt printer.
It must be connected to an external printer to print receipts or daily reports.

entries.title: Run a chip credit sale (Aries8)
steps: From the home screen select SALE.
If prompted, select BANK CARD or CREDIT.
Enter the amount.
Insert the chip card with the chip facing up.
The terminal shows AUTHORIZING TRANSACTION, then a confirmation.
The customer removes the card when prompted and may be asked to sign.
Print a receipt if wanted.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Run a manual-entry credit sale (Aries8)
steps: From the home screen select SALE.
If prompted, select BANK CARD or CREDIT.
Enter the amount.
If prompted, select MANUAL ENTRY.
Enter the card number, expiration date, CVV and any other card details asked for.
Select AUTHORIZE.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Run a debit sale (Aries8)
steps: From the home screen select SALE.
If prompted, select BANK CARD or DEBIT.
Enter the amount.
Insert the chip card chip-up, or tap the card over the contactless reader.
The cardholder enters the PIN and may need to confirm the amount.
Wait for the confirmation message.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Void a credit transaction (Aries8)
steps: From the home screen select BANK CARD or CREDIT.
Find and select VOID.
Select the transaction to void, then CONFIRM.
Print a receipt if wanted.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Refund to a credit card (Aries8)
steps: From the home screen select FUNC.
Select REFUND.
Choose to refund by CARD NUMBER or by TRANSACTION REFERENCE NUMBER (the transaction ID on the original receipt).
If prompted, select BANK CARD or CREDIT.
Enter the refund amount and confirm.
Tap, swipe, insert or key in the card.
If prompted, enter the server ID or authorization details.
Confirm; print a receipt if wanted.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Refund to a debit card (Aries8)
steps: From the home screen select FUNC.
Select REFUND.
Choose to refund by CARD NUMBER or by TRANSACTION REFERENCE NUMBER.
If prompted, select BANK CARD or DEBIT.
Enter the refund amount and confirm.
Swipe or insert the card; enter the PIN if prompted.
Confirm; print a receipt if wanted.
entries.note: The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Change the date and time (Aries8)
steps: The date and time are normally set automatically.
To set them by hand: select the BACK ARROW from the main screen and enter the password.
Select SETTINGS (enter the password again if asked).
Under SYSTEM select DATE & TIME.
Turn off AUTOMATIC DATE & TIME and AUTOMATIC TIME ZONE.
Select SET DATE, then SET TIME.

entries.title: Adjust the volume (Aries8)
steps: From the home screen select SETTINGS.
Select SOUND.
Select DEVICE VOLUME.
Adjust as needed.

entries.title: Adjust brightness (Aries8)
steps: From the home screen select SETTINGS.
Select DISPLAY.
Select BRIGHTNESS LEVEL.
Select ADAPTIVE BRIGHTNESS.

entries.title: Aries8 will not turn on
steps: Make sure the Aries8 has been charged enough.
Plug it into its power source; the battery charge shows on the screen as it charges.
If it still will not turn on, leave it connected to power, wait a few minutes and press the power button again.

entries.title: Reboot the Aries8
steps: Press and hold the power button.
Select RESTART when it appears on screen.

entries.title: Factory reset (Aries8)
steps: A factory reset erases all data on the device, including transaction history and customised settings.
Source path: SETTINGS, the device password, BACKUP & RESET, FACTORY DATA RESET, RESET PHONE, ERASE EVERYTHING.
Do not do this without support.
entries.note: Marked not for merchants: the reset wipes the terminal. 'Do not do this without support' is our routing.

entries.title: Load a paper roll (S920)
steps: Open the paper compartment release lever.
Place the thermal paper roll in the compartment.
Leave a little paper hanging out, close the compartment and tear off the excess.
Make sure the lid is completely closed before use.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base).

entries.title: Turn the S920 on or off
steps: Press and hold the red X button for about three to five seconds, then release.
The terminal performs a self-test when it starts.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base).

entries.title: Run a ping test (S920)
steps: Connect to your WiFi network first.
In the WiFi parameters select PING.
Check the address shown and press ENTER.
The result of the ping test shows on screen.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base).

entries.title: Install a SIM card (S920)
steps: Remove the SIM socket cover on the back of the terminal.
Carefully remove the battery.
Insert the SIM card into its slot.
Re-attach the cover.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base).

entries.title: Turn on No Paper Mode (S920)
steps: From the main menu select OPERATION SETTINGS.
Select NO PAPER MODE.
Enter the password if prompted.
Select YES to confirm.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base).

entries.title: Run a credit sale (S920)
steps: Select CREDIT.
Select SALE.
Enter the amount and confirm.
The cardholder taps, swipes or inserts the card.
A receipt prints on approval.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base). The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Run a manual-entry credit sale (S920)
steps: Select CREDIT.
Select SALE.
Enter the amount and confirm.
Key in the card number, expiration date, CVV and possibly the billing zip code.
A receipt prints on approval.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base). The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Run a debit sale (S920)
steps: Select DEBIT.
Select SALE.
Enter the amount and confirm.
The cardholder swipes or inserts the card and enters the PIN.
A receipt prints on approval.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base). The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Reprint a receipt (S920)
steps: On the main menu select REPRINT.
Choose the last transaction or a specific one; you may be asked for MERCHANT COPY or CUSTOMER COPY.
The receipt reprints.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base). The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Refund to a credit card (S920)
steps: Select CREDIT.
Select RETURN or REFUND.
Enter the amount and confirm.
The cardholder taps, swipes or inserts the card.
Receipts print on approval.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base). The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

steps: Select DEBIT.
Select RETURN or REFUND.
Enter the amount and confirm.
The cardholder swipes or inserts the card and enters the PIN.
Receipts print on approval.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base). The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Void a transaction (S920)
steps: If prompted, select FUNC.
Select VOID or V SALE.
Select the type of transaction: DEBIT, CREDIT, etc.
Enter the transaction number from the original receipt.
Check the details and press the green button.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base). The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Print a report (S920)
steps: Select FUNC.
Select REPORT.
Select PRINT.
Alternatively select REPORT and enter the password; the default report prints automatically.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base). The source does not name the payment application; its menus (FUNC, Batch, Reports) match PAX BroadPOS. Steps can differ on another application or build.

entries.title: Turn on Battery Saver (S920)
steps: Select ENTER.
Press 1.
Select OPERATION SETTINGS.
Select BATTERY SAVER.
Choose the operation mode: OFF or AUTO OFF.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base).

entries.title: Make the S920 check for updates by restarting it
steps: Make sure the S920 is connected to WiFi.
Turn the terminal off and wait ten seconds.
Turn it back on; it checks for updates automatically on restart.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base).

entries.title: PED TAMPERED (S920)
steps: Do not select any on-screen options.
Do not attempt to fix the problem yourself.
Contact support to get a replacement terminal.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base).

entries.title: S920 touchscreen is unresponsive
steps: Make sure the device is dry and has not been damaged by liquid.
Make sure the terminal is not near any magnetic devices.
If the problem persists, contact support.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base).

entries.title: Factory reset (S920)
steps: Do not factory reset on your own: the source strongly advises doing it only with the merchant service provider's help.
A factory reset erases all data, including transaction history and customised settings.
entries.note: From PaymentCloud's guide to the S920 terminal (the traditional, non-Android terminal that sits in this base).

entries.title: Fit and activate a SIM card (A920 Pro)
steps: Slide the latch on the back to the right and lift off the battery cover.
Lift the battery out from the bottom.
Place the mini-SIM card into the SIM1 slot (usually the left one).
Put the battery back and secure the cover.
Hold the power button for 2 to 4 seconds to turn the terminal on.
Go to Settings.
Select Wireless & Networks or Cellular Settings.
Make sure Mobile Data is turned on.
A cellular signal icon shows in the top header once active.

entries.title: Connect the A920 Pro to Wi-Fi
steps: Select the Settings app on the idle screen.
Enter the Settings password, select the green check button and select OK.
Turn Wi-Fi on.
Select the network.
Enter the Wi-Fi password and select connect.

entries.title: Wi-Fi network is not in the list (A920 Pro)
steps: In the Wi-Fi screen select the 3 dots in the top right corner.
Select Add Network.
Enter the network name (SSID) and select the security type.
Enter the Wi-Fi password and select Save.

entries.title: Change the paper roll (A920 Pro)
steps: Turn the device over.
Pull the paper cover latch away from the device; the top section pivots down.
Pull the old roll out.
Insert the new roll with the paper poking out of the top of the device, in the orientation shown in the holder.
Close the lid until it snaps into place and is fully closed.
Tear off any excess paper.

entries.title: Power the A920 Pro on
steps: Press and hold the power button for three seconds until the screen powers on.
entries.note: PAX's own guide says 3 to 5 seconds.

entries.title: Power the A920 Pro off
steps: Press and hold the power button for three seconds until the power menu shows.
Tap Power off.
Tap Power off again; a 'shutting down' message shows.

entries.title: Sleep or wake the A920 Pro
steps: Click the power button once to put the device to sleep or wake it.

entries.title: Run a sale (A920 Pro, Paysafe build)
steps: From the main menu choose Sale.
Key in the amount and select Done.
When prompted to Tap, Swipe or Insert, have the customer tap on the contactless reader, swipe through the magstripe reader or insert into the card reader.
entries.note: Paysafe help-centre article for Paysafe's own build; the application is not named and its menu (Sale / Refund / Admin) may differ from BroadPOS on our terminals.

entries.title: Run a refund (A920 Pro, Paysafe build)
steps: From the main menu choose Refund.
Key in the refund amount and select Done.
When prompted, have the customer tap, swipe or insert the card.
entries.note: Paysafe help-centre article for Paysafe's own build; the application is not named and its menu may differ from BroadPOS on our terminals.

entries.title: Print an X report / end of shift (A920 Pro, Paysafe build)
steps: From the main menu swipe across to the Admin menu.
Choose X Report (End of Shift).
The report prints; an X report can be taken at any time and does not zero the totals.
entries.note: Paysafe help-centre article for Paysafe's own build; the Admin menu / X Report is not the BroadPOS FUNC > Reports layout.

entries.title: Invalid batch sequence error (A80, Paysafe steps)
steps: It usually means a mismatch, often an open batch from the previous day or a problem at batch close.
Try closing the batch manually: FUNC, BATCH, BATCH CLOSE.
Check the Ethernet or Wi-Fi connection.
If one transaction is the problem: void it if unsettled, refund it if settled.
Other fixes in the source (clear the batch under System Settings > Database; change the Device ID or batch number) are for support.
entries.note: PAX's own FAQ fixes this by raising the batch number by 1 under Function > Settings > Host settings. Clearing the batch deletes transactions, so we route it to tech.

entries.title: Terminal freezes or crashes
steps: Hold down the power button until the terminal powers off.
Wait a few seconds, then press the power button again to restart.
Make sure the device is charged or plugged in; if it uses a charging base, check the base is connected to power.
If it still happens, check the internet connection (Wi-Fi, Ethernet or cellular) and reconnect or restart the network.
If the terminal has a built-in printer, open the lid and check for a paper jam or misfeed.
If restarting does not fix it, contact support with the terminal model, a description of the issue and any error messages on the screen.
entries.note: General Paysafe article for all terminal brands, not PAX-specific.

entries.title: Paradise POS tech support: phone, after-hours line and email
steps: During business hours call Paradise at 877-777-5530.
After hours and at weekends call 877-777-5530 and use extension 1.
You can also email tech support at support@paradisepos.com.

entries.title: Paradise asks merchants to work through its troubleshooting steps before calling
steps: Work through the troubleshooting steps for your problem first.
If the equipment still is not working after all the steps, call Paradise Tech Support at (877) 777-5530.

entries.title: First-time Paradise setup must be booked with the Paradise training team
steps: If you are setting up the equipment for the first time, schedule your installation and training with the Paradise training team.
Do not rely on the tech support line for an unscheduled install: Paradise says tech support is not meant for unscheduled installation and training sessions.
The booking link printed in the manual is https://calendly.com/paradise-pos-installation-and-training.

entries.title: Paradise POS video tutorials (official list)
steps: Open the Paradise tech support page at paradisepos.com/techsupport.html.

Pick the tutorial you need: drawers, register mode, scheduled discounts, items, employees and roles, tip-outs, tip adjustment and shift report, company settings, reports, voiding a ticket, ticket and drawer recall, refunding a payment, transferring items.
The same page has a Download Manual button for the full user guide.

entries.title: Set up the Titan 3000 cellular router
steps: Run an Ethernet cord from your modem to the WAN port of the cellular router.
Plug the router into a power outlet with the included adapter and turn on the power switch.
Wait for the SYS light to change from orange to green, which means startup has finished.
The router connects to the strongest available signal by itself.
Use the remaining LAN ports to connect switches that run the network to your stations.

entries.title: Set up the Plasma Cloud PA2200 access point
steps: Find the PoE injector, a small rectangular box with a power port and two Ethernet ports.
Run an Ethernet cord from your router or modem to the LAN port of the PoE injector.
Run a second Ethernet cord from the PoE port of the injector to the port marked 54V PoE - Ethernet 2 on the access point.
Plug the power cord into the PoE injector. The injector powers the access point.

entries.title: Install the Epson TMU220 kitchen printer
steps: Connect an Ethernet cord to the 10/100Base-TX port on the printer and connect the power cord.
Open the paper tray and load kitchen printer paper following the instructions inside the tray.
Turn the printer on with the power toggle switch and wait for a green light.
Within about a minute the printer should print a short settings page. Keep it: it shows the MAC address and IP address.
In the Paradise app go to Admin > Printer Maintenance and pick the kitchen printer in the list on the left, or create a new one.
Name the printer, select Printer Model and choose Epson Thermal.
Select the scan button and pick the MAC address that matches your printed slip, or type the IP address in by hand.
Select Save, then select Test Print. A test slip should print.

entries.title: Epson TMU220: print the status sheet to find the printer's IP and MAC address
steps: If the settings page did not print when the printer was turned on, use a pen or paper clip to press and hold the reset button on the back of the printer for 5 seconds.
The printer prints a sheet listing its details.
Find the MAC address and IP address on that sheet.

entries.title: Install the Epson TM30 receipt printer (Ethernet)
steps: Take off both interchangeable plates on the printer casing so you can reach the ports.
Connect an Ethernet cord to the Ethernet port.
If you use a cash drawer, plug the end of the drawer cord labeled Printer into the printer's Cash Drawer port.
If you use a USB scanner at this station, plug it into the USB-A port.
Connect the power cord to the 24V power port, decide whether paper loads from the top or the front, and put the plates back with the rubber-bumper plate on the base.
Load thermal paper following the instructions inside the tray and turn on the printer.
Keep the short configuration slip the printer prints.
In the Paradise app go to Admin > Printer Maintenance, pick the receipt printer or create a new one, choose Printer Model Epson Thermal, and enter the IP address from the slip in Address.
Select Save, then Test Print. A test slip should print.

entries.title: Install the Epson TM30 receipt printer (USB)
steps: Take off both plates on the printer casing to reach the ports.
Connect the USB cord from the Paradise device to the port labeled iPad 2.1A on the back of the printer.
If you use a cash drawer, plug the end of the drawer cord labeled Printer into the printer's Cash Drawer port.
If you use a USB scanner, plug it into the USB-A port.
Connect power to the 24V power port, refit the plates, load thermal paper and turn the printer on.
In the Paradise app go to Admin > Printer Maintenance and pick the receipt printer or create a new one.
In the Printer Owner list select the device marked (This Device) so the printer is assigned to the device you are using.
Select Save, then Test Print. A test slip should print.

entries.title: Card terminals do not work with Paradise until Paradise support has connected them
steps: You can physically install the card terminal yourself (power, network).
The terminal will not work with the Paradise app until the Paradise support team has helped with the installation.
Schedule the installation with Paradise.

entries.title: Prepare a PAX A35 for Paradise
steps: The A35 comes with a communication cable that supplies both power and internet.
On that cable, connect power and run an Ethernet cord from your modem or router to the LAN port.
Remove the back cover of the terminal and plug the communication cable into the Type-C port.
The terminal powers on by itself.
Paradise support then connects the terminal to the Paradise station.

entries.title: Set up a Castles V3000 for Paradise
steps: Turn the device screen-down. The back has an Ethernet port, a power port and a cord management latch above them.
Unhook the latch to make room for the cords.
Run an Ethernet cord from your router to the Ethernet port.
Plug the supplied power cable into a wall outlet and then into the device, and close the latch over the cords.
The device powers on when the adapter is plugged in.
Open the Paradise application and log in.

entries.title: Connect the POS X EVO 2D USB scanner
steps: Plug the scanner's USB cord into the port labeled USB on the back of your receipt printer.
Connect the printer following the instructions for that printer.
Open the Paradise app and log in.
Scan a barcode. The app should either ring up the item or prompt you to create a new item. If it does, the scanner is connected.

entries.title: POS X Bluetooth scanner is not scanning: check the Bluetooth connection
steps: Make sure the scanner is turned on, in range and fully charged. It should already be paired when you receive it.
On the Paradise device, open the Settings app and open Bluetooth settings.
Make sure Bluetooth is turned on and connected to the scanner.
If the scanner is not connected, select it in the list to connect it.
Open the Paradise app, log in and scan a barcode. The app should ring up the item or prompt you to create a new item.

entries.title: Connect a Paradise station by cable with the hardwire kit
steps: Connect the USB power cord to the USB port on the hardwire kit.
Run an Ethernet cord from your modem or router to the Ethernet port on the hardwire kit.
Connect the power cord on the hardwire kit to the Paradise device.
Open the Settings app on the Paradise device and turn Wi-Fi off.
If the device shows a separate Ethernet section, the hardwire kit is connected properly.

entries.title: Set up the Paradise kitchen display (KDS) tablet
steps: Ethernet model: run an Ethernet cord from your modem or router to the tablet's Ethernet port. Wi-Fi model: attach the Wi-Fi antenna if it is not already attached.
Connect power and turn on the device.
Open the Google browser. It should already be on the right page; if not, go to paradiseposkds.com.
The device should connect to your database automatically.
If it shows a setup screen instead, contact Paradise support to schedule your installation.

entries.title: Connect and test the KB9000 bump bar
steps: Plug the bump bar into either USB port on the KDS tablet.
On the KDS, use the arrows to change the highlighted ticket, or use the bump bar buttons to bump a test ticket.

entries.title: Set up the Star MG-T60 scale
steps: Plug the scale into power and turn it on.
The scale should already be connected to the Paradise device.
To test, ring up an item that has been set up to require the scale.

entries.title: Set up the Zebra ZD411 label printer and load labels
steps: Run an Ethernet cord from your modem or router to the Ethernet port on the back of the label printer.
Connect the supplied power cord.
To load labels, slide the release latches to the front to unlock the cover.
Spread the roll holders open and place the roll in the printer.
Check the roll turns freely and does not sit on the bottom of the media compartment.
Pull the end of the roll past the front edge of the printer.

entries.title: Log in or clock in on Paradise (employee number or swipe card)
steps: On the login screen, type your personal employee number on the keypad to clock in or out and to log in or out.
If your business uses swipe cards, select Swipe and swipe your card on the card terminal connected to the station.

entries.title: Add a new employee login in Paradise
steps: Go to the Admin tab and select Employee Maintenance.
Select New Employee at the top right.
Enter the first and last name, a unique password and a role. These are the only required fields.
To assign the role, select the small plus sign next to Roles and choose a role.
Save the changes.

entries.title: An employee cannot clock in or get into Paradise: check the Active box
steps: Go to Admin > Employee Maintenance and select the employee.
Check the Active setting. If it is deselected the employee is disabled and cannot clock in or access the system.
Select Active again to re-enable the employee and save.

entries.title: Stations behaving oddly: check every device is on the same Paradise software version
steps: Look at the software version shown on the login page of each station.
All stations should be on the same version.
Different versions on devices that share one database can cause operating issues.

entries.title: Start or end an unpaid break
steps: On the login screen, type your employee number first.
Then select Start Break or End Break.
Your open tickets stay under your employee number while you are on break; break hours are not tracked on the payroll report.

entries.title: Send an order to the kitchen (Send, Quick Pay, Fast Send, Print & Send)
steps: Send: sends unsent items to the kitchen and clears the ticket from view.
Quick Pay: skips the usual prompts and goes straight to the payment screen.
Fast Send: sends unsent items but keeps the ticket open so you can keep adding items.
Print & Send: prints a receipt and sends unsent items at the same time.
Once items are sent they can no longer be deleted; they must be voided if a change is needed.

entries.title: Take a card payment on Paradise
steps: Open the ticket and tap Pay at the bottom left to reach the Payment Screen.
Tap Credit. The customer is prompted to pay on the connected card terminal.
When the transaction completes, the credit card receipts print automatically.
Choose the receipt option when asked: No Print, Email or Print.

entries.title: Take a cash payment on Paradise
steps: Open the ticket and tap Pay.
Enter the amount received on the keypad, or tap one of the preset bill amounts.
Tap Cash.
The cash drawer opens and the screen shows the change due and the receipt options.

entries.title: Take a gift card payment on Paradise
steps: Open the ticket and tap Pay, then Gift Card.
The terminal prompts the customer to use their gift card.
If the card balance does not cover the full amount, the system shows what is still owed so you can pick another payment method for the rest.

entries.title: Why the Paradise payment screen shows two totals (Total and Cash Total)
steps: If the business uses cash discount or dual pricing, two values show on the payment screen.
Total is the full ticket price.
Cash Total is the price if the customer pays in cash.

entries.title: Receipt choices after a payment: No Print, Email or Print
steps: After the payment completes, choose No Print, Email or Print.
No Print closes the ticket without a receipt. You can still find the ticket in Ticket Recall and print it from there.
Email asks for an email address to send the receipt to.
Print sends the receipt to the printer assigned to the device. If no printer is assigned, you are asked to pick one.

entries.title: Reprint a receipt on Paradise
steps: Go to the Manager page and select Ticket Recall.
Use the filters on the left (customer or tab name, ticket ID, employee, date range, price range, SKU or item name) to find the ticket. Ticket Recall covers the past month.
Select the ticket to open the Ticket Admin screen.
Select Print Ticket to print another copy of the receipt.

entries.title: Hold an item so it does not go to the kitchen yet
steps: Swipe left to right on the item in the ticket and select Hold.
The item stays on the ticket but is not sent to the kitchen.
To release it, reopen the ticket, swipe on the item again and select Remove Hold, then send the ticket.

entries.title: Transfer a ticket or an item to another employee or ticket
steps: Swipe left to right on an item and select Transfer. The employee needs transfer permission.
Choose To Employee to move the whole ticket to another clocked-in employee.
Choose To Ticket to move the whole ticket onto another existing ticket.
Choose Item to move a single item to another ticket.
The ticket or item must already be sent before it can be merged or moved.

entries.title: Void or comp a single item
steps: Open the ticket.
The item must already be sent. Unsent items can only be deleted.
Swipe the item from right to left.
Tap Comp or Void.
Select a reason from the preset list, or select Other and type one.

entries.title: Void or comp: which one to use
steps: Use a void when an item or ticket was entered by mistake, usually before the customer received the product.
Use a comp when the customer already received the item or ticket but the business is covering it, for example for food quality or service concerns.
Voids and comps are tracked separately in reports.

entries.title: Void a whole ticket
steps: Open the ticket and tap Void Ticket in the bottom-left corner, or go to the Payment Screen and tap Void Ticket at the bottom.
Follow the on-screen prompts.
Select a void reason.

entries.title: Comp a whole ticket
steps: Open the ticket.
Go to the Payment Screen.
Select Comp Ticket from the payment options.
Follow the prompts and select a comp reason.

entries.title: Open a cash drawer at the start of the day
steps: The first employee with drawer access who clocks in is prompted to open the drawer; select Yes. Otherwise go to the Employee screen and select Open Cash Drawer.
Count the starting cash and enter it by denomination, for example enter 5 under $20 for five $20 bills.
Select Confirm. The drawer is now open with its starting funds.
If the physical drawer shut while you were counting, select Open Drawer at the bottom of the prompt.

entries.title: Close the cash drawer at the end of the shift or day
steps: First make sure all tickets are closed, shift reports are completed and tips are tipped out.
Go to Employee > Close Cash Drawer and select Close.
Count all the cash in the drawer, including the starting cash, and enter it by denomination. This is a blind count.
Select Confirm, check the total, and select Confirm again.
If the count is right or over, the drawer closes, a drawer report prints and a summary shows on screen.
If the drawer is short, enter a reason. A manager can recount if needed.

entries.title: Error when closing the cash drawer: tickets still open or shift reports not done
steps: The system shows an error if any tickets are still open or any shift reports are incomplete.
Close or transfer every open ticket.
Have each employee complete their shift report.
Then go back to Employee > Close Cash Drawer.

entries.title: Swap cash drawers mid-day without closing tickets
steps: Select Close Cash Drawer and choose Swap instead of Close.
Count the whole outgoing drawer and select Confirm. A drawer report prints.
Select Confirm again to move on to the next drawer.
Count the starting cash for the new drawer by denomination and select Confirm.
Every employee who will use the new drawer must select Join Drawer, or their sales will not be recorded under the new drawer.

entries.title: Join or leave a cash drawer
steps: On the Employee page select Join/Leave Drawer.
When you are joined to a drawer your sales count in that drawer's totals.
If you are not joined, your sales are recorded under your own employee number instead of the drawer.

entries.title: Record a pay in or pay out (cash added to or taken from the drawer)
steps: A cash drawer must be open on the station.
Select Pay In/Pay Out.
Enter the amount.
Type a reason, and assign a vendor if your system uses vendors.
Select Pay In or Pay Out. The drawer opens so you can put in or take out the cash.

entries.title: Check a gift card balance
steps: On the Employee page select Gift Card Balance.
Type the gift card number, or swipe the card on the connected card terminal.
The system shows the balance on the card.

entries.title: Look up an item's price (Price Check)
steps: Select Price Check.
Type the item's SKU, or scan the item if a barcode scanner is connected.

entries.title: Enter or adjust credit card tips
steps: Go to Employee > Tip Adjustment. The screen lists the credit card transactions closed under the logged-in employee.
Select the transaction: tap the blank (0.00) field under the Tip column and a number pad appears.
Type the tip amount.
Repeat for each transaction that needs a tip.
Select Save All Tips. The system then talks to the card terminal to apply the tips.

entries.title: Run an employee shift report
steps: Only run it after all your tickets are closed and all tips are adjusted. Only one shift report can be run per shift per employee.
Go to Employee > Shift Report.
Captured Tips at the top shows your credit card tips. Enter any additional declared tips, such as cash tips, in the blank field.
Select Confirm. The shift report prints and a summary shows on screen.

entries.title: Reprint an employee shift report or fix a missed clock-in or clock-out
steps: Go to the Manager page and select Shift Maintenance.
Choose By Employee and select the employee to see their shifts.
To reprint a shift report, select the shift and tap Print Report.
If an employee forgot to clock in, select New Shift to create the shift by hand.
To change clock-in or clock-out times, select a closed shift. An open shift must be closed first before it can be edited.

entries.title: Tip out an employee at the end of their shift
steps: The employee adjusts their credit card tips, closes or transfers all tickets, and runs their shift report. It reads either Employee Owes Restaurant or Restaurant Owes Employee.
Someone assigned to the drawer goes to Employee > Employee Tip Out.
Select the employee marked Has Report.
Enter the amount shown as owed in the blank field.
Tap Tip Out Employee and confirm. The drawer opens and a tip-out slip prints.
If you are tipping yourself out, answer No when asked to clock out so you keep access to the system.

entries.title: Kitchen ticket did not print: resend it to the kitchen printer
steps: Open the ticket so it shows in the ticket field.
Go to Employee > Resend Ticket.
The ticket prints again on the assigned kitchen printer.

entries.title: How to read a Paradise ticket number
steps: The first 6 digits are the date the ticket was created, as YYMMDD.
The next 3 letters are the device ID of the register that created it.
The next 4 digits are the ticket number.
The last 2 digits identify a split ticket, if there is one.

entries.title: Refund a ticket or individual items
steps: Go to Manager > Ticket Recall and find the ticket.
Select the ticket to open the Ticket Admin screen and select Refund Ticket.
To refund everything choose Refund Ticket; to refund only some items, select them and choose Refund Items.
Choose Give Gift Card to put the refund on a gift card, or Refund All Payments to refund the original payments.
For a card refund the same card must be swiped.

entries.title: Refund without the original receipt (Open Refund)
steps: Create a new ticket with the items being returned, or items matching the refund value. A generic Open Item with Prompt for Price enabled can be used if the original item is not in the system.
Check the return total on the ticket.
Select Open Refund on the Manager page.
Choose Refund Ticket to refund everything, or select items and choose Refund Items.
Choose the refund method. For a card refund the customer must have their card to swipe or insert.

entries.title: A ticket will not close: Force Close is a last resort
steps: Force Close in Ticket Recall closes a ticket without processing a payment.
Paradise describes it as a last resort, often used with tech support guidance.
Used wrongly it can cause reporting discrepancies, so call Paradise tech support before using it.

entries.title: Reopen a closed ticket
steps: Go to Manager > Ticket Recall, find the ticket and select it.
Select Reopen Ticket.
Make the adjustment, such as a void.
Be careful: reopening tickets can affect reports if misused.

entries.title: Look up a current or past cash drawer and reprint its report
steps: Go to Manager > Drawer Recall and filter by date. The To date must be later than the From date or nothing shows.
Select a drawer to see starting cash, cash payments, change given, pay ins and outs, tip ins and outs and the drawer total.
Select Print to reprint the Drawer Report.
If starting cash was entered wrongly, tap the edit icon to recount it, then select Save.

entries.title: Drawer Recall shows no results
steps: Check the date filter.
The To date must be later than the From date. If it is not, no results appear.

entries.title: A cash drawer cannot be closed the normal way: Force Close Drawer
steps: Force Close Drawer in Drawer Recall is only for a drawer that cannot be closed through standard means.
It can disrupt reporting.
Only do it with management or with help from Paradise tech support.

entries.title: Batch out credit card transactions by hand (Batch Adjustment)
steps: Go to the Manager page and open Batch Adjustment. It lists all processed credit card transactions that have not yet been batched.
Check every tip has been entered and is correct. You can adjust tips here and change which employee a tip belongs to.
Select the Batch button at the bottom left.
All listed credit transactions are batched out and finalised for deposit.

entries.title: Tips are missing or wrong and the batch has already gone
steps: Once a batch is processed, tips cannot be adjusted through the POS.
Contact your credit card processor directly.
Have each signed credit slip ready: you will need them to claim or correct the tips.

entries.title: A tip was assigned to the wrong employee
steps: Go to Manager > Batch Adjustment before the batch goes out.
Find the transaction.
Select the employee assigned to the tip and change it to the right one.

entries.title: Add a gratuity to a ticket
steps: Select Add Gratuity on the Manager screen or Add Grat on the Payment Screen. The user needs the right permission.
Apply the gratuity as a percentage or a fixed dollar amount.
The gratuity shows above the total, prints on the customer receipt and is tracked separately from tips.

entries.title: Reset a gift card balance to zero so the card can be reused
steps: Select Manager > Reset Balance.
Swipe the gift card at the terminal when prompted. If you cancel the terminal prompt you can type the card number.
Tick the checkbox next to the card number to see the current balance.
Select Reset Balance and accept the final warning.
This is permanent, cannot be undone, and does not refund earlier payments made with the card.

entries.title: Split a ticket (by payments, by seat, evenly or by hand)
steps: Open the ticket, then select Employee > Split/Combine Tickets.
Split Payments: enter how many payments to divide the total into and process each one.
Split by Seat: divides the ticket into one ticket per seat; select Done.
Split Evenly: enter the number of splits and select Done.
Manual: tap Split to create a blank ticket, tap an item so it turns green, then tap the destination ticket.
To split one item, swipe left on it, tap Split and enter the number of parts.

entries.title: Combine tickets
steps: Open one of the tickets.
Go to Employee > Split/Combine Tickets and select Combine at the bottom right.
Select the other open tickets (same employee) to merge in, or select Scan Tickets if tickets print with barcodes and a scanner is connected.
Tap Combine, then Done.

entries.title: Run reports on Paradise
steps: In the app go to Manager > Reports and pick a category. The app holds the past 30 days.
For older data use the online Paradise Dashboard at www.myposdashboard.com.
To get access to the dashboard, contact Paradise POS Tech Support.
Hourly Overview is available straight from the Manager tab.

entries.title: Which Paradise reports still work when the network is down
steps: All reports are available in the app while it is connected to the internet.
When the network fails, two reports still work on the device: the Drawer Report when closing a cash drawer, and the employee Shift Report.

entries.title: Taking payments on Paradise when the internet is down (Local Mode)
steps: The setting Allow Payment Offline (Admin > Company Settings, Ticket section) enables several payment methods while the system is offline.
Payment methods that need the credit card terminal are not included.
Allow Splits Offline lets you split tickets offline, but the split shows only on the iPad where it was done, which can cause discrepancies with several iPads.

entries.title: Old print jobs are stuck in Open Print Jobs: clear the queue
steps: Go to the Admin page. Open Print Jobs is in the bottom centre. Jobs wait there until a printer becomes available, for example after it was off or out of paper.
Press and hold the top print job and drag your finger down toward the bottom of the page.
A red Clear Queue button appears. Lift your finger and select it.
If many jobs are backed up, repeat this several times.

entries.title: Card terminal shows disconnected on the Paradise Admin page: Check Connection
steps: Go to the Admin page and look at Terminal Status.
Select Check Connection. This often reconnects a terminal that was turned off and on or went offline.
When the terminal is connected properly its status shows Available.
A Bluetooth card reader has no IP address listed and may show Label instead of Connected.

entries.title: Print Queue Unavailable
steps: This message in the Printer Status section of the Admin screen most likely means a problem with the internet connection.
Work through the networking troubleshooting steps: check the iPad's Wi-Fi, then restart the modem, router and Pi.

entries.title: Printer not printing: check Printer Status on the Admin page first
steps: Go to the Admin page and look at Printer Status at the bottom right.
It lists each Ethernet printer, whether it is online, and its IP address.
It may show the cause, such as out of paper or the tray or cover being open.

entries.title: Do not change the default printer settings unless Paradise support says so
steps: Printers shipped from Paradise are usually already created in Admin > Printer Maintenance.
Leave their default settings alone unless tech support tells you to change them. The printers need those settings to work.

entries.title: An item does not print in the kitchen: assign it to the kitchen printer
steps: Go to Admin > Printer Maintenance and select the kitchen printer.
The list on the right shows the items assigned to that printer.
Tap the small plus sign at the top left of the list to see all items. Use the small i to filter by department or category.
Select the items (or Select All) and tap Add Items to Selected Printer.
Save.

entries.title: Receipts go to the wrong printer or ask which printer to use: set the station's Receipt Printer
steps: Go to Admin > Device Maintenance and select the device marked (This Device).
Set Receipt Printer to the printer this station should use for receipts.
Settings shown in grey are locked and cannot be changed.

entries.title: Customer-facing display not showing: check CFD IP and the network
steps: The iPad stations and the customer-facing display must be on the same network.
Go to Admin > Device Maintenance and select the device.
Check the CFD IP setting. Scanning the QR code on the customer display fills in the IP address automatically.

entries.title: Station keeps returning to the login screen: Device Timeout
steps: Go to Admin > Device Maintenance and select the device.
Device Timeout is the number of seconds before the system returns to the login screen.
Set it to zero to turn the timeout off.

entries.title: Paradise app frozen on an iPad: close and reopen the app
steps: iPad without a Home button: swipe up from the bottom of the screen and pause in the middle to open the App Switcher.
iPad with a Home button: double-press the Home button to open the App Switcher.
Swipe left or right to find the Paradise app.
Swipe up on the app's preview to close it.
Go back to the Home screen and tap the app icon to reopen it.

entries.title: Paradise app frozen on an Android device: close, reopen or force stop the app
steps: Open the Recent Apps screen (tap the square icon, or swipe up from the bottom and pause).
Find the app and swipe it off the screen to close it.
Go back to the Home screen or app drawer and tap the app icon to reopen it.
If problems continue: open Settings, tap Apps or Apps & notifications, select the app, tap Force Stop and confirm, then reopen the app.
Exact steps vary a little by tablet brand and Android version.

entries.title: Restart an iPad running Paradise
steps: iPad without a Home button: press and hold the Top button and either Volume button until the power off slider appears.
iPad with a Home button: press and hold the Top (or Side) button until the power off slider appears.
Drag the slider to turn the iPad off.
When the screen is completely off, press and hold the Top button again until the Apple logo appears.

entries.title: Restart an Android device running Paradise
steps: Press and hold the Power button, usually on the side or top.
When the power menu appears, tap Restart or Reboot. If there is no restart option, tap Power Off.
If you chose Power Off, wait until the screen is fully off, then press and hold the Power button until the device starts again.

entries.title: Cash drawer will not open and you hear a click
steps: First make sure the drawer is not physically locked.
A clicking sound when you try to open it from the Paradise app means the drawer is likely locked or jammed.

entries.title: Cash drawer will not open and there is no sound at all
steps: Check the receipt printer is powered on and working. The app opens the drawer through the receipt printer, so if the printer is not working the drawer will not open.
If the printer prints receipts but the drawer still will not open, check the cable between the printer and the drawer.
