The cable has two labeled ends. The Cash Drawer end goes into the bottom of the drawer and the Printer end goes into the back of the receipt printer.

entries.title: Drawer opens with Open Drawer in the app but not on a cash payment
steps: This usually means no drawer was opened when the station was first used that day.
Go to the Employee screen.
If the button says Open Cash Drawer, no drawer is active. Open one.
Cash taken before a drawer was opened is recorded against the employee instead, and the system shows that employee as owing the restaurant money.

entries.title: Bluetooth receipt printer is not printing: first checks
steps: Turn the printer off and back on.
Make sure all cables are connected and secure.
Check paper is loaded correctly in the tray.
Press the Feed button on the front of the printer. If paper feeds through, the paper is installed correctly.
If it still does not print, reconnect the printer to the iPad over Bluetooth.

entries.title: Reconnect or re-pair a Bluetooth receipt printer to the iPad
steps: Make sure the printer is plugged in and switched on with a steady light on the front panel.
On the iPad Home screen (not inside the Paradise app) tap Settings > Bluetooth and make sure Bluetooth is on.
If the printer shows under My Devices as Not Connected, tap its name. If it changes to Connected you are done.
If it is listed but will not connect, tap the i icon next to its name and select Forget This Device.
With the printer on, press and hold the red Pair button on the back until the indicator light starts flashing, then release.
Wait about 30 seconds. The printer should reappear under My Devices. Tap its name to pair.
The indicator light on the back of the printer turns blue when pairing has worked.

entries.title: Ethernet receipt or kitchen printer is not printing
steps: Check every iPad is on the correct Wi-Fi network, usually named POS - your company name. Open Safari and load a web page to confirm internet access.
If the page does not load, restart your router and Pi.
Open the paper tray, clear any jam, reload the paper, close the tray and hold the Feed button to check paper feeds.
Check all cables on the back of the printer, then turn the printer off and on. The front light should be steady with no flashing error light.
If an error light is on, trace the Ethernet cable from the printer to the router and make sure it is plugged in firmly.
In the Paradise app look for the PQ (Print Queue) indicator at the top of the screen. If it is red, the Pi may need to be restarted.
If all of that is fine, the printer may have a new IP address: print its IP slip and compare it with the app.

entries.title: Ethernet printer may have a new IP address: print its IP and compare with the app
steps: Turn the printer off.
Hold down the Feed button and turn the printer back on while still holding it.
Keep holding for about 10 seconds. The printer prints a slip with its IP address.
In the Paradise app go to Admin > Printer Maintenance, select the printer and compare the IP address.
This may not work for every printer brand. Ask Paradise tech support if you need help.

entries.title: USB receipt printer is not printing
steps: Make sure the iPad is connected to the printer with a genuine Apple charging cable. Off-brand cables may not carry both charging and data.
Make sure the printer is on. A solid blue light on the front means it has power.
Open the paper tray, clear any jam, reload the paper, close the tray and press Feed to check it feeds.
In the Paradise app go to Admin > Device Maintenance, select This Device and check the correct printer is chosen as the Receipt Printer.
Then go to Admin > Printer Maintenance, select the printer and check its settings.

entries.title: DHCP Error (card terminal)
steps: A DHCP error means the terminal is offline.
Check the Ethernet cable is firmly connected to both the terminal and the TP-Link router. Try a different port or another cable.
Turn the terminal off, wait 5 seconds and turn it back on. See whether the DHCP error clears.
Make sure the TP-Link router has internet access. Restart your modem and router if the connection problem continues.

entries.title: Paradise networking problem, step 1: check the iPad's connection
steps: On the iPad go to Settings > Wi-Fi and make sure it is on the correct network.
Open a web browser and try to load a page.
If the page fails to load, the device is not connected to the internet. Go on to restart the networking equipment.

entries.title: Paradise networking problem, step 2: restart the modem, router and Pi
steps: Unplug the modem's power for 30 seconds. Plug it back in and wait for the lights to settle, which may take 2 to 3 minutes.
Unplug the TP-Link router for 30 seconds. Plug it back in and wait for it to fully reboot.
If you have a Pi (a small box with a red/green light), disconnect and reconnect its power cord and wait for the lights to turn solid.

entries.title: Paradise networking problem, step 3: check each device's network indicator
steps: iPads and Android devices: check the Wi-Fi icon is showing in the top-right corner. Reconnect to the POS network if needed.
Printers: look for a steady green light. Flashing or red means a printer problem.
Card terminals: should show Connected or Ready. If one shows DHCP error, follow the DHCP error steps.

entries.title: Paradise networking problem, step 4: check Ethernet cables and ports
steps: Check all Ethernet cables are firmly plugged into the correct ports on the modem and router.
Double-check each device is connected to the correct network.
Try plugging the Ethernet cable into another free LAN port on the router.

entries.title: A device is online but not talking to Paradise: check for IP address conflicts
steps: In the Paradise app go to Admin > Terminal Status.
Compare the IP addresses listed there with the ones printed or displayed by the devices. Duplicate or mismatched IPs can stop communication.
Restart each station, printer and terminal.

entries.title: Reset Paradise app connections to terminals and printers
steps: Open the Paradise app.
Go to Admin > Terminal Status.
Tap Check Connection, or Reset Connection if it is offered.
Check all terminals show Available and all printers show Online.

entries.title: HotSauce Technologies phone number and address
steps: HotSauce Technologies lists its telephone number as 678.325.5300.
Its address is 7001 Peachtree Industrial Blvd Suite 4200, Norcross, GA 30092.
The public site gives no support hours on its home page; its FAQ page says the support department is 24/7.

entries.title: HotSauce support is 24/7 and has Spanish, Tagalog and Mandarin speakers
steps: HotSauce describes its support department as 24/7.
Support has Spanish, Tagalog and Mandarin speakers.
The implementation department has Spanish and Tagalog speakers.

entries.title: HotSauce is sold and serviced through certified resellers
steps: HotSauce POS systems are sold only through its certified reseller channel.
If you have a certified reseller, keep working with them for sales and service.

entries.title: Which paper HotSauce printers take
steps: Kitchen printers (impact printers) take 3 inch x 150 foot 1-ply white bond paper, or 3 inch x 90 foot 2-ply carbonless paper.
Kitchen printers also need an ink cartridge. One is supplied with the printer.
Receipt printers (thermal printers) take 3-1/8 inch x 230 foot thermal paper.
The two printers do not use the same paper.

entries.title: Where to buy HotSauce printer paper and kitchen ribbons
steps: Order from the HotSauce online store at store.hotsaucepos.com.
Or buy from other distributors, including your food supplier.
HotSauce does not supply free POS paper.

entries.title: Internet is down on HotSauce: offline payments must be switched on by hand
steps: Offline payments are not automatic. If the internet goes down, the settings have to be changed manually.
Understand the risk before you do: while processing offline you will not know whether a card was declined until the system is connected to the internet again.
The public FAQ does not say where the setting is, so contact HotSauce support to change it.

entries.title: HotSauce training mode: card payments do not go through and nothing is saved
steps: A HotSauce system is not delivered in training mode. It is only turned on at the owner's request.
In training mode card transactions do not go through and transactions are not saved on the system.

entries.title: Where HotSauce reports are and how to print them
steps: The HotSauce back office is only on the SERVER terminal.
Have the reports emailed to you, or print them on the receipt printer attached to that terminal.
Reports away from the restaurant need the add-on Mission Control: Reporting.

entries.title: HotSauce is not cloud based: the data is held on the POS terminal
steps: The HotSauce system is not cloud based.
All of the information is held only on the POS terminal.

entries.title: Why HotSauce needs its own router
steps: HotSauce says PCI compliance requires a specific router to be used with its system.
Keep the HotSauce router in place; it is also how HotSauce keeps the system private and secure.

entries.title: HotSauce stations are touch screens; the back office server needs a mouse and keyboard
steps: All server POS stations are touch screens.
The Back Office Server computer needs a mouse and keyboard.

entries.title: Start a bar tab with the PAX S300 chip reader on HotSauce
steps: Tap Start a Tab. You can enter a name, swipe a card, or start the tab with the chip reader.
If you start the tab with the chip reader, you still need to enter the name or swipe the card on the terminal, because the chip reader does not pull a name.

entries.title: HotSauce manager cards and the 4 digit PIN
steps: Staff clock in and get into the front of house with a 4 digit PIN.
A manager card works the same way as the PIN: you swipe the card instead of typing.

entries.title: HotSauce PAX A920 handheld has weak or no signal
steps: The A920 gets its signal from a wireless access point.
More than one wireless access point may be needed to cover the floor. Ask HotSauce or your reseller about adding one.

entries.title: HotSauce A920: the chip reader is always active
steps: The A920 is a wireless card terminal used to order and pay at the table.
It cannot be used without the chip reader; the chip reader is always active.

entries.title: UberEats, GrubHub and other delivery orders on HotSauce are entered by hand
steps: HotSauce is not integrated with any third party delivery service.
HotSauce can set up payment buttons labeled with each delivery service you use.
The orders themselves have to be entered into the POS by hand.

entries.title: HotSauce online orders print in the kitchen automatically
steps: An online order prints to the kitchen automatically.
The front of house also shows notifications in several places so servers and the host know an online order came in.
The wait time sent to customers can be controlled on the main POS terminal.

entries.title: An imported (older) gift card will not swipe on HotSauce
steps: Imported cards may not swipe, depending on which track of the magnetic stripe holds the data.
Type the full card number instead.

entries.title: HotSauce does not install on your own computer
steps: HotSauce does not install on any third party hardware.
For a back office computer for reports and menu edits, the Elite Server has to be added to the contract.

entries.title: HotSauce staff training videos
steps: HotSauce's FAQ page links training videos: Full Service in English, Full Service in Spanish, Quick Counter Service / Bar in English, and Handheld A920.
Open the FAQs page on hotsaucepos.com to reach them.

entries.title: Genius for Restaurants support: 24/7/365 phone and email
steps: Genius for Restaurants support is open 24/7/365.
Call 800-3Genius.
Or email GeniusRestaurantSupport@globalpay.com.

entries.title: Genius Enterprise support channels (SMS, chat, phone, email)
steps: SMS 1-844-957-4434 for critical issues where pictures or detailed steps help, such as network or hardware issues.
Phone 1-800-547-4266 for emergencies or complex issues, such as network cables, credit card processing or offline equipment.
Email sos@globalpay.com for non-critical issues or questions.
WebChat and Web-to-Case are also offered through the support-request link on the Genius Contact Support page.
entries.note: This page is headed Contact Genius Enterprise Support; restaurant merchants are given 800-3Genius in the XC23 guide.

entries.title: Global Payments general support numbers by portfolio (US and Canada)
steps: USA Global Payments: +1-800-688-5378.
USA Heartland: +1-888-963-3600.
Canada Global Payments: +1-800-263-2970.
No hours are given on the page.

entries.title: Older Heartland Restaurant support line (2020 FAQ)
steps: The 2020 FAQ lists a 24/7 support phone, 1-833-844-HPOS (4767).
It also lists the email HRPOSSupport@heartland.us.
Use the current Genius numbers first; this entry is here in case a merchant quotes the old line.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Genius GC26 countertop: what is in the box
steps: The GC26 arrives assembled.

Check for: the 15.6-inch merchant-facing display, counter-top stand, removable plastic top cover, magnetic metal front cable cover, port hub, USB-C cable for the display, power supply and power cable.
An optional 10.1-inch customer-facing display may be included, with or without a payment reader, either on a bracket on the stand or on its own low-profile stand.

entries.title: Set up the Genius GC26 countertop station
steps: Remove and discard the shipping tape and covers from the displays, stand and cables.
Tilt the merchant display back and pull off the magnetic cable cover on the stand to reveal the port hub.
Feed the power cord, Ethernet, cash drawer and USB cables up through the hole in the bottom of the stand and plug them into the port hub.
If a customer display was ordered it is already plugged into the top USB-C port; check that cable is properly seated.
Refit the front cable cover: angle the top in first and let the magnets connect.
Take off the black top cover and check the display cables are seated at the back under the display arm and in the top of the stand, then refit the cover.
Adjust the screens, then plug the power cable into an outlet.
Press the power button on the lower-left back corner of the merchant display. It lights blue when the display is on.
After boot-up the GC26 launches the Genius app. Set up Wi-Fi and the Genius app.

entries.title: Genius GC26 display does not power on
steps: Check the power supply connections.
Check the electrical outlet it is plugged into.
Make sure all cables are in their correct ports in the hub and firmly seated.

entries.title: Genius GC26 on Ethernet is not connecting
steps: Make sure all cables are connected to their correct ports in the hub and are firmly seated.
Verify network connectivity for the Ethernet connection.

entries.title: Enable a location for Genius on XC23, GC26 (NextGen) or Mobile 2.0 devices
steps: Only registered devices can access Genius Restaurant at a location.
In a web browser, log into the Admin Portal for your account and location.
From the Main Menu select Location Setup, then the Mobile/NextGen Settings tab.
Select Add Location to Mobile NextGen Group.
Force close and restart the Restaurant app on all other devices on the network, including tablets and kiosks. This resets their socket connection.

entries.title: XC23: reach the ports to attach a printer, customer display or other peripherals
steps: At the back of the XC23, under the display, find the access opening to the drive.
Find the plastic cover that holds the drive chassis. Two screws under the chassis secure it.
Remove the screws with a Phillips screwdriver and set them aside.
Attach the peripherals to the appropriate ports.
Put the plastic cover back and secure it with the screws.

entries.title: A peripheral on the XC23 is dead: check the XC23 base is powered on
steps: Some peripherals are powered over USB from the XC23.
Make sure the XC23 base is powered on, or those peripherals will not work properly.

entries.title: Connect the receipt printer to an XC23 and load paper
steps: Plug the power cable into the printer.
Plug the USB-B end of the data cable into the printer and the USB-A end into the XC23 drive.
Thread the cables through the access panels and plug the power cable into an outlet.
Open the paper feed lid.
Insert the paper roll so the paper feeds from the bottom of the roll.
Close the lid and flip the power switch on.

entries.title: Receipt paper size for the Genius XC23 receipt printer
steps: Use paper 80mm wide, 0.053 to 0.085mm thick, with a roll diameter of up to 83mm.
A USB thermal receipt printer cannot currently be used as a shared kitchen printer.

entries.title: Connect the cash drawer on a Genius station
steps: Turn the cash drawer over to reach its ports.
Plug the cable end marked Cash Drawer into the cash drawer.
Plug the other end, marked Printer, into the receipt printer's data port.

entries.title: Connect the barcode scanner to an XC23
steps: Plug the RJ45 end of the cable into the scanner charging cradle.
Plug the USB end into one of the black USB-A ports on the XC23 drive.
Scan the QR code that comes with it.
Wait for the scanner to chirp twice, the green light to flash, and the scanner to chirp once more.

entries.title: Fit the ribbon and paper in the Genius kitchen printer
steps: Open the ribbon cassette cover using the tabs on each side.
Unpack the ribbon cassette and turn its knob to take up the slack.
Insert the cassette and push down until it clicks into place, then close the cover.
Open the paper feed lid and insert the roll so paper feeds from the bottom of the roll.
Close the lid, plug the power cable into an outlet and flip the power switch on.

entries.title: Connect the Genius POS Reader to an XC23
steps: The POS Reader is plug and play and needs no Admin Portal setup.
Attach its cable to the XC23 drive.
Stay on the reader login PIN screen until all firmware updates finish. This can take up to three minutes.

entries.title: Card swiped but the Reader shows a status panel: it is still initializing
steps: The payment device re-initializes when the POS app first runs, after the device restarts, after a Publish update from the Admin Portal, after the app cache is cleared, or after the app is reinstalled.
Stay on the PIN screen for 2 to 3 minutes to let it finish.
If you swiped while it was still initializing, tap Cancel to close the panel and go back to Checkout.
Swipe the card again once the device has finished initializing.

entries.title: Connect power to a Verifone T650C used with Genius
steps: On the bottom of the device, press the release button and slide off the protective plate.
Connect the power supply cable to the power port. Connect an Ethernet cable if you use one.
Replace the plate and plug the power cable into an outlet.
Then connect the device to the network.

entries.title: Connect a Verifone T650C or T650P to Wi-Fi for Genius
steps: Power on the device and tap the Home icon.
At the bottom of the screen tap the ^ icon.
Select Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi.
Select the Wi-Fi network. It should be the same network the POS is on.
Type the Wi-Fi password and tap Connect.
Write down the IP address assigned to the device. It is needed in the Admin Portal.
The T650C can use Wi-Fi or Ethernet. The T650P can only use Wi-Fi.

entries.title: Connect a Verifone T650C to Ethernet for Genius
steps: Ethernet needs the additional charging base.
Power on the device, tap the Home icon and tap the ^ icon at the bottom of the screen.
Select Settings > Network & Internet > Advanced Options > Ethernet.
Select DHCP or Static.
For Static, enter the IP address, gateway, network prefix length (24 by default), DNS 1 and DNS 2.
Tap Save.

entries.title: A Verifone T650 cannot share a terminal with a PAX or CFD device
steps: You cannot run a Verifone T650 with a PAX or customer-facing display device on the same terminal.

entries.title: Get a Device Login Code for a new or logged-out Genius device
steps: Connect the device to the network.
Log into the Admin Portal and open the right location.
In the Main Menu click Location Setup, then Authorized Tablets.
Click the Login Code tab and click Generate Code.
The same code can log in multiple POS, KDS or kiosk apps. For a new code select Regenerate Code.

entries.title: Sign a device in to the Genius POS
steps: Connect the device to the network and let it finish updating. It reboots and opens Genius for Restaurants.
On the XC23 Home screen tap the Genius icon if the app is not open.
Enter a valid Device Login Code and tap Confirm.
When asked how the device will be used, tap Permanent.
On the PIN screen enter a valid PIN and tap Go.

entries.title: Genius login (authorization) codes: how long they last and how they work
steps: For merchants a new code is valid for one hour.
While valid, one code can log in several devices and apps (POS, KDS and Kiosk).
Codes belong to the location, not to a device.
Device Licensing Codes are six alphanumeric characters.
Staff still use their normal PINs on the PIN screen once the device is logged in.

entries.title: A Genius device got logged out and nobody on site can get into the Admin Console
steps: A logged-out POS, KDS or Kiosk needs an authorization code to log back in.
If staff cannot reach the Admin Console to get one, ask the dealer or the Genius Support department for a temporary login code for the location.

entries.title: Genius Admin Console sign-in codes (multi-factor authentication)
steps: Everyone who logs into the Admin Console must enter an authentication code; there is no opt-out.
The first code is emailed. After that you can choose text message, email or an authenticator app (Microsoft Authenticator or Google Authenticator).
You can ask the Admin Console to remember a code for up to 45 days.
Login passwords do not expire.

entries.title: Do not tap System Logout by mistake: it needs a Device Login Code to get back in
steps: Logout (lower right of the Room screen) only logs the staff member out and shows the PIN screen.
System Logout (last option in the Manager Settings menu) logs the whole device out of the account and shows the Account Login screen.
After a System Logout someone must enter a valid Device Login Code for the account to get back into the POS.

entries.title: Cannot sign in to a new Genius POS: Staff users have not been created
steps: You cannot sign in to the point of sale until Staff users have been created in the Guided Setup process.
Check your inbox for the Account Activation email and start the Guided Setup.

entries.title: XC23 first power-on: connect to the internet and wait for updates
steps: Feed the power cable through the openings on the bottom of the stand and press the power button on the back of the device.
Wi-Fi (recommended): when first turned on the device asks you to select a wireless network. Select it and enter the password.
If that prompt disappears, turn the device off and back on to get it again.
Ethernet: route the network cable through the bottom access port and the cable channel in the neck of the stand and connect it to the Ethernet port.
Let the device download and install its updates. This can take 15 to 30 minutes depending on network speed.

entries.title: Genius NextGen or Mobile 2.0 device will not join the Wi-Fi: WPA3 is not supported
steps: NextGen devices and Mobile 2.0 handhelds do not support the WPA3 security standard.
Set the Wi-Fi network to WPA2 (or WEP) for these devices.

entries.title: Connect an XC23 to Wi-Fi from its settings
steps: Go to the XC23 Home screen and tap the Settings icon.
Tap Network & internet, then Wi-Fi.
Select the network, enter its password and tap Connect.

entries.title: Power up a Genius NextGen device
steps: Press and hold the Power button on the underside of the screen.
When it has powered up it shows its Home screen.

entries.title: No content is configured for this device.
steps: This blue-screen message appears when the NextGen stand's Network prompt timed out before a Wi-Fi network was selected.
Restart the NextGen device manually.
When the Network screen shows again, select the Wi-Fi network and connect straight away.

entries.title: NextGen device stuck on the blue 'device setup is completed' screen
steps: After its update utilities run, the device shows a blue screen with a spinning icon and then restarts. This normally takes 5 to 15 minutes.
If it has not restarted by itself after 15 minutes, restart the device manually.

entries.title: Customer display or NextGen screen does not display properly: set screen density to 160
steps: Tap the Home button in the bottom panel, then tap the Settings icon on the Apps screen.
Tap Display, then Advanced.
Tap Screen density and select 160 MDPI.
Tap REBOOT NOW when prompted. The device restarts with the new density.
Do this before signing into the Genius POS app.

entries.title: Update the Genius POS app on a NextGen device
steps: Turn on the device and run the POS app.
On the PIN screen tap the Information icon in the lower left corner.
In the Information panel tap Check for Update.
If there is no update the POS briefly shows Resync Complete.
If there is one it downloads and installs straight away, which can take several minutes. The POS then restarts and shows the PIN screen.

entries.title: Do not remove the blue or black pull tabs on the USB-C cables
steps: Some USB-C cables supplied with the NextGen device have small plastic pull tabs on their ends.
Leave them on. They give you grip to pull the cable out of the inner housing of the device.

entries.title: Customer-facing display beeps but shows a black screen
steps: Find the circular button on the back of the customer display.
Press and hold it until the screen flashes on.

entries.title: Connect the customer-facing display to a NextGen terminal
steps: Turn the customer display over and unspool its USB-C power cable.
Slide the back panel off the NextGen device to reveal the USB-C port labeled CFD.
Plug the cable into the CFD port and refit the back panel, threading the cable through its access hole.
Power on the NextGen device and log into the POS. The customer display then shows a smaller version of the POS screen.

entries.title: Set which printers a Genius station uses (printer template and Default Register Printer)
steps: Log into the POS and tap the Options button on the Rooms screen.
Tap Settings, then Printers.
Tap New Template, name it and select the rooms that use the printer on this device.
Tap Enable on each printer this device will use. Tap Send Test on a printer's tile to send a test print.
Tap Save, then select the template and tap Use.
Select the Default Register Printer, then tap Exit.

entries.title: Guest checks will not print or the cash drawer will not open: no Default Register Printer set
steps: Each station needs a default register printer to print guest checks or use an attached cash drawer.
Open the Manager Settings menu and tap Printers.
Select a printer template with Use, or create one, and choose the Default Register Printer for this device.

entries.title: Printing problem on Genius: open the Printer Queue panel
steps: On the Room screen tap the Printer Queue button.
The panel describes the printer's current status in detail.

entries.title: Add an Ethernet or Wi-Fi printer in the Genius Admin Portal
steps: USB-attached printers need no configuration. Ethernet and Wi-Fi printers do.
In the Admin Console click Location Setup, then Printers, then +New.
Type a name and the printer's IP address. For kitchen printers also select Shared.
Select the Printer Brand and Printer Series, then Save.
Select the Upload icon to publish the change and answer Yes.

entries.title: Set a backup printer for when a kitchen printer fails
steps: In the POS go to Options > Settings > Printers and open the printer template.
On each enabled printer, use the Backup printer for formats area to choose the display formats that should fall back to this printer.
Save the template.

entries.title: Epson TM-U220 kitchen printer: print the network status sheet (find its IP address)
steps: Make sure the printer is turned on.
Turn the printer around and push the pinhole reset button on the back with a pen or pencil tip for four seconds.
A status sheet prints with the printer's IP address on your network.

entries.title: Connect an Epson TM-U220 kitchen printer by Ethernet for Genius
steps: Turn the printer off with the power button.
Connect the Ethernet cable between the printer and your internet router.
Turn the printer on.
Push the pinhole reset button on the back for 4 seconds with a pen or pencil tip. A status sheet prints with the printer's IP address.
Add the printer in the Admin Portal under Printers with that IP address, then save and publish.

entries.title: Star SP700 kitchen printer: print the status page (find its IP address)
steps: Load paper and turn the printer off.
Hold the Feed button while turning the power on, and keep holding as it powers up.
After several seconds the power lights come on and it beeps once. Release Feed after the first beep.
The Printer Status page prints, then the network information.
The IP address is in the Current IP Parameters Status section at the bottom of the second printout.

entries.title: Star SP700: reset the printer with the RST button
steps: With paper loaded and the printer on, the green POWER light is on.
Hold the RST button on the back with a small tool for more than five seconds.
The front lights flash while it resets, then the light turns solid green.

entries.title: Wi-Fi receipt printer setup failed: you did not wait for the lights to stop blinking
steps: The error means the printer had not finished updating.
Start the Wi-Fi setup step again.
This time wait until all the lights on the printer stop blinking while it receives its configuration.

entries.title: Epson Wi-Fi receipt printer: print its network interface information
steps: With the printer off, hold the feed button.
While holding it, power the printer on.
A slip prints with the Wi-Fi and Ethernet interface information.
Press the feed button once more to print a self test.

entries.title: Epson TM-L90 label printer is not feeding labels correctly: format it for the label size
steps: Turn the printer off and open the roll paper cover. Leave it open.
Turn the printer on, then off again with the cover open.
Turn it on while pressing and holding Feed, with the cover still open, until the error and power lights are on.
Press the feed button six times.
Close the cover. The printer should feed labels by itself to learn the label size.
If it does not feed when the cover is closed, the process went wrong: start over.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: All printing stopped on a Genius iPad system: the Dedicated Socket Server is down
steps: If the iPad set as the Dedicated Socket Server goes down, all printing goes down, and the other devices stop syncing tickets to the cloud.
Get that iPad running and connected again.
If you have several iPads, another one can be set as the Dedicated Socket Server and it takes over.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: A Genius printer has locked up
steps: Restart the printer. The FAQ says restarting is the only way to clear a locked-up printer.
Lockups and lost jobs are a known risk of the Shared Printing without Sockets setting, which Global Payments says not to use in normal operation.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Where a report prints when you tap Print in the Genius POS app
steps: Print in the POS app sends the report to the default register printer set for that device under Manager > Printers.
Print in the Admin Portal opens your browser's own print settings instead.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Take payment on a Genius ticket (card, cash, gift card)
steps: Open the ticket and tap Checkout to reach the Payment screen.
For a credit card tap Card. For a gift card tap Gift Card. For a custom tender tap Custom.
For exact cash tap Cash.
If the customer hands over more cash, enter the amount on the keypad or tap a suggested amount. The POS shows the change due.

entries.title: Void a whole ticket on Genius
steps: Open the ticket and tap Actions.
Tap Void Order.
Tap a void reason, and add a description if you want.
Tap Void. The ticket is voided and its table shows as available.

entries.title: Refund a paid ticket on Genius
steps: Open the paid ticket, tap Actions, then Refund. Refund appears only after a ticket is paid and refunds the full amount.
Tap OK at the Refund Ticket prompt.
Select a refund reason or type one, then tap Refund.
Choose how to pay the refund: Cash, Card, Gift Card (if enabled) or Custom.
The POS processes the refund and shows a screen confirming approval. Tap Print for a receipt.
A refunded ticket shows its items in red text and its tile is highlighted red.

entries.title: Reprint a ticket or receipt on Genius
steps: Open the ticket and tap Actions, then Reprint.
Tap the button for the printer you want. The ticket is sent to that printer.
Press and hold a printer's button to get a Preview option.

entries.title: Apply or remove a discount on a Genius ticket
steps: Open the ticket, tap Actions, then Discounts.
Tap a discount. For an open-amount discount enter the amount on the keypad and tap Apply.
To remove it, tap the discount in the ticket panel and tap Remove Discount.

entries.title: Move a ticket to another server on Genius
steps: Open the ticket, tap Actions, then Change Server.
Select the server (only clocked-in servers are listed) and tap Go.
If you do not see the server, type the name in the Server Name box.

entries.title: Find a ticket on Genius
steps: On the Room screen tap Tickets.
Type a ticket number, customer name or card number in the Search box.
Or filter by Servers, Statuses, Service Areas or Payments. Tap Clear Filters to reset.

entries.title: Open the cash drawer without a sale (No Sale)
steps: On the Rooms screen tap the Options button in the top right corner.
Tap No Sale.
This only works if your job type has access to the cash drawer and the No Sale permission.

entries.title: Record a pay in or pay out on Genius
steps: Open the Pay In/Out section and select the cash pay type.
Enter the amount. Add a comment if needed.
Tap Pay In or Pay Out.

entries.title: Card reader not responding: check its status and re-select the payment terminal
steps: On the Rooms screen tap the Card Reader icon. A panel lists the status of the card readers; a working one shows CONNECTED.
If it is not connected, open Options > Settings > Payment Terminals.
Tap the tile of the terminal for this station (available ones show light green). The POS tries to connect to it.

entries.title: Add a payment terminal (not the POS Reader) to Genius
steps: In the Admin Portal go to Location Setup > Payment Terminals and select +New.
Type a name and the IP address of the payment device, then Save.
Select the Upload icon to publish.
In the POS select Menu > Manager > Payment Terminals and select the terminal.

entries.title: Payments are not processing or orders are not syncing: check Training Mode is off
steps: Open Options > Settings > General.
Check the Training Mode switch.
In training mode the POS does not process payments or sync its orders with other devices. Turn it off for live service.

entries.title: Change how quickly the Genius POS logs out when idle
steps: Open Options > Settings > General.
In the Auto Logout section pick a duration: 30 seconds, 1, 2, 5 or 10 minutes, or 1 hour.

entries.title: Mark an item out of stock (86) on Genius
steps: Open Options > Settings > Item Stock Management.
Search for the item and set its count to 0, then tap Save.
Out-of-stock items show in red and cannot be ordered in the POS or on the Online Order website.

entries.title: Fix a clock-in or clock-out on Genius (Time Punch Management)
steps: Open Options > Settings > Time Punch Management.
Set the date range, and filter by Staff or Job Type if needed.
Tap Edit on the time punch, then tap the Clock In or Clock Out tile to set a new date or time.
Tap Save. To delete a punch, swipe left and tap Delete.

entries.title: Each Genius device needs its own ticket prefix
steps: Set the prefix under Options > Settings > Tablets: one to four characters, then Save.
If you use prefixes, every POS device must have a unique one. Letters are recommended.

entries.title: End of day on Genius: clear the Daily Review screen
steps: Tap the Options button, then Settings, then Daily Review.
The screen has three tabs: Tips, Tickets and Cash. A tab with unresolved transactions shows a red mark.
Tickets: open each ticket that is not closed and close it.
Tips: enter the missing tips, or tap Empty Tips then Mark empty tips as 0, then tap Submit Tips.
Cash: check every server bank and cash drawer has been checked out.

entries.title: Transactions will not batch at end of day: tips have not been captured (Auth/Capture)
steps: If your card processing is set to Auth/Capture, tips must be captured for a transaction to batch out at the end of the day.
Open Daily Review and tap the Tips tab. A red X means tips are still outstanding.
Enter each tip, or mark empty tips as 0, then tap Submit Tips.
With Sale/Adjust processing the indicator does not show because it is not required for end of day.

entries.title: Enter tips on closed card transactions (Daily Review > Tips)
steps: Open Daily Review and tap the Tips tab. It lists transactions closed without a tip.
Tap the ticket's Tip box, enter the amount on the keypad and tap Done.
To set every empty tip to $0, tap Empty Tips, then Mark empty tips as 0.
Tap Submit Tips to save.

entries.title: A server did not check out: Force Server Checkout
steps: Open Daily Review and tap the Cash tab. Banks not checked out show a red Report button.
Tap the Report button and then Force Server Checkout at the bottom of the report.
This only works if all of that server's tickets are closed. If any are open the POS shows an error, so close them first.

entries.title: Server checkout at the end of a shift
steps: Close all of your tickets, or transfer them to another staff member.
Tap Checkout and confirm.
Hand any amount shown as Server Owes Merchant to the restaurant. If the amount is negative, the restaurant pays that amount to the server.
A manager can review the checkout in Daily Review.

entries.title: Tip out to another staff member on Genius
steps: On the Room screen tap the Options button, then Tip Out.
On the Tip tab, under Tip Out From, choose the pool (My Tips is the default).
Under Tip Out To choose Staff, pick the job type and the staff member's name.
Type the dollar amount, add a comment if you want, and tap Tip Out.
Tap OK to confirm.

entries.title: Genius Room screen status icons: Socket Server, Printer Queue, Messages
steps: Socket Server icon: shows the POS's current connection status with the socket server.
Printer Queue: opens a panel describing the printer's status.
Messages: opens the list of messages you have received.

entries.title: Find a Genius device's name, IP address and app version
steps: Open Options > Settings > Info.
The Device section shows the device name, IP addresses and the POS app's version number.
The Communication section shows the network SSID, connected servers and network interfaces.

entries.title: Attach a cash drawer before taking cash (iPad)
steps: Tap the User Menu in the top right corner.
Tap Attach Drawer.
Enter the starting cash on the keypad if it is not preset.
Tap Confirm.
If you try a cash transaction with no drawer attached you get a message saying one needs to be attached.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Connect an iPad to its card terminal or card reader
steps: Tap the User Menu in the top right, then Manager, then Payment Terminals.
Tap the terminal. The iPad tries to connect to the PAX device.
Tap the Card Reader icon. If it worked the screen shows CONNECTED.
A magnetic stripe reader plugs into the iPad's headphone jack; a message says a reader was attached.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Take a card payment on the Genius iPad app
steps: Open the ticket and tap Checkout.
For the full amount, swipe or dip the card while on the Checkout screen.
For a partial payment, enter the amount on the keypad first, then swipe the card.
To key in a card number, select Card and fill in the fields.
On approval choose Sign, Tip, Email, Print or Void Payment.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Void or change a payment taken today (iPad)
steps: Open the ticket.
At the bottom of the Ticket Preview, tap the payment.
Choose to change, print or void the payment. Void Payment asks for a void reason.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: A payment from a previous day needs changing
steps: You cannot adjust transactions from previous days. You can only view and print them.
Tap the User Menu, then Reports, then Transactions, pick the date and tap Run.
Tap the ticket number, then View Original, to see and print the transaction.
To give money back, go to the Ticket Info screen and select Refund Ticket.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Reprint a customer receipt or kitchen slip (iPad)
steps: Open the ticket and select Reprint from the left-hand menu.
Choose to reprint the customer receipt or a slip for the kitchen.
Use Preview to see the ticket in each format first.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Close a ticket by hand (iPad)
steps: Open the ticket once payment is final.
Select Close in the left-hand menu.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Split a check on Genius (iPad)
steps: Open the ticket and select Split from the left-hand menu.
New creates an empty second check. Select items and use Move, or tap Check 1 or Check 2, to move them.
Evenly splits selected items evenly. Advanced splits an item into halves, thirds, quarters or fifths.
By Seat splits by seat. 2x to 9x splits everything evenly across that many checks.
Remove All undoes the splits.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Start and end a staff break (iPad)
steps: Tap the User Menu in the top right and select Clock-Out.
Select Start Break, and the break type if asked. You are logged out.
When you return, log in and select End Break.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Message that you cannot check out until tickets are paid and closed
steps: A server or cash drawer checkout needs every ticket under that staff member closed and paid.
Close or transfer the open tickets.
Then select the User menu, Server Bank, and Checkout.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: After a cash drawer checkout the drawer is detached
steps: Checking out a cash drawer detaches it from the iPad.
Attach a new drawer before taking more cash on that iPad.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Counting the cash drawer at checkout (Actual Cash Counting)
steps: If cash counting is on, checkout asks how much cash is in the drawer.
Enter the amount and select Save, or select Count Later.
If you choose Count Later, only someone with access to Daily Review can enter the count.
With this option on, every cash drawer must be counted to close the day properly.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Reading the Daily Review marks at closing time (iPad)
steps: At closing you want a green checkmark or no indicator on Tips, Tickets and Cash.
A red X means that section still has items to complete.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: How to tell a Genius POS is offline (Cloud Sync icon, No Wi-Fi watermark)
steps: Look at the Cloud Sync icon at the top of the screen. A red badge with a number means the tablet is not communicating with the cloud.
The No Wi-Fi watermark means the iPad is not connected to the proper local network. It does not necessarily mean the internet is down.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: What does not work on Genius without internet
steps: Reports and time punch management need internet, because reports come from the cloud.
You cannot change your PIN without an internet connection.
Kiosk and Guest App orders need internet.
A guest display keeps working, but needs internet for its first login.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Offline mode is not available when the internet drops
steps: Offline card processing must be switched on for the location before an outage.
In the Admin Console open Location Setup, tick Offline Transactions in the Transaction Settings area, click Save, then Publish.
If this was not enabled when the location went offline, staff cannot use offline mode.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Authorize offline card payments once the internet is back
steps: In the POS tap the menu in the top right corner, then Manager, then Daily Review.
Tap Tickets, then Authorize All.
For pending tips tap Tips, then Capture Tips.
To do one ticket: open it, tap the Payment box near the bottom and tap Auth.
If a card is declined at this point it is likely an invalid card.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: Store and Forward: what the red status bar and purple tickets mean
steps: If the site loses its connection, the POS shows a red status bar with a count of stored transactions waiting for approval.
While offline all card transactions are approved in offline mode and stored in a queue.
Tickets not yet authorized show purple and stay open, including through end of day, until they authorize.
When the connection returns the devices upload the stored transactions automatically. There is no way to authorize them by hand.

entries.title: Back online but offline (Store and Forward) payments have not authorized
steps: This is expected: once the site is back online, stored transactions can take from 2 to 24 hours to authorize.
Keep all devices connected to the POS, powered and online so every pending transaction uploads.

entries.title: Store and Forward with the Reader: what it cannot do offline
steps: Not supported offline: bar tabs, gift cards, partial refunds, tip refunds, duplicate checking and reference refunds.
The merchant accepts the risk of loss: there is no guarantee a stored transaction will be approved.

entries.title: Bad Debt on the Daily Summary Report (offline card payments that were declined)
steps: If an offline (Store and Forward) card payment is only partly approved later, the unapproved amount is reported as bad debt.
Transactions that are fully declined are also reported as Bad Debt.
It appears in the Transactions section of the Daily Summary Report.

entries.title: Switch a PAX Store and Forward site into offline mode by hand
steps: Store and Forward must already be boarded and set up for the site.
In the POS tap the menu in the top right corner, tap Manager, then General.
Turn on Force Offline Credit Card Processing.
Genius approves all transactions offline and queues them. It does not try to upload them until you turn the setting off again.
The ceiling limit still applies.

entries.title: How long Genius can run offline and what keeps working
steps: It can run offline indefinitely. Orders are cached until the connection returns.
Printing, KDS and syncing between local devices keep working.
Online ordering, Kiosk, Guest App, reports, and card transactions (unless offline transactions are enabled) do not.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Internet down: EMV payment terminals stop, a magnetic stripe reader can be the backup
steps: All LAN printers and KDS keep working, but EMV payment terminals are down.
Offline EMV transactions are not supported (per the 2020 FAQ).
A magnetic stripe reader on a supported gateway supports offline transactions and can be set up as a backup.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product. Newer Store and Forward guides describe offline card acceptance on the Reader and PAX devices.

entries.title: Sync In Progress
steps: The iPad is in the middle of syncing to the cloud. Syncing normally happens every 60 seconds.
If the message keeps appearing for a long time, an internet connection problem may be stopping the sync.
Restore the connection. Once syncing completes you can view and edit tickets again.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Not on Wifi/Ethernet or No Sockets watermark on the Genius screen
steps: The no-Wi-Fi watermark means the device is offline. Get the connection back and it disappears.
The No Sockets watermark means printing is currently down.
In a special case it can be hidden: iPad Settings > Heartland Restaurant app > turn on Ignore Wifi Restrictions, then restart the app.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: You’re already attached to a drawer on another device
steps: You already have a drawer attached somewhere else.
Close any tickets open under that staff member.
Go to User Menu > Manager > Daily Review > Cash, tap the person icon on the open drawer, scroll to the bottom of the checkout and force a checkout.
If several people share the drawer, all of them need to be checked out.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: DEMO shows at the top right of a live Genius system
steps: It means the account is a demo account. A live account should never show it.
Contact support so the account can be corrected.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: A manager cannot see reports in the Genius app
steps: Most often it is the Report Access permission. In the Admin Portal check the staff member is assigned to a Report Access option with the needed reports ticked.
Three reports only exist in the Admin Portal: Dashboard, Ingredients and Loyalty.
More rarely, the site's firewall is blocking traffic.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Scan to Pay shows Unable to Fetch Ticket
steps: Check Scan to Pay is enabled under Location Setup > Rooms > QR Code.
Make sure the socket server tablet is connected to the internet.
Make sure the ticket's preview is not open in the system when the customer pays.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: If a Genius tablet dies, are its transactions lost?
steps: If the device had synced to the cloud and to the other tablets, the data is there.
If it failed before it could sync, those transactions or tickets may be overwritten or lost.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Refund a specific ticket (iPad, 2020 FAQ)
steps: Select the ticket.
Select Info from the left-hand menu and, under Ticket Actions, select Refund Ticket.
Confirm, then enter a reason for the refund.
Pay out the negative amount to the payment type you want.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Where yesterday's closed tickets went
steps: Closed tickets are removed from the POS app at the configured End of Day.
They can still be viewed, reported on and reprinted in the Admin Portal under Reports, or in the POS app under User Menu > Reports.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Transfer a ticket to another staff member (iPad)
steps: Select the ticket.
Select Info from the left-hand menu.
Under Room/Owner tap Server and select the staff member.
Select Send from the left-hand menu to complete the transfer. Exit discards the change.
Whether you can transfer depends on the job type and the Modify Server permission.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Keying in a card by hand fails because CVV is required
steps: On the Monetary gateway the CVV requirement on the manual entry form cannot be removed.
The processor may be able to adjust a setting to allow the transactions to be keyed. Contact the processor.
On PAX with Heartland a setting under Card Type can allow manual entry without CVV; that is a configuration change.
entries.note: From Global Payments' Heartland Restaurant FAQ PDF (Rev. 1/2020), written for dealers about the iPad version; check details against the current product.

entries.title: Card terminal is stuck and the POS says a transaction is in progress
steps: Cancel on the card terminal itself first.
Only use the Cancel button on the POS (shown when a transaction takes longer than 30 seconds) if the terminal does not report that it cancelled.
Cancelling on the POS does not guarantee the terminal stops trying to process, especially when the two have lost their connection.
If the Cancel button setting is disabled, the POS waits 5 minutes for the terminal before letting you do anything else.

entries.title: A payment void failed and the POS offers a Force void
steps: A Force void is not sent to the processor at all. It only removes the transaction from Genius reporting.
If you force void, write down the transaction details.
Contact the processor so the transaction is handled on their side.
Global Payments recommends keeping the Force Voids setting off except for one-off needs.

entries.title: Cannot open a ticket because it is being changed on another station
steps: With Ticket Locking on, a ticket being viewed or changed on another device is locked and the message cannot be bypassed.
Close the ticket on the other station, then open it again.

entries.title: Firewall blocking Genius: domains to allow
steps: If the site has a firewall, the Global Payments article lists the domains to allow, including *.heartland.us, *.appcenter.ms, *.eloview.com, *.datadoghq.com and *.gpapis.globalpay.com.
With EMV terminals a more detailed list is provided, because those terminals talk directly to the processor.
Give the article to whoever manages the network.

entries.title: ControlScan-managed Genius networks: changes go through ControlScan
steps: If the site's network is managed by ControlScan, any change has to go through ControlScan.
The article gives the ControlScan support number as (800) 393-3246, option 1.

entries.title: Genius Admin Portal: Troubleshoot and Request Screenshot for a device
steps: In the Admin Portal open the Authorized Devices screen and click Troubleshoot on the device.
The panel shows diagnostic counts such as items waiting to upload.
Click Request Screenshot to have the device send a screenshot of the POS app; click Refresh until it appears.
Remove deletes a device so another permanent device can be added within the licence limit.

entries.title: Load receipt paper in the Mobile 2.0 handheld
steps: Lift the top lid of the printer to loosen the cover.
Tilt the cover back to expose the paper roll.
Place the roll in the device with the paper feeding from the bottom.
Close the printer cover.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Charge the Mobile 2.0 handheld
steps: Plug the USB-A end of the cable into the power supply and the USB-C end into the charging base, then plug the supply into an outlet.
Place the device in the base, leading with the bottom lip of the device.
The device beeps to confirm it is charging.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Turn on the Mobile 2.0 handheld
steps: Press and hold the power button on the left side until the screen powers on.
Release it when the orange boot logo appears.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0 handheld is showing the End of Day screen
steps: Swipe up on the device and tap the app overview button.
Tap the Genius tile. The Genius app comes back to the front.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0 handheld cannot take a payment
steps: Check the Payments and PA apps are both running in the background. Their icons show in the notification bar at the top; if not, open the Apps screen and run the Payments app.
Check the device is connected to the location's Wi-Fi.
Check the battery is at least 10% charged. Below 10% the Payments app will not work. Put the device on the charger and charge above 25%.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0: the battery pack cannot be swapped
steps: If the battery is low, put the handheld on the charger and charge above 25%.
The battery pack cannot be swapped out.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Genius app shows a red icon in the top panel (handheld not connected to the socket server)
steps: The red icon means the device is not connected to the Dedicated Socket Server.
Check the handheld is on the same Wi-Fi network as the Dedicated Socket Server.
Check the Dedicated Socket Server device is running the Genius app and is on that same network.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0 app is not updating to the latest version
steps: Swipe up from the bottom of the screen and open the app overview.
Swipe the Genius tile up to close it.
Open the Apps screen and tap the Genius icon. This starts a version check and update.
A blank white screen means the app is checking for and installing the latest version. Make sure the device is on the location's Wi-Fi.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Download Error Terminal Code: 300 Cannot Connect
steps: Same cause and fix as Network Unplugged: the device is not on the network, or the Downloader failed to fetch an update.
Check the network connection and try the download again.
If it persists, forget the Wi-Fi network in Settings, reboot, reconnect and run the Downloader app again.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: D2 RETRY LATER - The transaction cannot be completed at this time. Retry later.
steps: This is a response from the card issuer, the bank or card company behind the card.
Ask the customer to try a different card.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Keys Not Injected
steps: The device cannot be used until its keys are re-injected.
It has to be sent back to the hardware team for that.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0 POS app is frozen: close and relaunch it
steps: Swipe up from the bottom of the screen.
Tap the Overview button.
Press the POS app's tile and swipe it up until it disappears.
Open the Apps screen and launch the POS app again.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0 shows a Please Wait screen after restarting
steps: This is normal: the Payments app starts by itself after a restart and shows Please Wait because it is meant to keep running in the background.
Swipe up from the bottom of the screen and tap the Home button.
On the Home screen, run the Restaurant POS app.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Mobile 2.0: clear the POS app's data (last resort)
steps: In the POS Tickets screen tap Options, then System Logout.
Swipe down from the top, tap Settings and enter a valid password.
Tap Apps, then the Restaurant icon, then Storage.
Tap Clear Data and OK, then Clear Cache.
Reboot the device and run the POS app.
You will need a valid Device Login Code to sign back in, so have one ready before you start.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: Things the Mobile 2.0 handheld cannot do (use the iPad POS instead)
steps: The guide lists: referenced refunds, server checkouts, clock ins, Scan to Pay transactions, item discounts, advanced item splits, and duplicate ingredients and sub-items.
entries.note: Applies to the Genius Mobile 2.0 handheld.

entries.title: WiseCube card reader is not connecting
steps: Charge the reader first if it is not charged.
Plug the power cord into the Mobile POS enclosure to wake the reader, wait ten seconds, and tap the card icon at the top of the POS to see if it is connected.
On the iPad open Settings > Bluetooth and check the reader is connected. If not, tap the CHBxxxx device to connect, then reopen the app.

If that fails: close the app, tap the Information button for the WiseCube in the Bluetooth list and tap Forget device. Reopen the app, go to Settings > Manager > Payment Terminals, tap Scan for WiseCube Devices and tap Pair.

Last resort: remove the reader from the enclosure, hold its power button until it powers off, turn the iPad's Bluetooth off and on, turn the reader back on (its lights chase), then scan and pair again.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: Error System Error (WiseCube)
steps: Either CrossTID is not enabled on the processing file, or the processing URL used for WiseCube devices is down.
Call processing to re-enable CrossTID for the WiseCube device, or to report or confirm the outage.
If it is an outage, wait for processing to be restored.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: Error Offlinedecline (WiseCube)
steps: The device is misconfigured.
It needs to be returned and replaced (an RMA).
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: Insert, swipe, or try another card error (WiseCube)
steps: The card may have been inserted the wrong way. Flip it over and try again.
The card may be defective. Try another card.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: Tap does not work on the Mobile POS (WiseCube)
steps: The reader is not installed correctly in the enclosure.
Refit it so the NFC logo on the reader faces the NFC logo on the enclosure.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: WiseCube Error
steps: Restart the tablet and the WiseCube device.
If failures continue, uninstall and reinstall the Heartland Restaurant POS application.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: Frequent WiseCube disconnections in the MobilePOS case: battery removal
steps: Global Payments saw far fewer disconnections between the iPad Mini and the WiseCube once the HBSM-CH60 battery was removed from the case.
Removing it means opening the case with tools and can cause irreparable damage, so this is not a job for the merchant.
After removal the case needs charging after each busy shift.
entries.note: Applies to the older Mobile Point of Sale kit (iPad Mini with a BBPOS WiseCube reader in an enclosure).

entries.title: Staff swipe card is not recognised, or the POS keeps showing Swipe Card to Link
steps: The swipe was probably unreadable: misaligned, too fast or too slow.
Swipe again with a steady motion, with the magnetic stripe facing the right way (usually shown by the light on the Reader).
Check the stripe is clean and intact. Debris, sticky residue or deep scratches can stop it reading.

entries.title: Assign a swipe card to a staff member on Genius
steps: Log in to a POS device that is connected to the internet, with an account allowed to assign PINs and cards.
Open the User Menu and tap Assign Card.
Select the staff member.
Swipe an unassigned card through the reader at a steady, moderate speed.
The POS shows a confirmation message.

entries.title: XC23 camera: features missing, blank or blurry picture, slow scanning
steps: Features missing: connect the camera as in the setup steps and reboot the POS terminal.
Blank or blurry: check the lens for obstructions and remove any plastic film. If it continues, reboot the POS terminal.
Slow or failed scanning: make sure the area has enough light.

entries.title: Pair the Zebra DS2278 Bluetooth scanner with a Genius iPad
steps: Scan the two programming barcodes shown in the Global Payments article.
Press the button on the scanner to begin pairing.
On the tablet open Bluetooth settings and make sure Bluetooth is on.
Tap the device named DS2278 followed by numbers and check it shows Connected.

entries.title: Barcode scanner does not scan when picked up off its stand
steps: It does not scan automatically when picked up.
Press the black button on top to scan while holding it.

entries.title: Caller ID box is not sending calls to Genius
steps: Make sure Multicast is enabled on the network and port 4100 is open.
Make sure port 3520 is open for UDP traffic.
The box must be on the same local network as the tablets.
A ticket must be open on the Ticket Info screen to receive the call.
Only the supported Whozz Calling boxes work; Deluxe boxes do not. For phone-line wiring or dip switches contact Whozz Calling.

entries.title: Wire a Genius iPad stand to Ethernet (Ethernet cable kit)
steps: Plug the Ethernet adapter into the internal cable of the Genius stand.
Plug the Lightning end of the Y cable into the Ethernet adapter.
Plug the male USB-A end of the Y cable into the Apple power brick.
Plug in an Ethernet cable.
Connect the Apple power brick to a power source.
Newer iPads use USB-C instead of Lightning; the cabling is otherwise identical.
entries.note: From the guide for the iPad version of Genius for Restaurants (formerly Heartland Restaurant); screens on an XC23 or GC26 station can differ.

entries.title: HotSauce Support: phone option and email
steps: Call HotSauce Support on 678.325.5300 and choose option 2.
Or email support@hotsaucepos.com.
HotSauce's FAQ describes the support department as 24/7.

entries.title: What must be ready on site before a HotSauce installation
steps: The counter or desktop is installed where the terminal will go, with a hole of at least 1-1/2 inches for cables if needed.
Powered electrical outlets are within 5 feet of the computer's location.
The DSL or cable modem is installed and the internet is working.
All network wiring (CAT 5 / Ethernet) is run and terminated. HotSauce does not run Ethernet cabling; it recommends a local company.
Remote printer wiring is run and terminated.

entries.title: When HotSauce installations happen and who does them
steps: Installations are only performed Monday to Thursday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm Eastern.
HotSauce contracts a local installation tech to install the POS hardware on site, supported remotely by the HotSauce implementation team.
That visit covers HotSauce hardware only: not wiring, third party equipment or on-site training.

entries.title: HotSauce Go Live call: what gets checked on the first day
steps: The HotSauce implementation team contacts the merchant on the first day of live use, ideally 1 to 2 hours before opening.
Together you run through order placement, processing a credit card, the cash drawer opening, all printers, and the end of shift and end of day procedure.
A follow-up call happens 3 to 5 days after Go Live.

entries.title: How HotSauce staff training is delivered
steps: Training is by online video, in English and Spanish. HotSauce provides the video links.
On-site training is available for an additional fee.

entries.title: HotSauce menu review before install
steps: The implementation team reviews the whole configured menu with the merchant: items, modifiers and pricing.
Have a computer or laptop and the day-to-day manager on the call.
Skipping the review leads to problems using the system.

entries.title: HotSauce preferred hardware (which printer, drawer and terminal models to expect)
steps: POS terminal: Partnertech Grace G4 or SP550 touch POS system.
Receipt (thermal) printer: Partnertech RP-630.
Kitchen (dot matrix) printer: SNBC M-300 or Epson TM-U220B.
Cash drawer: Partnertech CDR-6E410. Barcode scanner: Honeywell 1250G-2USB. Scale: Avery Berkel 6712.
Routers: MikroTik hEX RB750Gr3 or RB760iGS, or TP-Link ER605. Wireless access point: TP-Link EAP225 V3 or Ubiquiti UniFi AP AC.
Kitchen display: Logic Control LS8900 with KB9000 bump bar.

entries.title: HotSauce needs a Gigabit network switch
steps: Use a Gigabit switch (up to 1000 Mbps).
So-called Fast switches max out at 100 Mbps and are too slow.

entries.title: Terminal will not power on or charge: check the power cables
steps: Make sure the charging cable is firmly plugged into the terminal.
Make sure the other end is firmly plugged into an outlet or surge protector.
Check that the outlet or surge protector has power; if the outlet is dead, check the circuit breaker.
Plug the terminal into an outlet you know works.
Swap the charging cable for one you know works.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Terminal still will not charge: test it apart from the card reader
steps: Unplug the card reader from the terminal and, if it has a case, take the reader out of its case.
Charge the terminal and the card reader separately, each on its own cable, for about 20 minutes.
Reconnect the two charged devices.
If the reader is an iDynamo6, turn the terminal off and on again after reconnecting.
If the terminal will not charge on its own, its charging port may need to be looked at in an Apple store.
If it still does not charge, stop and contact Support.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Where to get a replacement charging cable
steps: Order parts directly at parts.getunion.com, or follow Union's Order Replacement Hardware process.

entries.title: Card reader not working: check the indicator light first
steps: Look at the indicator light on the card reader.
If it is green (solid or blinking), carry on with the re-pairing steps for your reader model.
If it is any other colour, or the light is out, stop and contact Support.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Re-pair an eDynamo card reader (Bluetooth)
steps: On the POS terminal, close the Union POS app and open iPad Settings.
Select Bluetooth and write down the reader's serial number as shown there (eDynamo-######).
Scroll down the left menu and select Union.
Check that Card Reader Model (iPad only) is set to eDynamo.
Check that the switch next to Enable Card Reader Pairing (eDynamo) is on and green.
Hold the small button on the left side of the eDynamo until the light flashes blue.
Close Settings and reopen the Union POS app; a popup appears.
Pick the reader by the serial number you wrote down.
When asked, swipe a test card to finish pairing. A 'Pairing was successful' message should show.
If pairing does not succeed, stop and contact Support.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Reset the connection to an iDynamo card reader
steps: Close the Union POS app on the terminal.
Open iPad Settings, scroll down the left menu and select Union.
Check that Card Reader Model is set to iDynamo.
Select General, scroll down and select Shut Down.
With the iPad off, unplug its power source from the back of the iPad or from the outlet.
Wait for the iPad to shut down completely.
Plug the power back in; the iPad should turn on by itself.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Cash drawer will not open: fix the receipt printer first
steps: The cash drawer is connected to the terminal through the receipt printer.
If the receipt printer is not working either, fix the printer first; that usually fixes the drawer.
Check that the cash drawer cable is firmly plugged into its port on the receipt printer.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: Cash drawer will not open: check whether it is locked
steps: Find the key that came with the drawer.
Put the key in and turn it counterclockwise to open the drawer.
If the key turns but the drawer does not open, the drawer is probably broken; order a new one from parts.getunion.com.
If the key is lost, a replacement can be bought at parts.getunion.com; if it is not listed there, contact Support.

entries.title: Cash drawer opens with the key but not from the POS
steps: Run a test print from the printer the drawer is connected to.
If the printer works and the drawer opens with the key, the cord between printer and drawer is faulty.
Order a replacement from parts.getunion.com.

entries.title: Order replacement Union hardware
steps: Order common hardware items online at parts.getunion.com; search by item name or picture.
Online orders take about 48 hours to process, depending on stock.
Orders can also be placed through the Support team; those take 3 to 7 business days, depending on stock.
For a new terminal, contact Support.

entries.title: Get an update on a Union hardware order
steps: Reply to the order confirmation email and ask for an update, or contact Support.

entries.title: A hardware item shows as Sold Out
steps: The online ordering page shows current stock, so Sold Out means Union is out of that item.
Contact Support to ask when it will be back in stock.
If an item already bought becomes backordered, Union will contact you with an availability date.

entries.title: Kitchen Display System (KDS) is not showing orders: remove other Wi-Fi networks
steps: Make sure at least one order for the KDS is open, or create a test order.
On the KDS terminal, close the KDS app and open iPad Settings.
Select WiFi, then Edit at the top right to see the saved networks.
If any non-Union networks are listed, select the red minus icon and Delete for each one.
Reopen the KDS app; orders should show again.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: KDS still not showing orders: check the POS terminals that send to it
steps: Close the KDS app on the KDS terminal.
On every POS terminal that prints to that KDS, close the Union POS app and open iPad Settings.
On each one, select WiFi, then Edit, and delete any non-Union networks.
When all terminals are checked, reopen the KDS app on the KDS terminal.
entries.note: Union's article is written for Union iPad terminals; confirm it matches the merchant's setup.

entries.title: KDS still not showing orders: check the terminal is set to send to that KDS
steps: On a POS terminal that prints to the KDS, go to the Log In screen and note the Register ID in the bottom-right corner.
On another device, sign in to the Manager Portal.
Select Settings, then Hardware Setup, then Registers.
Select the terminal with that Register ID.
Check that the right KDS is selected in the KDS dropdown.
If it is already correct, stop and contact Support.
If it is wrong or empty, add the KDS, create a test order and check it appears on the KDS.
If the test order does not appear, stop and contact Support.

entries.title: Terminal seems offline: check it is not set to Offline Mode
steps: Log in to the Union POS app with Manager or Admin credentials.
Select the menu (three lines) at the upper left.
Select Turn Online/Offline Mode.
If Set to Online Mode is switched off, the terminal is in Offline Mode; switch it on to connect.

entries.title: Network trouble: power cycle the printers and read their test prints
steps: Unplug all printers from their power outlets.
Plug them back in.
Wait up to 5 minutes for each printer to print its test print.
Check that the IP addresses printed all begin with the same two numbers.
