steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Button Configurations, select the configuration and click the layouts button.
Open the layout, right-click an empty square and choose Select Payment Method.
Pick the payment method, click Add, and Save.

entries.title: Open a card tab (take a pre-authorization)
steps: Ring the items and go to the payment screen.
Press the Credit Pre-Auth button, enter the amount and press Enter.
The card is run on the card terminal.
Two tip slips print along with the itemized receipt.
entries.note: Not all processors and card terminals support pre-auth/post-auth; Korona calls Tip Adjustment the newer method.

entries.title: Close a pre-auth receipt and add the tip
steps: Open the receipt archive; Show Open Pre-Authorizations filters to receipts waiting to be closed.
Select the receipt and press Re-Open Receipt.
Enter the tip amount and press Apply Payment Tip; enter 0 if there is no tip.
Press Enter to finalize; the card is charged the final amount.

entries.title: Pre-auth tabs must be closed before end of day
steps: A pre-auth receipt stays open until it is finalized at the register.
If it is still open when End of Day runs, it is not approved and the card is not charged.
Close every open pre-auth receipt before running end of day.

entries.title: Apply Payment Tip asks for a payment method first
steps: A tip can only be applied after a payment is on the receipt.
Run the Credit Pre-Auth first, then reopen the receipt to apply the tip.

entries.title: Pre-auth/post-auth is not supported by every processor
steps: Not all processors and card terminals support pre-auth and post-auth.
The newer method is Tip Adjustment.
Ask the processor which they support.

entries.title: Redeem a voucher
steps: For single- and multi-purpose vouchers press Redeem Voucher and enter or scan the voucher number.
Deposit vouchers are redeemed by scanning their barcode.
After scanning a deposit voucher, keep the deposit receipt, or it can be redeemed again.

entries.title: Cancel a voucher
steps: Vouchers do not show as items on a receipt.
Press the Cancel Voucher button, then enter or scan the voucher.

entries.title: Check a voucher's status
steps: Press the Show Voucher button, then enter or scan the voucher.

entries.title: Vouchers are an add-on package
steps: Vouchers must be added to the KORONA Studio account as a package; contact support to add it.

entries.title: Set up the customer-facing display
steps: On Windows the display must show up as a secondary monitor in Windows settings.
In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Customer Displays, create one, and for Display usually choose 'On Display 2'.
Choose what shows on the Welcome, Booking and Closed screens and Save.
In Sales > Points of Sale edit the POS and pick the display under Customer Display.
Restart the POS.

entries.title: Customer display changes are not showing
steps: For a newly assigned display, restart the POS.
If the display already existed and only settings changed, run Retrieve Master Data.

entries.title: Stop cash drops and deposits showing on the customer display
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Accounts.
Untick 'Show transaction on customer display' for that account.

entries.title: Fit a customer display to a Partner Tech A5 II register
steps: Power off the POS and remove the power cable and all other cables first.
You need a flathead and a Phillips screwdriver and a flat surface; lay a towel under the screen.
Follow Korona's installation video.
Then set the display up in KORONA Studio.

entries.title: Support hours printed on Korona hardware setup guides
steps: The Aures Sango and SP-5514 setup guides give Mon-Fri 9:00AM to 6:00PM Pacific on +1 (702)-997-7672.
entries.note: Disagrees with Korona's Contact Us page, which says general support is Monday to Friday 6 AM to 6 PM PT with 24/7 emergency support.

entries.title: Log in to the handheld inventory app (Korona.mde)
steps: Install 'Korona.mde' from the Google Play Store; uninstall any old version first.
The first time, log in with your KORONA Studio credentials.
After that, employees log in with their cashier login code and choose the store location.

entries.title: Count inventory with the handheld app
steps: Retrieve master data in the app before starting.
Open Inventories and tap + to create a count, or open an existing one.
Tap the magnifying glass to find a product, or scan it.
Key the quantity and press plus to add, or equals to set the count; scanning again adds 1 each time.
When done, swipe left on the inventory in the list and press upload.

entries.title: Handheld app: retrieve master data before, upload after
steps: Always retrieve master data before working on an inventory count.
Press Upload when finished.

entries.title: Handheld app: refresh stock values
steps: Swipe down from the top of the screen.

entries.title: Receive stock with the handheld app
steps: Open Stock Receipts and press +; start from a stock order, a dispatch notification, or an empty receipt.
Search for or scan the items; plus adds, equals sets the amount, scanning again adds 1.
Swipe left on the stock receipt to upload it.
Stock receipts must then be booked from the back office.

entries.title: Handheld app does not show prices in Product Information
steps: Tap the menu icon at the top left, then Settings.
Scroll to the Product Information tab and enable retail and/or purchase prices.

entries.title: A product rings up at the wrong price
steps: In KORONA Studio open the product and check the Prices section; each column is a Price Group.
Check which Price Group is set for the Customer Group and the Organizational Unit (Settings > Customer Groups / Organizational Units).
Check whether a customer or a button at the POS is applying a different Customer Group.
Check Store Prices (button at the top of the product); a store price overrides any price group price.
After correcting, retrieve master data at the register.
entries.note: The retrieve-master-data step comes from Korona's general rule for back-office changes.

entries.title: Price changed when a customer was added to the sale
steps: A Customer Group with a different Price Group overrides the product's current price.
Setting a customer by number does not automatically apply their Customer Group.

entries.title: Inventory count is wrong
steps: Check whether inventory tracking was ever disabled; that resets the count.
Check sales are syncing; a register not connected to the internet syncs late and throws counts off.
Check all stock receipts and inventory counts are booked.
Check the register is assigned to the right warehouse (Sales tab, point of sale screen).
Look at Evaluations > Stock History Report for the product.

entries.title: Sales reach the back office late when the register is offline
steps: Sales sync late if the POS is not connected to the internet.
Doing an inventory count while the POS has not synced throws the count off.

entries.title: Promotion is not triggering on a product
steps: In KORONA Studio open the product under Inventory > Products and make sure Is Discountable is ticked and saved.
At the register go to the Total screen; discounts only apply there.
Check the promotion's tag, date and customer group.

entries.title: Find the card's last 4 digits and approval for a past sale
steps: Open the Receipt Archive at the POS, type the receipt number and press Enter.
At the bottom, 'Account: xxxx' is the last 4 of the card and 'Approval' is the transaction token.
Without the receipt number: in KORONA Studio go to Sales > Receipts, filter by Payment Method = Credit, date and gross total.

entries.title: Chargebacks and signatures
steps: Korona notes the major card brands no longer require a signature for purchases, so one is not typically needed to dispute a chargeback.

entries.title: Sell an item that is not in the catalog (open product)
steps: In KORONA Studio create a product with name, commodity group, assortment and sector, leaving prices blank.
Set it to Price changeable and save.
Click To Button, choose Quick Keys and place the button.
Run Retrieve Master Data at the register.

entries.title: Discount Reasons report: what (PR), (P) and (RD) mean
steps: (PR): a price rule caused the discount.
(P): a promotion caused it.
(RD): a receipt discount triggered manually at the POS.

entries.title: Emailed (digital) receipts are not arriving
steps: In KORONA Studio click your username at the top left and open My Company Data.
Make sure Email Alias is not blank.

entries.title: Turn on digital receipts
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > POS Profile, and in the Receipt field choose Digital Receipt and save.
Retrieve master data and restart the point of sale.
The customer display then shows a QR code; the customer scans it and enters their email.

entries.title: Email a receipt by typing the customer's address
steps: Type the email address with the on-screen keyboard.
Press Enter (if set up with number ranges) or the 'Set email for digital receipt dispatch' button.
A popup confirms a digital receipt will be sent.

entries.title: Add a cashier or change a login code
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Employees > Cashiers.
Click +New, or select a cashier and press Edit.
Fill in a unique cashier number, first and last name, a Login Code and a Cashier Role.
Press Save.

entries.title: Stop a cashier's full name printing on receipts
steps: In KORONA Studio fill in the cashier's alias field; the receipt shows the alias instead of the full name.

entries.title: Block a cashier who has left
steps: Deleting a cashier cannot be reversed.
If work times are still needed for payroll, change the login code or use the Lock option instead of deleting.

entries.title: "You are not authorized to perform this action."
steps: The cashier's role lacks the permission for that action.
Have someone with the permission do it, or change the role in KORONA Studio under Employees > Cashier Roles.
Move the permission from the left box to the right and save.

entries.title: Korona cashier permissions: what each allows
steps: Cancel Items: remove line items.
Cancel Receipt: cancel an unfinished receipt.
Return: process returns, void receipts, and ring negative quantities.
Void Receipt: void finalized receipts.
Price: override item prices even when the product does not allow it.
Open Cash Drawer: use the Open Cash Drawer button.
Reports: pull POS reports.
Foreign Receipt: open receipts assigned to other cashiers.
Blank Receipt: finalize a receipt with no items.

entries.title: Cashier cannot remove the last item from a receipt
steps: Without the Cancel Last Receipt Item permission a cashier cannot remove the last item.
Use Cancel Receipt, or have the role changed in KORONA Studio.
entries.note: The Cancel Receipt suggestion needs the Cancel Receipt permission.

entries.title: Void Item button
steps: Voids a single item from the receipt.

entries.title: Immediate Cancellation button
steps: Removes the most recent item added to the receipt, but nothing before it.

entries.title: Cash Void button: undo a cash payment before the receipt is finished
steps: Cancels a cash payment taken at the POS before the receipt is finalized.
It only works from the payment layout.

entries.title: Return Item button: return one item inside a normal sale
steps: Marks a product on a normal transaction as a return of goods and asks for a return reason.
Useful for exchanges, since the whole receipt is not turned into a return.

entries.title: Return page button
steps: Search for a receipt number and refund individual items on it without going to the receipt archive.

entries.title: Receipt Reversal button
steps: Reverses a receipt as if the transaction did not happen; similar to Void Receipt.

entries.title: Receipt Print button reprints the second most recent receipt
steps: Receipt Print reprints the 2nd most recent (not the last) receipt in the print queue.
To reprint a specific receipt, use Print from the receipt archive.
entries.note: The second step is from Korona's Print function page.

entries.title: Print reports at the register
steps: Print POS Report prints the activity of one POS for the day.
Print Cashier Report prints one cashier's sales for the period.
Print POS Week Report and Print POS Month Report print the previous week or month.

entries.title: Print POS Week Report for the current week
steps: The week report prints the previous week.
For the current week, enter a negative number to reflect days.

entries.title: Cash Check
steps: Checks whether the money in the drawer matches what the POS expects.
It only works on the balance screen.

entries.title: Change Item Price button
steps: Adjusts the dollar amount on a product.

entries.title: Add Discount and Item Discount buttons
steps: Add Discount adds a % discount to the highlighted product, on top of any existing discounts.
Item Discount applies a % discount to the highlighted item(s).

entries.title: Target Price Discount button
steps: Applies the price you want to a product and shows the discount as a percentage.

entries.title: Tax-free sale (for example EBT): Apply Alternative Sector
steps: Apply Alternative Sector changes the selected products to their alternative tax sector, for example for a tax-free EBT sale.
Apply Default Sector changes them back.

entries.title: Toggle Sector button must be pressed after all items are added
steps: Toggle Sector switches between tax sectors.
Press it after all items have been added.

entries.title: Clear a wrong entry
steps: Clear Input Line clears anything keyed by mistake before a function is chosen.
Backspace removes the last entry.

entries.title: Show or hide the on-screen keyboard
steps: The Keyboard function turns the virtual keyboard on or off.

entries.title: Price check
steps: Price Info looks up a product's price by product number and lets you select the product.

entries.title: Check stock of a product from the register
steps: List Stocks shows a product's stock across warehouses, quantities on order and the last stock order.

entries.title: Find a customer at the register
steps: Customer Lookup searches customers by name, number or address.

entries.title: Remove all coupons from a receipt
steps: Removes every coupon applied to the current receipt without cancelling the receipt.

entries.title: Receipt cannot be finalized: receipt finalization lock
steps: A receipt lock stops a receipt being finalized, for example until someone with more authority reviews it.
Remove Receipt Finalization Lock removes the lock from the current receipt.

entries.title: Restart POS and Exit Application buttons
steps: Restart POS restarts the point of sale terminal.
Exit Application closes the KORONA client immediately.

entries.title: Revision: a manager steps in without losing the sale
steps: Revision switches login quickly without deleting the current ticket, so a manager can use a function the cashier is not allowed to.

entries.title: Stop one item printing to the kitchen or ticket printer
steps: Select the item and press Deactivate Print by Production Type; that product will not trigger its print.

entries.title: Send the kitchen print or activate a gift card manually
steps: Trigger Production manually triggers production types such as gift card activation, kitchen print or ticket activation.

entries.title: Clock in and out
steps: The Time Tracking function lets employees clock in and out, and for lunch breaks.

entries.title: Tip as a percentage of the receipt
steps: Set % of Receipt Total adds a tip based on a percentage of the receipt total; several buttons can be set with different percentages.

entries.title: Credit Card Terminal: Configuration (DataCap terminals)
steps: Updates DataCap card terminals.
Required if the processor's settings or file build are changed.

entries.title: EBT balance check (DataCap terminals)
steps: Credit Card Terminal: EBT Balance Cash/Foodstamp shows EBT balances on DataCap card terminals.

entries.title: ZVT card terminal functions do not apply in the US
steps: Diagnosis, Initializing, Maintenance and Repeat receipt apply only to ZVT card terminals used in the EU.

entries.title: Serial (RS-232) barcode scanner
steps: Activate Barcode Scanner enables RS-232 communication for serial-connected scanners.

entries.title: Handheld Manager
steps: Lists devices connected to KORONA, lets you accept or remove a device, and release receipts from a device.

entries.title: Payment button: pay in the default method without the total screen
steps: Enter the amount paid in the input field and press Payment.
Change is displayed as normal.

entries.title: Round Receipt Total Down
steps: Rounds the receipt total down by the amount entered; repeat to reverse.
Works only on the payment layout.

entries.title: Cancelled transactions are not in the receipt archive
steps: Show Receipt Archive lists the most recent receipts but not cancelled transactions.

entries.title: A button asks for a manager's or second cashier's login code
steps: Buttons can be restricted by role or set to need approval.
The action is blocked until a higher-level employee (or, in the alternative setup, a second user) enters their login code.
It is set in KORONA Studio under Settings > Button Configurations, on the button itself.

entries.title: Park a sale under a name or order number and recall it later
steps: Ring the items.
Press Set Order Number and enter a number or name.
Press Park Receipt; this receipt will not pop back up by itself.
To recall it press Open Receipt via Order Number and select it from the list or enter the order number.

entries.title: A blank receipt opened when recalling an order number
steps: If the order number entered does not exist, the POS creates a new receipt with that number.
Check the number, or pick the receipt from the list instead.

entries.title: Move items from one parked receipt to another
steps: Both receipts need an order number and must be parked.
Open the receipt you are moving items from with Open Receipt via Order Number.
Enter the order number of the receipt to move to in the panel at the bottom left.
Select the items to move.
Press Transfer Items.

entries.title: Take a payment toward a store (house) account
steps: Add the account to the receipt.
Type the amount with a minus sign in front.
Process the transaction normally.

entries.title: Charge a sale to a store account
steps: Ring the items.
Attach the customer's withdrawal account to the receipt.
Press Total and then the credit account button.
entries.note: Requires the account and its button to be set up in the back office first.

entries.title: Boca ticket printer: wait before loading tickets
steps: After powering on, wait at least 5 seconds before loading ticket stock.
The cutter moves rapidly at start-up and can jam tickets loaded too early.

entries.title: Boca prints in the wrong place or feeds blank tickets
steps: The sensors usually need cleaning; follow Boca's cleaning guidelines.

entries.title: Boca is skipping tickets
steps: Turn the Boca off.
Hold the test button and turn it on, keeping the button held for at least 5 seconds.

entries.title: Boca tickets print with blank spaces
steps: The thermal printhead usually needs cleaning.

entries.title: Boca tickets are not cut properly or cut in erratic places
steps: Check the cutter is not blocked and moves freely.
Check the ticket stock is not defective, for example unevenly spaced or faint black marks.

entries.title: Boca ticket printer care
steps: Clean it whenever dust is visible, and check each time ticket stock is changed.
Clean the platen at least once a year.
Do not store tickets in the printer out of season, especially adhesive stock.
Keep it on the connection configuration KORONA Support set up.

entries.title: Cancel and refund an event ticket order
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Sales > Orders, filter, and search the order number including the 'OR'.
Press Cancel at the bottom right and confirm with Cancel Order; the customer is emailed and the tickets become invalid.
Press Initiate Payment to refund.
Depending on the payment service the refund is immediate or needs a further step with the payment provider.

entries.title: Change an item's price at the register
steps: Add the product to the receipt.
Key the new price on the number pad.
Press Change Item Price.
It works if the product is Price Changeable or the cashier has the Price permission.

entries.title: Register asks for a price when an item is rung
steps: The item is an open product: it has no price in the back office and is price changeable.
Enter the price and press Enter.

entries.title: Receipt logo prints as a black box
steps: The image size or format is usually wrong.
Use the .png format, or change the image's size or dimensions, and upload it again.
Restart the POS.

entries.title: Add a logo to the receipt
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Receipt Layout.
Click the box with the camera for the Header or Footer logo.
Click the plus button to upload the image.
Cancel the current receipt for the new logo to apply; if the logo got bigger, restart the POS.

entries.title: Clock in or out at the register
steps: Press the Time Tracking button; a new screen opens.
Enter the cashier number (it can be different from the login code).
Press the action, for example Start Shift or End Shift.

entries.title: Fix a missed or wrong clock-in
steps: In KORONA Studio open the cashier's edit screen.
Under More > Time Tracking Entries, review, correct or create entries.

entries.title: Time tracking is only in the Retail package
steps: Time Tracking is only available in Korona's Retail Package.

entries.title: How price-embedded (deli/scale) barcodes are read
steps: The barcode is split as: leading digit, item number, price, check digit.
Example 2123450015955: 2, item 12345, price 001595 ($15.95), check digit 5.
Korona recognises in-store codes with 4, 5 or 6 digit prices, and 5-digit weight codes.

entries.title: Set up price-embedded barcodes
steps: In KORONA Studio go to Settings > Number Ranges, click Add Number Range and choose 'Add Sale' as the function.
Choose one Expression Type (4, 5 or 6 digit price, or 5-digit weight); only one can be active at a time.
On each product enter the matching product code and mark it Price Changeable.
Retrieve Master Data at the register and restart the software (restart is only needed after adding the number range).

entries.title: Scale or deli labels will not scan
steps: The check digit at the end of the code is needed when scanning these items.
Make sure the barcode scanner's check digit setting is enabled.

entries.title: Lottery sales and payouts are accounts, not products
steps: A lottery purchase is recorded as a deposit; a payout as a withdrawal.
Press the Lottery Purchase or Lottery Payout button and enter the dollar amount.
These do not count in revenue totals.
Do not create products for lottery.

entries.title: Trigger Production only prints each item once
steps: Trigger Production runs all allowed production types for items not yet produced.
Pressing it again on the same receipt does not reprint items already produced.
Some production types need payment first and cannot be triggered manually.

entries.title: Refund a bottle deposit
steps: Ring up the main product and press Extract Deposit Items; the deposit becomes its own line, and the main product can then be removed.
Or activate deposit refund mode and ring the product; a negative deposit line appears for the returned bottle.
The current mode is shown only next to the cashier's name.

entries.title: Reprint a transaction receipt on the Android terminals (VL550 / VP550C / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Press the Menu button.
Choose Reprint Receipt.

entries.title: Key in a card by hand on the Android terminals (VL550 / VP550C / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Start the sale as usual.
At the Present Card screen, select the Manual Entry button to continue.

entries.title: Where Reset Terminal (soft reset) is on the Android terminals
steps: Press the Menu button.
Choose Settings.
Choose Utilities.
Choose Reset Terminal.
entries.note: The FAQ gives only the menu path. Valor's soft reset article for the Linux models says a reset clears the terminal's database and needs the master password.

entries.title: Battery behaves inconsistently (VL110 / VL550 / VP550E)
steps: Let the battery run down to 0% until the terminal powers itself off.
Let it charge overnight.
Use the charging cable and wall adapter that came with the terminal.
entries.note: The current knowledge base lists VL110 / VL500 / VL550 / VP550E for this answer.

entries.title: Receipt prints very light (VL110 / VL550 / VP550E)
steps: Make sure the receipt tray is clean and closed properly.
On a VL110, make sure the terminal is not in Power Save mode.
Make sure the battery is at 45% or more.

entries.title: Connection types supported: VL550 / VP550E / VP800
steps: These terminals connect by cellular or Wi-Fi.

entries.title: Make the terminal use its SIM (cellular) connection: VL550 / VP550E / VP800
steps: Press the Menu button.
Choose Settings.
Choose WIFI Config.
Toggle Wi-Fi off.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: dual pricing and BIN-based surcharge are supported
steps: Dual Pricing is available in the Virtual Terminal.
It detects whether the card is debit or credit (BIN detection).
entries.note: Differs from the older Freshdesk copy of the FAQ, which said dual pricing was not available in the Virtual Terminal. This is Valor's current knowledge base.

entries.title: Update a VL300, VP300 or VP300 Pro PIN pad to the latest app version
steps: Make sure the PIN pad is connected properly to its terminal.
Run a Package Download so the latest software is installed.
If nothing updates, App Download has to be switched on for the terminal in the Online Portal first.
entries.note: Valor says the ISO must toggle App Download to Enabled in the Online Portal for this to work.

entries.title: Invalid Parameter
steps: Close the terminal's batch from the Online Portal.
Try the download again.

entries.title: View a previous batch on a VL500-series terminal
steps: Press the Menu button.
Choose Report.
Choose Closed Batch or Detailed Report.
entries.note: The knowledge base names the VL500 for this path.

entries.title: Parameter Disabled (when reloading the EPI after a reset)
steps: This message appears when the terminal tries to reload its EPI and ParamDownload is not enabled for that EPI in the Online Portal.
ParamDownload has to be enabled on the Online Portal for that EPI, then the reload can be tried again.

entries.title: VP800: connect a cash drawer
steps: Check that the cash drawer is compatible with the terminal.
You need the cash drawer, the terminal and the Multi-Comm Hub.
Connect the cash drawer with an RJ11/RJ12 cable to the Cash Drawer port on the Multi-Comm Hub.
Dock the VP800 on the Multi-Comm Hub.

entries.title: VP800: turn on the cash drawer in the terminal settings
steps: On the terminal go to Settings, then Utility, then Cash Draw.
Enable the cash drawer.
Set the payment type and transaction status that should open it.

entries.title: VP800: open the cash drawer by hand
steps: Go to the terminal's settings.
Select the CASH DRAW OPEN option.

entries.title: Portal setting: Server/Clerk Setup (also turns on tip adjust)
steps: Server/Clerk Setup makes the terminal ask for a clerk or server ID during transactions.
Turning it on also activates tip adjustment.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Clerk Mandate (clerk ID asked on every sale)
steps: When Server/Clerk Setup is on, Clerk Mandate makes the clerk or server ID required on every transaction.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: tip suggestions on screen and on the receipt
steps: Smart Tip prints four suggested tip options on the receipt.
Tip On Screen shows the Smart Tip suggestions on the terminal for the customer to choose.
Tip On Receipt prints a tip line so the customer can write in a tip.
Show "No Tip" Option adds a No Tip button.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Max Tip
steps: Max Tip sets the largest tip, as a percentage or dollar amount, that the terminal will accept.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Fixed Tip (a tip is added to every sale)
steps: Fixed Tip automatically applies a preset tip percentage or dollar amount to all transactions.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Receipt for Tip Adjust
steps: When this is on, the terminal prints a new receipt each time a tip is adjusted.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Receipt for Declined Transactions
steps: When this is on, the terminal prints a receipt for declined or failed transactions.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: "No Transactions to Settle" slip at settlement
steps: The No Transaction Report setting makes the terminal print a slip saying "No Transactions to Settle" when the batch is empty.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Email Report (batch report by email)
steps: Email Report sends the batch settlement report to the primary merchant account email on file.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: which report prints at settlement
steps: Detailed Report prints a detailed list of transactions at batch settlement.
Summary Report prints a summarized version.
Settlement Report Tip adds tip information to the settlement report.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Hide Receipt Option
steps: Hide Receipt Option turns off SMS receipts and the SMS collection screens.
It overrides the SMS Receipt and Paper Receipt settings.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: SMS Receipt (merchant copy must be reprinted)
steps: SMS Receipt sends the receipt by text message.
If a merchant copy is needed it has to be reprinted.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: signature line and merchant receipt copy (not on RCKT, VP550E or Virtual Terminal)
steps: Force On Screen Signature asks for a signature on the screen for signature debit or credit sales.
Forced Signature prints a signature line on paper receipts.
Forced Signature and Merchant Receipt Option are not supported on the RCKT, VP550E or Virtual Terminal.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Sleep Mode / Timer
steps: Sleep Mode / Timer sets how long the terminal sits idle before it goes into power-save mode.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Terminal shuts down by itself at a set time (Auto Shutdown setting)
steps: Auto Shutdown is a portal setting that schedules the terminal to shut down at a set time.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Batch Out (manual or automatic)
steps: Batch Out chooses manual or automatic batch settlement.
In automatic mode a specific time can be set.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: VP800: what the customer-facing screen shows
steps: A portal setting chooses whether the customer-facing display shows the current time or an image.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Split Payment
steps: Split Payment lets one transaction be split into up to five payment methods.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Cash Back on Debit
steps: Cash Back on Debit lets customers get cash back on PIN-verified debit transactions.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Change Management on Cash Transactions
steps: With this on, the merchant enters the cash received and the terminal works out the change.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Disable All Passwords
steps: Disable All Passwords turns off the terminal-level passwords.
The master password is still needed for resets and key actions.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: password prompts for refund, EBT, void and pre-auth
steps: Password for Refund adds a password requirement for refunds.
Prompt Password For: EBT, VOID, PreAUTH makes the terminal ask for a password on those transaction types.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: No signature or receipt on small sales (QSR setting)
steps: QSR (Quick Serve Restaurant) skips the signature and receipt printing below a set dollar amount.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: manual card entry on credit and debit
steps: Manual Entry on Credit allows credit card numbers to be keyed in.
Manual Entry on Debit allows debit card numbers to be keyed in and needs credit manual entry enabled.
Bypass CVV Entry skips the CVV on manual entries and also needs credit manual entry enabled.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Present Card Prompt
steps: Present Card Prompt asks whether the card is present when card details are keyed in by hand.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Gift Card Partial Approval
steps: Gift Card Partial Approval allows a split payment when the gift card balance does not cover the sale.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: AVS (address or ZIP asked during a sale)
steps: AVS makes the terminal require the address, the ZIP, or both for verification during transactions.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: tax on sales
steps: State Tax applies a set tax percentage to transactions.
Include Tax for Cash charges tax on cash transactions as well.
Show Remove Tax gives an option to remove tax at the amount confirmation screen; it needs the differential removal options enabled too.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal setting: Access Valor Store (Android only)
steps: Access Valor Store gives the terminal access to the Valor Store marketplace.
It is for Android devices only and has a limited set of apps.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Portal settings: receipt header and footer lines
steps: Line 1 shows the store name.
Lines 2 to 4 default to the store's primary address, secondary address and phone number and can be customized.
Line 5 is empty by default.
A footer message prints beneath the disclaimer; more footer lines can be added with +Add.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Which transaction types a Valor terminal can show (POS Menu Configuration)
steps: Default / Credit covers Sale, Void, Pre-Auth, Ticket, Refund, Pre-Sale and Post-Auth.
Default / Debit covers Sale, Pre-Auth and Ticket.
EBT Food covers Sale, Refund, Balance Inquiry and Withdrawal.
EBT Cash covers Balance Inquiry and Withdrawal.
Cash covers Sale and Refund.
Gift Card covers Balance Inquiry, Add Value, Activate, Sale and Refund.
entries.note: A setting in the Online Portal under Device Management > Edit Parameters.

entries.title: Deferred Auth (offline transactions): turn it on for a terminal in the portal
steps: Log in to the Online Portal.
Go to Device Management.
Find the EPI, select the vertical ellipsis, then Edit Parameters.
Select the Terminal & Transaction tab, then the Transaction sub-tab.
Toggle Offline Transactions to Enabled.
Set the offline transaction limits and settings.
Select SAVE.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: switch the terminal to offline mode (VL100 / VL100 Pro / VL110 / VP100 / VL300 standalone)
steps: Select the Menu button at the bottom-middle of the screen.
Select Utility, then Deferred AUTH.
Select Enable Offline Mode and accept the terms by pressing YES.
An Offline icon at the top of the screen shows the terminal is in offline mode.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: print the offline transaction report (VL100 / VL100 Pro / VL110 / VP100 / VL300 standalone)
steps: Select the Menu button.
Select Utility, then Deferred AUTH.
Select Offline Reports.
Select Open Summary or Detailed Report to print.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: upload offline transactions (VL100 / VL100 Pro / VL110 / VP100 / VL300 standalone)
steps: Select the Menu button.
Select Utility, then Deferred AUTH.
Select Upload Offline Txn to capture the transactions.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: review pending offline transactions (VL100 / VL100 Pro / VL110 / VP100 / VL300 standalone)
steps: Select the Menu button.
Select Utility, then Deferred AUTH.
Select View Transaction.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: switch the terminal to offline mode (VL550 / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Select the Menu button at the bottom-left of the screen.
Select Settings, then Offline Transaction.
Select Offline Disabled and accept the terms by pressing YES.
"Offline" at the top-left of the screen shows the terminal is in offline mode.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: upload offline transactions (VL550 / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Select the Menu button at the bottom-left of the screen.
Select Settings, then Offline Transaction.
Select Upload Transaction to capture the transactions.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: review pending offline transactions (VL550 / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Select the Menu button at the bottom-left of the screen.
Select Settings, then Offline Transaction.
Select View Transaction.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: print the offline transaction report (VL550 / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Select the Menu button at the bottom-left of the screen.
Select Settings, then Offline Transaction.
Select Report.
Select Detailed Report or Summary to print.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: leave offline mode (VL550 / VP550E / VP800)
steps: Select the Menu button at the bottom-left of the screen.
Select Settings, then Offline Transaction.
Select Offline Enabled and confirm with YES.
Any transactions not yet uploaded will now upload and be captured.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: taking cards when the network is unstable
steps: Deferred authorization lets the terminal process transactions locally when the network is unstable.
The "Enable Offline transactions" flag has to be enabled in the Valor Portal first.
It can be used for sale and refund transactions.
Once a stable connection is back, the transactions are uploaded.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: limits on offline transactions
steps: The maximum amount for a single offline transaction is 500 dollars.
The maximum total before a batch out is 5000 dollars.
The maximum number of offline transactions per day is 60.
The maximum number of offline transactions for a single card is 5.
The merchant sets the actual limits in the Valor Portal within these maximums.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: when offline transactions are uploaded
steps: The portal's "Transaction upload mode" has two options: Upload before batch out, and manual upload.

entries.title: Deferred Auth on the Linux terminals: turn on offline mode from the offline icon
steps: After the terminal has been updated with the new parameters, a small offline icon appears in the top-right corner of the screen.
Select the icon to reach "Enable Offline Mode".
Select Yes to agree to the terms and conditions.
Another way: go to the main menu settings, select Utility, enter the EPI password, choose Deferred Auth, then Enable Offline Mode and Yes.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: upload and settle offline transactions (manual upload mode)
steps: Connect the terminal to a stable internet connection.
Select the offline icon or button to open the offline menu.
Select "Upload Offline Transaction" to upload all offline transactions.
Go to the main menu and select Settlement.
Enter the password or passcode for the EPI to batch out the uploaded transactions.

entries.title: Deferred Auth: settle offline transactions (Upload Before Batch Out mode)
steps: Go to the main menu and select Settlement.
A pop-up shows the EPI ID; enter its password or passcode.
Once confirmed, the offline transactions are credited to the merchant's account.

entries.title: VL550: run a fleet card (fuel) transaction
steps: Tap the Fuel icon on the terminal and choose the fuel type.
If needed, tap Service or Store and choose the service or product, or type the product code in the search bar.
Enter the transaction details and check the summary.
Complete the vehicle verification (odometer reading, Vehicle ID, driver number, user ID).
Process the payment.
entries.note: Valor's guide names the VL500 and VL550 for fleet cards. Fleet has to be enabled for the merchant in the portal.

entries.title: Fleet cards: manage fuel products in the Valor Portal
steps: Log in to the Valor Portal.
Go to Settings, then Fleet.
Organize products under Products, Product Types and Product Categories.
To change a product, select the vertical ellipses and Edit.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: run an ACH sale
steps: In the Virtual Terminal, select the ACH sale sub tag under the ACH tag.
Fill in the transaction details with a valid account and routing number.
Select Debit or Credit as the TXN Type.
Select PROCESS PAYMENT.
A pop-up shows the status of the transaction.
entries.note: ACH has to be configured on the Virtual Terminal device by the ISO first.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: set up a recurring ACH payment
steps: In the Virtual Terminal, select the ACH Recurring sub tag under the ACH tag.
Fill in the frequency and other details with a valid account and routing number.
Select PROCESS PAYMENT.
A pop-up shows the status of the recurring transaction.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: see the ACH threshold
steps: Go to Setting in the sidebar menu.
Go to the ACH Threshold tab.
entries.note: Per Valor's ACH guide the ISO sets the threshold; the merchant can view it.

entries.title: Portal: view or delete an ACH transaction
steps: ACH transactions have their own tabs in the transaction module.
From the vertical ellipses of a transaction the merchant can delete it or see an overview.

entries.title: ValorPay app: run a refund
steps: Select the Down Arrow box next to Sale on the home screen.
Select Refund.
Enter the amount, then Process Payment.
Enter the customer details, then Continue.
Enter the cardholder name, then Proceed.
Enter the customer signature and select Pay.
Enter the one-time passcode sent to the account's phone number and email address to confirm the refund.

entries.title: ValorPay app: run a Quick Sale
steps: Select the Down Arrow box next to Sale on the home screen.
Select Quick Sale.
Enter the amount, then Process Payment.
Enter the customer details, then Continue.
Enter the card details and cardholder name, then Proceed.
Enter a tip if any, take the customer signature and select Pay.

entries.title: ValorPay app: run an Auth
steps: Select the Down Arrow box next to Sale on the home screen.
Select Auth.
Enter the amount, then Process Payment.
Enter the customer details, then Continue.
Enter the card details and cardholder name, then Proceed.
Take the customer signature and select Pay.

entries.title: ValorPay app: record a cash sale
steps: Enter the sale amount, then Process Payment.
Select Cash as the method of payment.
Enter the customer details, then Continue.
Select Done, or Share Receipt to send the customer another copy.

entries.title: ValorPay app: take a gift card payment
steps: Enter the sale amount, then Process Payment.
Select Gift Card as the method of payment.
Enter the customer details, then Continue.
With a RCKT, swipe the gift card.
Without a RCKT, key in the card number, press Proceed, then enter the gift card PIN and Proceed.
Enter a tip if it applies and select Pay.

entries.title: ValorPay app: run a parameter download
steps: Select the horizontal ellipsis at the top-right of the New Sale screen.
Select Param Download.

entries.title: ValorPay app: review and close an open batch
steps: Open Open Batches to review the batches currently open on the merchant account.
To look at another device, select the Store at the top-left (multi-store accounts), then the EPI at the top-right, then Ok.
Select Close Batch at the top-right to close the open batch.

entries.title: ValorPay app: what you can do from the Transactions list
steps: Selecting the vertical ellipsis on a transaction lets you open a ticket about it, issue a refund, void it (within the same batch), or send the receipt by email or SMS.
Tapping a transaction shows its receipt.

entries.title: RCKT: pair from the ValorPay app (current knowledge base steps)
steps: Select the Phone icon at the top-right of the screen to check that the RCKT device EPI is set.
Select the RCKT EPI and confirm with Ok.
A pop-up lists the RCKT devices that are on nearby; select the serial number.
Confirm pairing in the app and press the green OK button on the RCKT.
The reader then loads the EPI and the RKI keys and prepares itself for use.

entries.title: RCKT: connect to an Android phone (06/2025 QRG)
steps: Power on the RCKT; it shows a Device Name.
Download the ValorPay app from the Google Play Store.
Log in with your username; a one-time password is sent to the mobile number on file.
Create a 6-digit passcode.
Select the switch icon at the top right of the app.
Select your store and the device EPI.
The app scans for nearby RCKT devices; select the right device name to pair.
Make sure Bluetooth and Location permissions are enabled.

entries.title: RCKT: connect to an iPhone (06/2025 QRG)
steps: Power on the RCKT; it shows a Device Name.
Download the ValorPay app from the App Store and allow notifications for it.
Log in with your username; a one-time password is sent to the mobile number on file.
Create a 6-digit passcode.
Select the switch icon at the top right of the app.
Select your store and the device EPI.
The app scans for nearby RCKT devices; select the right device name to pair.
Make sure Bluetooth and Location permissions are enabled.

entries.title: Valor Online Portal: first-time access
steps: After your sales representative creates the account you receive an activation email.
Open the link and create your password.
Then go to the Online Portal.

entries.title: Valor Online Portal: resend a user's verification email
steps: Go to User Management in the sidebar menu.
Select the vertical ellipsis next to the user.
Select Send Verification Email.
It is sent to the mobile number first, then by email.

entries.title: Valor Online Portal: make a user an Operator Admin
steps: Go to User Management in the sidebar menu.
Select the vertical ellipsis next to the user.
Select Assign as Operator Admin.

entries.title: Valor Online Portal: view a user's operator overview
steps: Go to User Management in the sidebar menu.
Select the hyperlinked email address of the user.

entries.title: Valor Online Portal: group transactions by day
steps: Go to Transactions in the sidebar menu.
Select the Group by Day icon next to the EXPORT button at the top-right.

entries.title: Valor Online Portal: see a device's RKI download log
steps: Go to Device Management in the sidebar menu.
Find the device EPI, select the vertical ellipsis, then RKI download log.

entries.title: Valor Vault: save a customer and card
steps: Go to Vault in the sidebar menu.
Select Add Customer.
Fill in the details; Customer ID is required.
Select Save.

entries.title: Valor Vault: save a customer from a past transaction
steps: Go to Transactions in the sidebar menu.
Select the vertical ellipsis next to the transaction.
Select Add to Vault.
Fill in any missing customer details and select Save.

entries.title: Valor Vault: edit a saved customer
steps: Go to Vault in the sidebar menu.
Select List Customer.
Select the highlighted customer name, or the vertical ellipsis and View/Edit Customer.
Make the changes and select Save.

entries.title: Valor Vault: delete a saved customer
steps: Go to Vault in the sidebar menu.
Select List Customer.
Select the vertical ellipsis to the right of the customer.
Select Delete Customer, then Yes.

entries.title: Valor Vault: import customers
steps: Go to Vault in the sidebar menu.
Select List Customer.
Select the Action button.
Select Import, locate the import file and select Yes.
Each import is limited to 1000 customers.

entries.title: Valor Vault: export customers
steps: Go to Vault in the sidebar menu.
Select List Customer.
Select the Action button.
Select Export and choose the file format.
Customer card details are not exported.

entries.title: Virtual Terminal: connect QuickBooks
steps: Go to Setting in the sidebar menu.
Go to the Quickbooks tab, then Authenticate.

entries.title: Transaction restricted (E98, V0, V0573)
steps: This means the transaction was restricted by a security rule, the Card Phishing RT Shield rule.
That rule is on for merchants that have no shield rules of their own.
Support needs to set up custom Valor Shield RT rules for the merchant, or turn the Card Phishing rule off if it is not needed.
After the rules are changed, run a parameter download on the device.

entries.title: Sales under $1 approve at first, then start declining
steps: Small transactions may not trigger the Card Phishing RT Shield rule at first.
As transactions continue the rule can activate and restrict further transactions.
The merchant's Valor Shield RT rules need to be changed by support.

entries.title: Merchant Profile Update Required. Kindly Contact ISO
steps: This appears when the merchant details on the device (such as MID, TID or MCC code) do not match what the processor has.
The device's merchant file build in the Valor Portal has to be corrected to match the VAR sheet from the processor; contact support for this.
Once updated, the change usually takes effect immediately, but processor verification can take a few hours.

entries.title: EPI Host Processor Info Not Found
steps: This appears when a transaction is run on a profile (Cash Discounting or traditional) of the merchant file build that has no processor information set up.
The processor information has to be entered in the matching profile in the Valor Portal; contact support.

entries.title: Run a software update on a Valor Android terminal (after a version is assigned)
steps: Press the Menu button (three lines).
Go to Updates.
Check the EPI and press ENTER to start the update.
entries.note: The new app version has to be assigned in the portal's Device Management first (done by the ISO/support). Valor's page says 'Android Terminal' without naming models.

entries.title: Run a software update on a Valor Linux terminal (after a version is assigned)
steps: Press the Favorites (star) button.
Go to Updates.
Check the EPI and press OK to start the update.
entries.note: The new app version has to be assigned in the portal's Device Management first (done by the ISO/support).

entries.title: Valor Connect listening screen: what the menu options do
steps: View Transactions shows past transactions.
Batch Out settles the current batch.
Reprint Receipt reprints earlier receipts.
Tip Adjust changes tip amounts.
Clear Reversal resolves pending or failed reversals.
Run Standalone Transaction takes a payment outside the POS system.
WiFi Config and Sim Config open the network settings.
Reboot Terminal restarts the terminal.
Run Download downloads configuration updates, software patches or parameter changes.

entries.title: Valor Connect listening screen on Linux terminals: only Run Standalone Transaction
steps: On the Linux-based terminals the only menu option the Valor Connect listening screen can show is Run Standalone Transaction.

entries.title: Valor Connect listening screen shows no menu options
steps: The "Show Menu Options" setting has to be enabled for the device.
It is under Device Parameters, Terminal & Transaction, Valor Connect: toggle Show Menu Options to Enabled.

entries.title: Remove the differential / custom fee from integrated transactions
steps: This is changed in the Valor Portal on the device (EPI): the "Cash Discount & Surcharge" profile is removed and saved.
Afterwards, power cycle the device (turn it off and on) so the change takes effect.

entries.title: How to read Valor response codes that start with V0
steps: In codes such as V00E9, "V0" is a standard prefix.
The remaining characters are the processor or switch response code, padded with leading zeros.

entries.title: Datawire failed: No ticket
steps: The processor declined because the MID and TID were changed after the device's first request created a Datawire ID.
This has to be corrected by support.

entries.title: Datawire failed: Provisioning ticket
steps: This means the same MID and TID already exist for another merchant, so the processor declines them.
This has to be corrected by support.
